Bayt Al-Muazzam (also: The Temple of Buried Dominion): Bayt Al-Muazzam is a cavern temple inside Mt. Damavand in the Desert of Hadramaveth of Sumeru. It lies beneath Qusayr Al-Inkhida' and leads into Deshret's Glass Goblet. The Traveler unlocks it in Dune-Entombed Fecundity: Part I.

The name is Arabic for House of the Glorified. The map viewpoint calls it the Temple of Buried Dominion. It has an upper and a lower level and is the first of three similar caverns found in the Dirge of Bilqis quests, the others being Bayt Al-Sukr and Bayt Al-Hayah.

Geography: In the middle of Mt. Damavand's maze of tunnels, under the ruins of Qusayr Al-Inkhida'. The Mt. Damavand map has two levels for this temple, upper and lower. Paths lead onward to the Goblet.

In Part I, the party enters the mountain through the entrance with the Tanit's help after Azariq relays Matriarch Babel's plan to use dried canals in the dunes to reach the underground foundations of the Eternal Oasis.

History: Liloupar, a Jinni who is the Traveler's companion in the quest, explains that the mortal kingdoms of the oasis drew their water from within this mountain, hollowing it and weaving a network of tubes through it. The first water-pumping mechanism the party finds now runs on sand instead of water.

Liloupar finds a fragment of herself here that the party collects, and she says green should flourish near a Jinni's fragments. Further on she names the mechanism built to sustain a dream of eternity for the oasis.

Atmosphere: Dry canyon-cavern air, shifting sand where water used to run, doors that open only when sand is drained. The sense is of enormous machinery asleep.

Dangers: Geo fungi wait outside the entrance. Further in, travellers meet Eremites' abandoned camp and various ancient mechanisms.

Quests: Dune-Entombed Fecundity: Part I, third part of The Dirge of Bilqis, with Jeht, Azariq, Babel and Liloupar.

The end of Part I shows the Goblet and the Eternal Oasis within sight. Jeht notes her father always hoped to enter the Eternal Oasis and find her mother again, and she never thought she would help make it come true.

Status as of 7.1: Open to explore as of Version 7.1.

The Eternal Oasis is reached later in the Dirge of Bilqis. No source up to Version 7.1 that I checked changes this temple.

45.content:
Bayt Al-Sukr (also: The Court of Dried Springs): Bayt Al-Sukr is a cavern temple inside Mt. Damavand in Sumeru's Desert of Hadramaveth, beneath the Sands of Three Canals, leading into Deshret's Glass Goblet. It is unlocked in Dune-Entombed Fecundity: Part II.

The name is Arabic for House of Drunkenness. The map viewpoint calls it the Court of Dried Springs. It lies on the upper level of the Mt. Damavand ruins.

Geography: Beneath the Sands of Three Canals, on the upper level of the Mt. Damavand map. It is one of the routes into the central cavern with Deshret's Glass Goblet.

Part II has the party reach the area by driving an ancient machine through the dunes with Azariq's help, then entering a cave through the machine's arm.

History: During Part II, Liloupar says the oasis honoured the Three Eternal Companion-Gods and that the tunnel was dug in the memory of the slumbering lady of the oasis. She says the Lord charged the mortals' ideal kingdom with guarding his oasis, which is why Gurabad stood on the dune's edge before sinking into the sand.

The party repairs pipes and a stone slate, opens an ancient gate and collects another fragment of Liloupar. Pipes that can be reconnected control the gate.

Atmosphere: Dry canals and pipes, sound of sand, ruined machinery. The viewpoint title evokes springs that no longer flow.

Quests: Dune-Entombed Fecundity: Part II, the fourth part of The Dirge of Bilqis.

Part II's last mechanisms lead deeper to the mountain's core. Part III follows with betrayal by Azariq and Aderfi; this temple is unlocked before that turn.

Status as of 7.1: Open to explore as of Version 7.1.

No source up to Version 7.1 that I checked changes this temple.

46.content:
Bimarstan: Bimarstan is the hospital of Sumeru City, run by the Akademiya, which gives free healthcare to every resident of Sumeru. It stands just southeast of the city's northwestern Teleport Waypoint. Interns and a doctor staff it, and its name is a variant of the old word for hospitals in the historic Islamic world.

When Eleazar cases rose in Sumeru City, a notice from the mahamatas urged residents with symptoms to go to Bimarstan for treatment. In the Traveler's voice-over, Paimon is amazed that medicine is free.

People: The doctor Zakariya and the intern doctors Golshan and Tamara work at Bimarstan. Patients and their families seen here include Javad (by day), Lila and Tahmina.

Places: A message board nearby, Bimarstan's Proverb Column, displays the sayings of past Akademiya researchers at random, with the stated aim of following the pioneers' trail to the light of wisdom. Behind the building is a medical file that disappears once read.

That file records the case of Giyath Khayyam, a 65-year-old male patient with a brain disease of unknown cause: his memory worsened over time and he was emotionally unstable, talking about childhood memories. He had applied to retire from Amurta, hoping a stable life would slow the decline, and Amurta announced that the sage Siman Farrokhzad would ensure his treatment.

Governance: Operated by the Akademiya as a public service for all Sumeru residents.

Atmosphere: A calm, clean clinic in the city, with the quiet of waiting families and the cautious optimism of a free-of-charge ward.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it remains the city's free hospital; the pages consulted record no later change.

Further details: Of the Proverb Column's quoted researchers, the wiki lists Albiruni, Alva Nikola, Ayesha, Cyrus, Fadhlan, Hipakretisa, Imhotep, Iskandar and Mahitab, with lines such as Cyrus' "Change is the only constant." The Chinese name of the hospital translates roughly as House of Health.

key: The Frontier Beneath the High Wall
47.content:
Caravan Ribat (also: The Frontier Beneath the High Wall): Caravan Ribat is a fortified village at the foot of the Wall of Samiel, the great wall that keeps desert sandstorms from the rainforests of Sumeru. It is the checkpoint between the forest and the desert, where travellers going to or from Aaru Village and the Great Red Sand must pass, and it is full of Eremites. Its official tagline calls it the frontier beneath the high wall.

Its name uses the Arabic ribat, a small frontier fortification that later served as a caravanserai defending trade routes. The Ribat sits in the Ashavan Realm of the Dharma Forest, so it feels like a border town that belongs to both worlds.

Geography: Caravan Ribat sits directly under the Wall of Samiel, the barrier between the Dharma Forest and the Great Red Sand. The road through it links the forest side (towards Gandharva Ville and Sumeru City) with the desert side (Aaru Village and the Great Red Sand).

The wall is described as an enormous barrier against searing sandstorms. Official text notes it also blocks the spread of "wisdom's blessing", asking whether divine wisdom is not meant to shine on all people.

Places: The Caravan Ribat Bulletin Board carries notices such as a recruitment drive for Wall of Samiel maintenance and a reminder that destroying the wall is prohibited. Gilded Journey is a business run by Maryam, with Maziar as an employee.

People: Eremite mercenaries (Aybak, Nasir, Safie, Thiyya) work here alongside merchants (Hawad, Yinjie), an adventurer (Baharak) and researchers (Behnam, Dunya, Juzjani, Ma'asudi, Railah) who monitor the wall. Arshia is also listed.

Behnam is one researcher who states that the Akademiya actively maintains the wall to stop the desert eroding the rainforest.

Governance: No local authority is named. The Akademiya looks after the wall itself; the village is described as the checkpoint between forest and desert.

Culture: Many people here are Eremites, and the village is a place where the desert and the Akademiya's world meet. Dehya says that as she grew up she realised the wall is not only there to keep out sandstorms but also to keep out desert people like her.

History: Collei tells the Traveler that Greater Lord Rukkhadevata created the rainforests and the Wall of Samiel around the desert, to protect the rainforests from sandstorms. Its upkeep has since passed to the Akademiya.

Samiel is another name for the simoom, a strong dry dust-laden wind of the Sahara and Arabian deserts.

In the Chinese name the place is a "post station" for caravans; other regional names stress the caravan or the ribat. The ribat was originally a frontier fortress for volunteer defenders, later used as a caravanserai.

Atmosphere: A frontier stop beneath a towering wall: Eremite mercenaries, merchants, researchers and adventurers gather around a bulletin board, and the village is a way-station between forest and desert.

Dangers: Sandstorms beyond the wall; in Chapter III the Traveler is trailed by Eremites here and needs Alhaitham's help to get away.

Travel: Caravan Ribat is the usual stop for anyone crossing between Gandharva Ville and the forest and Aaru Village and the desert.

Quests: In the Archon Quest the Traveler and Paimon narrowly escape Eremites trailing them at Caravan Ribat, thanks to Alhaitham; he then offers to go with them to Aaru Village. While searching for the missing Village Keepers, Dehya takes the Traveler back to the Ribat to meet her drinking friends.

The 4.6 Cyno story quest "Footprints Sunken Beneath the Sands" begins here and continues to Aaru Village and the Temple of Silence. In the 6.6 Welkin Moon story "Your Past Is Like a Garden" Dehya and Candace, having escorted people home, talk here with Sethos before heading back to Aaru Village.

During the Village Keepers search, Dehya meets her drinking buddy Zaki at the local tavern and says she has a spice-trading deal for Delavar. Zaki leads her and the Traveler to the spot, which proves to be an ambush by Delavar and Engur, Eremite radicals; Dehya and the Traveler defeat them, and the captives are questioned back in Aaru Village.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Caravan Ribat is an operating checkpoint under the Wall of Samiel. Nothing in canon shows it destroyed or abandoned.

It was last shown as a gathering place in the 6.6 Welkin Moon story, with Candace and Dehya saying they have finished escorting people home and are heading back to Aaru Village.

48.comment: Caravan Ribat: The Four at Loggerheads at Caravan Ribat
48.content: In Chapter III Act III the Traveler and Paimon escape Eremites trailing them at Caravan Ribat, thanks to Alhaitham, who says he is still studying the capsule and suspects the Traveler is hiding something. He offers to accompany them to Aaru Village, and they accept. Later, in Act IV, Dehya explains why she resents the wall: she says it serves to keep out desert-dwellers as well as sandstorms, that the sages treat desert people as tools to be used and discarded, and that she would tear the wall down with her own hands if she could.

49.comment: Caravan Ribat: The Wall of Samiel
49.content: The Wall of Samiel separates the Dharma Forest from the Great Red Sand and shields the rainforest from sandstorms. It is said to have been created by Greater Lord Rukkhadevata. The Akademiya maintains it, researchers such as Behnam work on it, and destroying it is forbidden. Caravan Ribat is at its foot.

50.content:
Chatrakam Cave: Chatrakam Cave is a cave system hidden deep in the Lokapala Jungle of Sumeru's Dharma Forest, best known for its huge number of fungi. Humans seldom enter: the damp air suits mushrooms, and apart from the Vanara, for whom mushroom picking is a duty, few people go in. Underground ruins, Eremites, ruin machines and the Realm of Khab are also found there.

The name derives from the Sanskrit chatraka, meaning mushroom. The cave also holds a Battered Notebook tied to the quest Aranakin's Old Friend, and the Realm of Khab opens within it.

Geography: The cave has two mapped levels, a Northern Underground Ruins and a Southern Cavern, with a Dendro Elemental Monument, Clusterleaf of Cultivation, Four-Leaf Sigil, bouncy mushrooms, poisonous mushrooms, Gloomy Path puzzles and Auspicious Branch plants. Outside lies Lokapala Jungle forest where hilichurl berserkers, Dendro samachurls and Eremite Sunfrost are found.

Nilotpala Lotus is the local specialty. The Battered Notebook interactable inside the cave is linked by the wiki to the World Quest Aranakin's Old Friend, which begins on the hill northwest of the cave.

Places: The Realm of Khab, reached from the Northern Underground Ruins, is described as the place where the memories of Nara Varuna and the Aranara converge and where the dreams of the Barsam Flower gather. Khab is a Persian word for sleep.

The Realm of Khab is entered during the Risen Moon Chapter of the Archon Quest. The wiki records Nara Varuna as the Traveler's sibling in that context.

Dangers: Many fungi: floating Hydro and Dendro fungi, stretchy Geo fungi, grounded Hydroshrooms and winged Dendroshrooms. Eremites (Ravenbeak halberdiers, axe vanguards, linebreakers, crossbowmen and sword-dancers) are also inside. Ruin Destroyers, Cruisers, Defenders and Graders form the elite foes.

Outside the cave there are Ruin Drake Skywatchers; a Fatui agent appears north of the cave during a limited event.

People: The Vanara, who treat mushroom picking as a duty, are the only people said to go into the cave in any number. According to the Amurta scholars quoted in the expedition text, the fungi come in a great many varieties.

The Aranara Aranakin is found on the hill northwest of the cave, singing next to a seelie; his quest ends with a notebook on the second floor of a tree house.

Quests: Aranakin's Old Friend (3.0) begins at the hill northwest of the cave and ends with a notebook in a tree house; Aranakin has forgotten many of the friends he made. The limited event Fabulous Fungus Frenzy (3.2) placed a Fatui Pyro Agent north of the cave carrying a letter from Second Lieutenant Yurochka that plotted against a rogue Fatui named Elchingen.

The Fabulous Fungus Frenzy material is limited-event content: the letter tells its recipient to ambush Elchingen as he is transferred to a prison after the Akademiya handles him, to prevent his unauthorised plans from endangering Yurochka's division.

Atmosphere: Damp, closed-in and thick with fungi; the official text calls it a damp environment hidden deep in the woods, ideal for fungal growth, and few people willingly go in.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Chatrakam Cave is still a fungus-ridden cave that few people enter.

The Fabulous Fungus Frenzy event is over, but the cave and the Realm of Khab remain accessible.

51.content:
A dream-like realm said to be the convergence of Nara Varuna's and the Aranara's memories and the gathering place of the Barsam Flower's dreams. It is reached through Chatrakam Cave in the Risen Moon Chapter.

The name Khab is Persian for sleep.

52.comment: Chatrakam Cave: Fabulous Fungus Frenzy Fatui Letter
52.content: During the limited event Fabulous Fungus Frenzy, a letter from Second Lieutenant Yurochka reveals Fatui rivalry: Elchingen is accused of acting without orders to win recognition, and an agent north of Chatrakam Cave is told to ambush him and remove his followers.

53.content:
Chemin Oublie: Chemin Oublie is a tunnel that connects the Girdle of the Sands in Sumeru to Romaritime Harbor in Fontaine. Its French name means "Forgotten Path". It is a point of interest, not a region.

It was added with Fontaine in version 4.0.

Geography: A cave-like tunnel running from Sumeru's Realm of Farakhkert to the harbor in Fontaine, a large coastal elevator and observation deck beside a waterfall that also provides the passage into Sumeru. Along it are seelie to follow, a Time Trial Challenge, Trishiraite and Mourning Flower to gather, and many sea shells scattered about.

Romaritime Harbor, at the Fontaine end, is a coastal elevator and observation deck on a waterfall vista, connected to the Clementine Line aquabus rail to the Court of Fontaine.

History: Canon does not say who made the tunnel. The wiki infers from the name and the many shells that Oceanids may have used it as a pilgrimage route.

In Sumeru's own story, the Oceanids rejected the ideals of the new Hydro Archon Focalors, travelled to Tunigi Hollow in search of their former master Egeria, found the Harvisptokhm was not what they hoped, and scattered; people later followed their pilgrimage trail, which eventually led to the Purification Spring domain. Whether they passed through Chemin Oublie is not stated.

Dangers: Hydro slimes and Hydro hilichurl rogues.

Travel: The tunnel is the walking link between Sumeru and Fontaine at Romaritime Harbor.

Atmosphere: Quiet and half-forgotten, in keeping with its name, with sea shells strewn through the cave giving a hint of the water-people who may once have passed this way.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tunnel is an open connection between Sumeru and Fontaine.

Nothing after its 4.0 introduction has changed it.

54.comment: Chemin Oublie: Chemin Oublie Name and Shells
54.content:
Chemin Oublie ("Forgotten Path") connects the Girdle of the Sands to Fontaine's Romaritime Harbor. The wiki points to the name and the scattered sea shells as a possible sign of an Oceanid pilgrimage route, an inference not confirmed in game text.

Use the inference as a rumour, not a fact, when portraying travellers: nobody in canon states that the Oceanids walked this tunnel.

55.content:
Chinvat Ravine: Chinvat Ravine is a ravine below Sumeru City, at the base of the Divine Tree, in the Avidya Forest area of Sumeru's Dharma Forest. Forest travellers use the name for the passage beneath the great tree, as an echo of the ancient literary image of crossing a sea of ignorance to reach the light of truth.

The name is a Sumeru-flavoured borrowing of the Chinvat Bridge, the bridge of judgement in Zoroastrian belief.

Geography: The ravine lies below Sumeru City at the foot of the Divine Tree. The expedition text treats it as the last stage of a forest journey before the city of wisdom. It is part of the Avidya Forest.

History: The expedition description explains the name: in Sumeru's ancient literary canon, Chinvat stands for the bitter sea of ignorance that seekers must cross to see the light on the far shore. Those who now navigate the forests apply it to this ravine, perhaps for the elation of finally arriving at the city of wisdom.

The Chinese name means "Separate-and-Cross Ravine", taken from a rendering of the Chinvat Bridge as the Separating-and-Crossing Bridge. In Zoroastrian belief that bridge sifts the dead, parting the living world from the world of the dead.

Dangers: Eremites (crossbow users, linebreakers and sword-dancers) and shaggy sumpter beasts roam the area. A random encounter called Unscrupulous Dealings can place the Traveler across from Fatui skirmishers, including Anemoboxer and Pyroslinger types, who are in what Paimon calls a dodgy under-the-table deal with Eremites; the Traveler is expected to break it up.

Atmosphere: The official wording gives it a sense of relief and arrival: the elation of reaching the city of wisdom after a long forest crossing.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Chinvat Ravine is an ordinary part of Sumeru's open world with no later story change.

The Fatui and Eremites that appear there are random encounters rather than any lasting presence.

56.content:
Name lore for the ravine below the Divine Tree: Chinvat is the bitter sea of ignorance in Sumeru's old literature, and travellers use it for the passage into the city of wisdom.

Its Zoroastrian source is the Chinvat Bridge, a sifting bridge between the living and the dead.

57.comment: Chinvat Ravine: Chinvat Ravine Random Encounter
57.content: The random event Unscrupulous Dealings can start in Chinvat Ravine, Ardravi Valley, Gandha Hill, Hypostyle Desert or the Land of Lower Setekh. The Traveler comes upon Fatui and Eremites in a shady exchange and is expected to defeat them.

58.content:
Citadel of Regzar: The Citadel of Regzar is the headquarters of the Corps of Thirty, the mercenary brigade that keeps the peace in Sumeru City for the Akademiya. It stands in the middle of the city, near Treasures Street. The name is a Persian word for desert.

The Corps began as thirty Eremite mercenaries hired by the sages; the barracks here fly the Eremite crest and colours on their banners, while members wear teal-green scarves with a petal-like emblem.

People: Rukh Shah, the Parchamdar, commands the Corps and is the youngest ever to hold the post. Asfand is the Consultant (the administrative leader). Others here are the researcher Effendi and the members Sekkura (called "Swallow"), Udad ("Goat") and Yunus ("Bigfish").

The Corps is the oldest of the Eremite brigades and coordinates the others, though its relations with other Eremites are tenuous, and Rukh Shah warns the Traveler about Eremites elsewhere. In the quest "After Repose" Collei and Asfand can be found at the Citadel.

Governance: Not a formal army but a permanently hired mercenary brigade working for the Akademiya; the Parchamdar is military commander and the Consultant handles administration.

Atmosphere: Disciplined but not grim, a barracks of hired soldiers in the middle of a scholarly city.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it remains the Corps' base.

Further details: The Corps takes its name from its first thirty members and kept it as it grew. Alhaitham notes its poor relations with the Ayn Al-Ahmar, devout followers of King Deshret. The Chinese name of the building can be glossed as Sand-Gathering Hall.

59.content:
Dar al-Shifa (also: Eleazar Hospital, Abandoned hospital near Aaru Village): Dar al-Shifa is an abandoned hospital in the Land of Lower Setekh, not far from Aaru Village. It once specialised in treating patients with Eleazar, the disease that covers the body in scabs and ulcers. Old notes found inside suggest that a doctor there was using patients as test subjects for dangerous treatments. In the Archon Quest the Traveler, Paimon and Alhaitham investigate it after villagers report crying at night.

The name means "house of healing" in Arabic, and the in-game viewpoint says it is named for a prayer for patients. It is now silent, missing both the doctors' bustle and the songs of recovered patients.

Geography: A weathered desert building, half full of sand, with a barrier hiding an older underground wing. A trapdoor leads down to a lower level that looks like a second hospital tucked inside the first. Tunnels beneath hold the remains of dead hilichurls. Eremites roam the surroundings.

In the Archon Quest the entrance and the lower level are sealed by barriers that open only when three Dendro monuments are activated, with Alhaitham's Vision starting the process. Hidden Exploration Objectives in the area include the Eleazar Hospital Notes and Abbas' Escape.

History: The hospital treated Eleazar patients, and rooms, labels and patient items such as bowls bearing patients' names remain. A medical file records a farmer called Abbas under a doctor named Amoudi, then continued by a doctor whose name is blacked out. The treatment documents describe replacement of a patient's skin and limb, and a physician's note links high elemental quantities in the body to the disease. The doctor writes of control without elemental power, a possible military use, and sees the patients as specimens.

Specimen IV, Abbas, is said to have attempted several times to leave, citing a guiding "God's voice", which the doctor recorded as a delusion. An emergency notice in the hospital mentions a 23-year-old patient with a mole on his left forehead and encouragement not to give up hope. A weekly meal and duty schedule lists Ibrahim and Amoudi as physicians. The date and cause of the hospital's closure are not given.

The wiki treats the redacted doctor as likely Dottore, but the text of the notes only blacks the name out. A linked Hidden Exploration Objective, Abbas' Escape, retraces Abbas's escape route from the hospital.

Status as of 7.1: Abandoned for years. In Cry From the Eleazar Hospital the party learns that the crying heard from the village at night came from here, and finds Razak, an Akademiya scholar and a senior of Alhaitham, in a mindless state.

The people who had been held here were already taken away when the party arrived, leaving drag marks from a cart. The hospital is later used as evidence in Alhaitham's reasoning about the Akademiya.

Dangers: Hilichurls and an Eremite presence nearby; a locked lower level that requires the Dendro monuments to open.

Atmosphere: Quiet and dusty, with sand piling in the corridors. It feels like a place hurriedly left, with old schedules, vases and tableware still in place.

60.comment: Dar al-Shifa: Razak and the night crying
60.content:
In the quest Cry From the Eleazar Hospital, the village girl Shani tells the party she hears faint crying at night coming from far away, and that the guards have heard similar sounds. Alhaitham leads the party to the hospital, where they find Razak, an Akademiya scholar whom Alhaitham says never trained in the forest or reached the Satyavada Life stage, and who now cannot speak and has unfocused eyes. Alhaitham links his state to that of the Eremite Mizri at Port Ormos.

Alhaitham's reasoning: the Akademiya spread a false rumour of King Deshret's resurrection so that the Radicals would round up the exiled "mad scholars" for them, turning them from exiles into missing persons who could be used as material for Divine Knowledge Capsules. He is explicit that this is a deduction and that he is not acting out of pity.

61.content:
Debris of Panjvahe (also: Panjvahe, The Forgotten River Valley, Remnants of Five Oases): The Debris of Panjvahe is a dry river valley and the ruins around it in the Desert of Hadramaveth, Sumeru. Panjvahe was once an irrigated district under Gurabad, where nobles sailed ornate boats on the river and flew hunting falcons. Its water system failed, the district fell into poverty and unrest, and today the valley is quiet and mostly empty, with wild vultures where falcons once flew.

Panjvahe's fate is told in notes and inscriptions: neglected maintenance of the irrigation network fed by the water system at Mt. Damavand, shrinking oases, and a Gurabad council that refused to pay for repairs. The name is read as "five oases" in the Chinese and Japanese versions.

Geography: A broad river valley cut into the desert, with ruins along its sides and a hidden quiet pool in the valley. It lies in the same desert as Gurabad and Mt. Damavand. The nearby Fane of Panjvahe, a domain listed under The Sands of Three Canals, is a separate place: a hermitage that Gurabad's ancestors built for the Lord of the Desert and that now shelters desert dwellers and bandits.

The Debris of Panjvahe has a fishing spot with desert species such as the Sandstorm Angler and several kinds of axe marlin, according to the wiki's fishing data.

History: In the viewpoint's telling, the great river valley once irrigated Panjvahe, and nobles of Gurabad sailed on it in ornate boats. Records at Mt. Damavand describe the system behind it: Jinn fragments set into machinery regulated the water supply, which was more efficient than older methods. Over time the canal system was clogged by sand. The priests wanted large-scale maintenance but the Jinni Ferigees, who guarded the nearby Orchard of Pairidaeza, refused it because it might disturb the Goddess of Flowers's tomb, and offered some of her own power instead.

Under King Parvezravan, maintenance funds were cut and the filtration system failed; a note says Panjvahe's irrigation network became unusable, mud and sand clogged everywhere, and the wealthy left the farmland. A note says the king seemed bewitched by Jinn-made spectacles and blind to the ground loosening beneath him. Gurabad's Records of Gurabad report the Council of Nobles refusing a general's request for funds, citing the district's long poverty and rebellion and the rise of the Brass Mask followers.

The same notes connect the failure of Panjvahe's water to Ferigees's weakening: she grew ever less responsive and by the last note lacked even the strength for wrath, though the records are the notes of a human official and not Ferigees's own words. Panjvahe's trouble is thus part of Gurabad's slow decline before its fall to a chasm.

Status as of 7.1: Today it is an empty, quiet valley of the Great Red Sand, with the remains of the old district along the dry riverbed.

As of Version 7.1 nothing found changes Panjvahe's status as an abandoned ruin.

Atmosphere: Dry stone and cracked riverbed, red vultures overhead, and the remembered image of gilded boats and falcons. A place of lost abundance, quieter than the ruins of Gurabad itself.

62.comment: Debris of Panjvahe: Records of Mt. Damavand
62.content: Three stone tablets near Mt. Damavand, readable only after pipe puzzles are solved in Dune-Entombed Fecundity: Part II. They record a priest's worry over falling water output, Ferigees's refusal of large maintenance, and the king's budget cuts, giving the best picture of why Panjvahe's irrigation failed.

63.content:
Desert of Hadramaveth: The Desert of Hadramaveth is the southwestern part of Sumeru's Great Red Sand, opened up in version 3.4. Its dunes and scimitar-shaped ravines hide the ruins of the ancient city of Gurabad, and the nomadic Tanit tribe once lived in its camps. Official text says a lost city lies hidden there, with a wandering tribe seeking refuge in its ruins, and that incessant sandstorms erode all things.

The name blends Hadramaut, a South Arabian region, with the biblical Hazarmaveth ("court of death"). It has eleven subareas, more than any other area in the game. Its main story is the Dirge of Bilqis world-quest series, in which the Traveler accompanies Jeht to the Eternal Oasis.

Geography: A broad desert plain crossed by canyons and wadis, with long sandstorms that the wiki lists as a regular feature. Ruins, obelisks, sandglasses, Jinn shrines and atmospheric vortices dot it, and wenut roam its dunes. The boss enemy is the Setekh Wenut, and the local specialties are Henna Berry and Sand Grease Pupa.

Subareas include Gurabad (southwest), Mt. Damavand with its permanent tornado, Wadi Al-Majuj (a large canyon south of the mountain, whose name roughly means canyon of the Majuj, the hilichurls), the Sands of Three Canals (an elevated area north of the mountain), the Sands of Al-Azif (one of the flatter areas, where wenut roam and the Wenut Tunnels lie below), Safhe Shatranj, Deshret's Glass Goblet and the Tanit Camps on the southern border.

Places: Gurabad, the ruined City of Brass and City of Kings. The Tanit Camps, the tribe's last settlement. Mt. Damavand, the smoking mountain with a tornado at its heart. Safhe Shatranj, the former Temples Forsaken, with a giant chessboard. Deshret's Glass Goblet, the sunken heart where the way to the Eternal Oasis lies.

Safhe Shatranj is the canyon the Tanit call the Great Rift; a chessboard puzzle with five chess pieces is found here. Before the quest The Temple Where Sand Flows Like Tears it is called The Temples Forsaken, and the sand is cleared during that quest. Its pieces are said to correspond to real structures of Deshret's civilisation.

Damavand's name in the lost desert tongue means "the mountain from which smoke and ash arise". Deshret's Glass Goblet is first shown in Dune-Entombed Fecundity: Part I and opened in Part III. The Eternal Oasis (the Orchard of Pairidaeza) lies beyond it.

People: The Tanit are a matrilineal Eremite tribe who revere the Goddess of Flowers and are led by a Matriarch and nine Elders. They value words and knowledge but distrust the Akasha, trade crocodile products, spices and essential oils, and hunt wenut for spice. After the Dirge of Bilqis the Tanit are removed and the Vahumana researcher Tanjiyy takes their camps.

Some desert tribes adopt or plunder young children and raise them as Falcons devoted to the elders; the Tanit's Falcon tradition is described as a perversion of King Deshret's priests' archery ceremonies. They have no written law, and their worst enemies are traitors from within. Jeht, the young Eremite the Traveler befriended in Lost in the Sands, belongs to the tribe in these quests; her father Jebrael is listed by the wiki as a former member.

History: Gurabad rose after Nabu Malikata's death and fell before the forbidden-knowledge incident that ended King Deshret's civilisation. According to the wiki, Ormazd ruled until Liloupar engineered his murder; his adopted son Kisra, who took the name Parvezravan and was in fact Liloupar's son, built Jinn-powered machines and was killed by his own son Shiruyeh. Liloupar's use of Abyssal power then sent much of the city into a chasm and a plague killed most of its people, after which Gurabad was abandoned and attempts to revive it failed.

Later accounts, drawn from the same wiki page, record Shah Ramshahr, the Cities of the Seven Towers, and a succession of kings and Khagans who fought over the desert; they involve Ay-Khanoum, Tulaytullah and Saleh. The Akademiya once sent an expedition to Gurabad, noted in Zandik's papers, and a massive Ruin Golem still sits in the ruins, like the ones at Devantaka Mountain and the Valley of Dahri.

In Memories of Gurabad, Liloupar's story continues after the Traveler places chess pieces on the Safhe Shatranj board and clears constructs; the gate to Gurabad opens, previously illegible stone tablets become readable, and Liloupar leaves her bottle to reunite with her children there while her gadget still works for the player.

Dangers: Sandstorms; wenut and the Setekh Wenut; Primal Constructs (Repulsors, Reshapers, Prospectors) and Eremites; hilichurls; Fatui camps (reports by a Fatui captain, Zoya Snezhevna, are among the interactables); quicksand; and the desert itself.

In The Dirge of Bilqis, a Fatui conspiracy and Tanit politics turn a pilgrimage into a series of ambushes; see the Tanit entry.

Travel: The Temir Mountains link the desert to the rest of the Girdle of the Sands; from the Tanit Camps the Dirge quests use Deshret's old canal tunnels to reach Mt. Damavand and the Glass Goblet. Before taking the quest the game recommends finishing Golden Slumber and accepting The Dirge of Bilqis.

Quests: The Dirge of Bilqis (3.4): Wisdom Has Built Her House, She Has Hewn Out Her Seven Pillars; The Temple Where Sand Flows Like Tears; Dune-Entombed Fecundity Parts I to III; and The Eternal Dream, Ever Lush. Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters... follows it (Behold, the Sign Comes Like A Thief...; Make Bright the Arrows, Gather the Shields...; For Her Judgment Reaches to the Skies...). Memories of Gurabad, The Fallen Falcon, Tadhla the Falcon and the Culling of the Worms series also take place here.

Atmosphere: Wind-scoured, haunted and desolate: ravines like scimitars, a tornado at the mountain's heart, and the dry hush of a city that once held kings. The official blurb hints at a story lost in time waiting to be uncovered.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the desert is an open, ruined wilderness without a Tanit tribe.

The Tanit's camps hold only the Vahumana researcher Tanjiyy; nothing from 6.x or 7.0-7.1 changes the area.

64.content:
A nomadic matrilineal Eremite tribe of the Desert of Hadramaveth, led by the Matriarch Babel. In The Dirge of Bilqis the Traveler and Jeht seek the Eternal Oasis; afterwards Babel, who had conspired with the Fatui against the other elders, tries to take the oasis for herself, and the Traveler and Jeht destroy the tribe.

The Falcons are children taken in and raised to be devoted to the elders. Aderfi, Azariq and Yuften are among the named Tanit.

65.content: An ancient desert city in the southwest of the Desert of Hadramaveth that fell before King Deshret's forbidden-knowledge incident. Liloupar, a Jinni, plotted its fall over three generations because Ormazd had not freed its slaves; a revolt, a chasm and a plague ended it.

66.content:
Deshret's Glass Goblet (also: Crystal Goblet of Al-Ahmar, Glass Goblet of King Deshret): Deshret's Glass Goblet is a huge goblet-shaped structure in the depths of Mt. Damavand, in the Desert of Hadramaveth. The platform at its center is the way into the Orchard of Pairidaeza, the Eternal Oasis. It is first seen in the Dirge of Bilqis world quests, and access opens during Dune-Entombed Fecundity: Part III.

Desert tales say King Deshret left the cup behind when he bade farewell to joy. The Jinni Liloupar says the visible structure is not the true goblet but a mechanism that holds the oasis in stasis. It was guarded by Ferigees, a Jinni whose spirit lived in a machine on the goblet.

Geography: The Goblet sits inside the cavernous interior of Mt. Damavand, reached by passing ancient pipes and mechanisms, with a platform at its center that leads to the Eternal Oasis. Seen from above it looks like a wide crystal cup. Jeht, a member of the Tanit tribe, described pipes running into the temple inside the mountain.

Liloupar remembers that her master Al-Ahmar (King Deshret) once shaped an elaborate canal system here to irrigate mortal lands, in a time when the dune was green hills before sandstorms took it.

History: In the account Liloupar gives in the quest, Deshret left the cup as a receptacle for past traumas and memories. Jinn-built machinery under the mountain, powered by gems under the sands according to artifact lore, keeps the oasis in a frozen moment. When the Traveler's party reached the center, Ferigees blocked them; her fall also ended the old arrangement.

The party broke the oasis's stabilising device on entering, according to Liloupar, which means the Goblet's mechanism no longer holds the place in perfect stasis and the oasis is eventually doomed to be buried.

Status as of 7.1: Ferigees was destroyed in Dune-Entombed Fecundity: Part III, and the Goblet is open to travellers as the way down to the oasis. The quest series continues in The Eternal Dream, Ever Lush.

The Goblet's shape is echoed by a chesspiece in Safhe Shatranj, another subarea of the Desert of Hadramaveth, though canon does not explain the link.

67.comment: Deshret's Glass Goblet: Ferigees at the Goblet
67.content: Her last words, as quoted in the quest, call the oasis an empty tomb that will crumble like her and like Liloupar, who is not whole. Liloupar had earlier called her sister, in a Chinese term the wiki notes is not necessarily about family.

68.content:
Devantaka Mountain (also: Devantaka): Devantaka Mountain is a mountain in Sumeru's Ardravi Valley, in the Dharma Forest, home to a massive Ruin Golem built in Khaenri'ah's time. The scholar Pir Kavikavus of the Akademiya's Kshahrewar once studied the machine and suffered a terrible accident, and the Akasha System gets no signal on the mountain. The official description calls it the mountain that saw the fall of the demons.

The name probably references Devantaka, a Hindu asura whose name means destroyer of gods. The Ruin Golem was the setting of the Vimana Agama world quests, in which a Kshahrewar researcher called Jazari studies it.

Geography: Valleys and greenery hide a giant machine whose circular holes seem to watch time pass. The Ruin Golem has three levels of rooms and corridors, with energy blocks, large gears and lifts; caves run beneath and behind it, and below it lies Dev's Cavern. Ruin Drakes, Ruin Graders and an Aeonblight Drake are the main hostile machines and beasts.

Local specialties are Nilotpala Lotus and Rukkhashava Mushrooms. Breaking Dendrogranum-locked rocks can release a Ruin Scout that leads to more ancient automatons and a chest.

Places: The Ruin Golem: one of three known in Sumeru, the others being at the Valley of Dahri and the Desert of Hadramaveth. Dev's Cavern: a cavern beneath the mountain where the Golem's core was removed and sealed, now also where the Abyss Order seeks power. The Ruin Golem's top floor and side chambers hold notes from the Akademiya investigation team's Zandik.

Inside, an Ancient Work Log records defects: energy cores stopping from overload, a weapons system melted from overuse, a smart boot system failing and walking ability lost. Mysterious Chronicles record the fates of three knights of the Schwanenritter: Hildric (death from organ failure in a foreign land), Hadura (executed by Knight Marshal Anfortas for a betrayal that caused irreversible damage to a machine; the Marshal lost his left eye) and Ynghildr (missing in battle against the onslaught of dark beasts).

History: The Ruin Golem was a Khaenri'ahn war machine whose core was removed and sealed in Dev's Cavern. Hundreds of years on, the Akademiya's Kshahrewar studied it. Pir Kavikavus joined Kshahrewar after the cataclysm of 500 years ago, rose to Herbad before thirty, and became the last person known to enter the Golem for systematic research before an accident erased his work. Kshahrewar's prestige fell, and the Akademiya has not raised its funding since.

Kavikavus was a friend of the Aranara Aralohita, who helped him and later hid some of his research behind riddles and puzzles. In the Pir Kavikavus Prize, named for him, scholars under forty are honoured. Many in Kshahrewar still admire him, including Jazari, who hopes to follow in his steps.

The wiki records that Kavikavus discovered the Akasha System has no signal on Devantaka Mountain; the Bimarstan proverb column quotes him on it.

Dangers: The Golem's Chaos Core leaked energy and polluted the nearby forest until it was sealed. Monsters gathered at the machine; Abyss Order mages sought the core's power; Eremites, hilichurls, Rishboland tigers and fungi are also present.

Ynghildr, a Khaenri'ahn knight cursed into an Abyssal creature, blocks the Traveler from the Golem's controls in Vimana Agama: Jazari's Chapter.

Quests: Vimana Agama: Ararycan, an Aranara, investigates a contamination around Devantaka Mountain with the Traveler and meets the Kshahrewar researcher Jazari. Jazari cannot see Ararycan, who explains that humans lose the ability as they grow older. Jazari's chapter has the Traveler reactivate the Ruin Golem enough for its arm to smash the ground and reopen Dev's Cavern; the Golem then breaks down again. In Until Vana is Healed, the Traveler finds Kavikavus's hidden research paper, brings it to Jazari and helps seal the Golem's Chaos Core, weakening the Abyss Order's threat to the forest.

The two quests use the mountain as stage and make Jazari the keeper of its research, while Ararycan tends the surrounding wood.

Atmosphere: A green and quiet valley slope with a colossal rusted machine watching over it: the official wording stresses a machine that has lost its light. Sumeru scholars and Aranara regard the place with awe and some sorrow.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Golem still stands idle, its core sealed, and Jazari researches it.

Nothing after 3.2 has changed the mountain, and no later Sumeru or Snezhnaya material in 6.x-7.1 references it.

69.content:
Historical Kshahrewar prodigy who became a Herbad before thirty and was the last known person to research the Ruin Golem on Devantaka Mountain. An accident lost his research and he probably died. He was friends with the Aranara Aralohita, who hid some of his work behind puzzles.

A prize for scholars under forty is named after him. His paper on sealing the Golem's Chaos Core was found in Until Vana is Healed and tested by Jazari.

70.comment: Devantaka Mountain: Dev's Cavern and the Chaos Core
70.content: Dev's Cavern lies beneath the mountain, where the Ruin Golem's core was sealed. The core leaked and polluted the forest; entrances were blocked, and the Golem's arm blow in Vimana Agama reopened them. The Traveler sealed the core with Kavikavus's method, which weakened the Abyss mages who tried to stop it.

71.content:
Dev's Cavern: Dev's Cavern is a cave in Ardravi Valley, in the Dharma Forest of Sumeru. It is a minor point of interest whose name uses the old Sumeru word for Abyssal monsters.

It is unlocked during the world quest Vimana Agama: Dev Delver Chapter. Its inhabitants are hilichurls and samachurls, with elite Abyss Mages of the Cryo, Electro, Hydro and Pyro varieties.

Because it is an investigation site rather than a story location, canon gives it no individual history.

Geography: A cavern within Ardravi Valley in the Dharma Forest.

History: A Sumeru loading-screen tip says the dark beasts from beneath the earth were once called Dev by the people of Sumeru, and the term also appears in the Oracle Parchment, for the End of Death text. This explains the name in general but not the cave itself.

Dev is a Persian-derived word for monsters; in-game it was applied to Abyssal creatures.

Dangers: Hilichurls, Electro and Geo samachurls, and elite Abyss Mages (Cryo, Electro, Hydro, Pyro).

Quests: Vimana Agama: Dev Delver Chapter unlocks the location.

Atmosphere: Dim, enclosed and quietly hostile, a hideout of Abyss casters and hilichurls.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 no change to the cavern was found.

Nothing in 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya) content was found that mentions it.

72.content:
Dharma Forest (also: Sumeru rainforest, Sumeru's rainforest): Dharma Forest is the rainforest half of Sumeru: a green, humid, many-layered country of giant trees, mushrooms, rivers and rain, in the east and centre of the nation. Sumeru City, the "City of Wisdom", is built on a vast tree here and houses the Sumeru Akademiya. Forest Rangers patrol the woods, merchants and students crowd Port Ormos, and the small plant-like Aranara live out of sight in the dreams of children. Its great danger is the Withering, a rot that spreads through the land. The desert lies beyond the Wall of Samiel to the west.

Travellers from Liyue can reach it directly from the Chasm, and Avidya Forest is the first area the Traveler enters in Sumeru. The forest is Dendro country: the nation's Archon, Lesser Lord Kusanali (Nahida), is the God of Wisdom, and the plants, fungi and "dream" magic here all reflect that.

Geography: Seven areas make up the subregion: Avidya Forest (the heart, with Sumeru City and Gandharva Ville), Ardravi Valley (the great river and its trade route), Ashavan Realm (the southern wetlands and hills), Lokapala Jungle (the north coast), Vissudha Field, Vanarana and the small Lost Nursery. The Wall of Samiel separates the forest from the Great Red Sand on the west. The river Ardravi cut the valley that carries Sumeru's main waterborne trade down to the southern shore.

Ashavan Realm is described as a materially rich southern land of hills, woods and wetland, with mighty ramparts guarding its western edge from the sandstorms. Lokapala Jungle runs along the north coast from Mawtiyima Forest, near Chenyu Vale in Liyue, to the slope of a nameless mountain west of Bayda Harbor, where it meets the Desert of Hadramaveth and the Realm of Farakhkert. The forest's flora includes Padisarah, Nilotpala lotus, Kalpalata lotus and Rukkhashava mushrooms, and fungi of every kind roam the undergrowth.

Places: Sumeru City sits on the Divine Tree, with the Akademiya in the middle and upper part of the tree and the Sanctuary of Surasthana, where Nahida lives, on top. Gandharva Ville, "the City Above the Forest", is the Forest Rangers' main outpost. Port Ormos is the largest port in Sumeru, a trade hub under two giant trees; Vimara Village is a quiet fishing town on the river between the two. Caravan Ribat is a fortified village at the foot of the Wall of Samiel, the checkpoint for everyone going to or from the desert and Aaru Village. Apam Woods is a rainforest where the rain never fully ceases; Pardis Dhyai is a garden research site of Amurta scholars.

Devantaka Mountain holds a huge Ruin Golem that the legendary scholar Pir Kavikavus once studied, with a terrible accident as the result; the Akasha has no signal on the mountain. Mawtiyima Forest is a forest of enormous glowing mushrooms; Mawtiyima is described as an energy form born of the forest's ancient dreams that fights the Withering, and in an ancient tongue the name once meant "human death". The Palace of Alcazarzaray in the Lokapala Jungle belongs to Dori and was designed by Kaveh. The Fane of Ashvattha in Vissudha Field shelters the first Vasara Tree and seals the way down to Old Vanarana. Ruins of Dahri are Khaenri'ahn remnants in Ashavan Realm.

Other named subareas are Chinvat Ravine, Gandha Hill, Yazadaha Pool, Yasna Monument, Bayda Harbor, Chatrakam Cave, Old Vanarana and Vanarana (the real Vanarana and its dream form Mahavanaranapna). The Lost Nursery is unlocked only by finishing the Aranyaka quest series' third part; before that, Paimon turns the Traveler back.

People: Forest Rangers (the civil-service guardians of the forest; the senior ones are Forest Watchers, among them Tighnari) patrol the woods and report to Pardis Dhyai's researchers. Students and scholars of the Akademiya fill Sumeru City and visit Port Ormos when academic life gets too stressful. Eremite mercenaries from the desert work in Port Ormos and Caravan Ribat. Traders, dockworkers and fishers fill the river towns. Children are the ones who see the Aranara.

Notable residents: Tighnari (Forest Watcher, Chief Officer) and Collei (Forest Ranger) at Gandharva Ville; the architect Kaveh, who designed Port Ormos's arch bridge and the Palace of Alcazarzaray; Dori, the merchant who owns the palace. The Rishboland Tigers, the forest's great cats, have inherited the "tiger" name of the lords of the forest, a line that began with Viaghara and whose last lord died defending the forest in the cataclysm.

Governance: Authority rests with the Sumeru Akademiya, whose darshans (colleges) run the city and manage the forest's affairs, with the Forest Rangers as the field service and the Corps of Thirty and General Mahamatra supplying order. Nahida is the Archon, kept for a long time in the Sanctuary of Surasthana and treated as a distant figurehead by the sages.

The Akademiya also maintains the Wall of Samiel, and destroying it is prohibited. In the Archon Quest the sages used the Akasha, a network that connects minds, to control the populace and Nahida; by the end of the chapter Nahida had taken the Akasha back for herself and cut off the sages' access. By the 6.6 crisis a new council of sages served alongside Naphis: Baladhuri (Vahumana), Alkindi (Spantamad), Firnas (Kshahrewar), Shakir (Rtawahist) and Rushd (Haravatat).

Culture: Sumeru's ideal is wisdom, and the forest shows it in its schooling, theatres and rapt debates. The Sabzeruz Festival, Lesser Lord Kusanali's birthday celebration, was revived in the Archon Quest; the Akademiya Extravaganza is the Akademiya's festival of an annual Wisdom Gala and a four-yearly Interdarshan Championship (seen in the 3.6 limited-time event A Parade of Providence). Folk belief holds the Aranara are the imaginary friends of children; adults mostly dismiss them. Student life and bazaar bargaining colour the towns.

Desert mercenary culture, the Eremites, is visible at the edges, at Caravan Ribat and in Port Ormos. Place names draw on Sanskrit and Persian vocabulary (dharma, avidya, ardravi, vanarana and so on).

History: By the wiki's reconstruction, the forest was once the domain of the Dendro Dragon Apep's court and the cradle of the first fern that grew into the Irminsul. After the Archon War era, Greater Lord Rukkhadevata left her friend King Deshret's desert kingdom, came to the east of the Great Red Sand and used the Varuna Contraption to turn desert into rainforest. She raised the Wall of Samiel against sandstorms, and the forest king Viaghara was born. Her followers became the founders of the Amurta darshan of the Akademiya; Sumeru City was built on the Divine Tree. She also created the Aranara.

Thousands of years ago she returned to the desert to help when King Deshret's forbidden knowledge poisoned his people, created the Akasha to unite human wisdom against it, and spent so much power that she shrank to a child's stature. Five hundred years ago, in the cataclysm, forbidden knowledge contaminated the Irminsul and Rukkhadevata herself. Lesser Lord Kusanali succeeded her, the last lord of the forest in Viaghara's line died protecting the forest, and the Aranara withdrew to dreams as the people of Sumeru stopped dreaming. Old Vanarana had been the Aranara's home for hundreds of years before then.

More than 400 years ago the scholar Zandik studied at the Akademiya before the Fatui took him as the Harbinger Dottore. Roughly the same time, the Temple of Silence left the rainforest for the desert in protest at the sages' corruption. Faruzan, trapped for a century in a ruin of Deshret's civilisation, was found in the forest. Kaveh's first palace at Lokapala was destroyed overnight by the Withering at 70 per cent completion; the Forest Rangers quickly dispersed the Withering, but the buildings could not be saved.

In 6.6 (Song of the Welkin Moon, Acts IX-X) Irminsul stopped recording properly because of Dottore's meddling. Nahida and the sages evacuated the whole rainforest (Sumeru City, Lokapala Jungle, Avidya Forest, Ashavan Realm and Ardravi Valley) to Caravan Ribat and then on to Aaru Village; civilians who tried to return were driven mad by the anomaly near Yasna Monument and killed one another. Silver branches burst from the rainforest floor into a colossal Irminsul tree tied to Dottore. The people of Sumeru overloaded Irminsul through the Akasha, the Traveler and Wanderer infiltrated it via the Divine Tree, and Nahida burned the corrupted Irminsul with the Pyro Gnosis obtained from Mavuika, ending Dottore; the reconfigured Aaru took over Irminsul's role. Afterwards the rainforest's people returned and began rebuilding.

Atmosphere: Humid green light through giant leaves, rain on broad canopies, glowing mushrooms and petals at night, the murmur of rivers, bazaar bustle in the city. It feels alive and a little dreamlike; in places there is a quiet wrongness where the Withering has rotted the plants.

Mawtiyima's fluorescent fungi and the flower gardens of Pardis Dhyai give night scenes a glow, and the dream version of Vanarana changes the light entirely.

Dangers: The Withering: zones of decaying land with Fetid Boughs, Withering Branches and enemies that hit with Decay, which saps the party's strength and can kill. Fungi and Ruin Machines roam the woods, and hilichurls, Eremite bands, Treasure Hoarders and Fatui agents are found in the forest. The Rishboland Tiger, Spinocrocodiles and Shaggy Sumpter Beasts are real wildlife dangers.

The worst Withering zones are Old Vanarana and the cave in Mawtiyima Forest, where decay accumulates by itself. Eleazar, the Withering's manifestation in humans and once endemic to Sumeru, vanished after Nahida removed Rukkhadevata from Irminsul in Chapter III, but Withering Zones that already existed remain. Aeonblight Drakes, powerful boss-class monsters, are found in Ardravi Valley and around Devantaka Mountain.

Travel: The forest is reached from Liyue by a tunnel from the Chasm's Cinnabar Cliff, or by river and sea at Port Ormos. The river carries boats between Sumeru City and Port Ormos, and plant-based Four-Leaf Sigils let travellers cross difficult ground quickly. The Wall of Samiel and Caravan Ribat gate the road to the desert.

In the Apam Woods the Varuna Contraption can be operated, once its quest is done, to start or stop the rain and to lower the water for access. The Vintage Lyre plays Aranara songs that activate Silapna (including the dream/real switch for Vanarana) and open Gloomy Paths.

Quests: The Sumeru Archon Quest (Chapter III) begins here. Act I: the Traveler wakes in Gandharva Ville after a strange incense vision and meets Tighnari and Collei. Later acts take place in Sumeru City, the desert and Port Ormos. The Aranyaka series covers the Aranara; the Nursery of Lost Dreams quest unlocks the Lost Nursery and Old Vanarana.

Caribert (Act VI) is set around Port Ormos and has Dainsleif looking for a field in Avidya Forest where he once travelled with the Traveler's sibling. In Act V the sages' hold on the Akasha is broken. A Prayer for Rain on the Fecund Land lets the Traveler control the Apam Woods' rain.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Dharma Forest is recovering from the 6.6 Irminsul crisis: the whole rainforest was briefly evacuated, Irminsul was burned away and replaced by the reconfigured Aaru, and Dottore is dead. People have returned and are rebuilding under Nahida's guidance. Old Withering Zones have not gone away.

Collei is now an official Forest Ranger, and the Akademiya works under Naphis and a new council of sages. The 7.0 and 7.1 Archon Quest has moved to Snezhnaya, and no new rainforest areas have been added since.

After the crisis Pulcinella wrote to Nahida from Snezhnaya apologising for Dottore and sending relief supplies; Nahida and Naphis judged the letter diplomatically airtight and agreed to keep watch on Snezhnaya.

73.comment: Dharma Forest: Avidya Forest and Sumeru City
73.content:
Avidya Forest is the most populous part of Sumeru apart from Ardravi Valley and the first area the Traveler enters. Sumeru City, the "City of Wisdom", is built on a gigantic tree, the Divine Tree, with its Grand Bazaar, Zubayr Theater and Treasures Street below the Akademiya, which occupies the middle and upper part of the tree. On top is the Sanctuary of Surasthana, a treetop palace and the Archon's home. Gandharva Ville, the Rangers' outpost, lies in the forest nearby.

The name Avidya is Sanskrit for "unwisdom", the opposite of vidya (wisdom), a pointed name for the home of the Akademiya. Local flora include Padisarah and Rukkhashava mushrooms, and the forest is home to shroomboars and countless fungi.

74.content:
The Withering is a blight that causes Withering Zones where land and life decay. Within one the party gains Decay, reducing resistances and Max HP, and can fall if it reaches the limit. Dendrograna (Dendro-charged seeds) destroy its Withering Branches, and defeating the enemies from the Tumor of the Withering clears the zone. After clearing one in Chapter III, Tighnari voices concern at how quickly new zones are appearing and how they worsen Eleazar.

According to the lore recounted on Apep's page, Tumors of the Withering are the form Apep's elemental lifeforms take at the end of their lives because of the torment of forbidden knowledge. King Deshret's forbidden-knowledge disaster brought the Withering into being, and Eleazar is its manifestation in humans. Kusanali purged the forbidden knowledge in Chapter III, which left a void in Apep that the Traveler and Nahida later helped to heal.

75.content:
The Aranara are small, plant-like forest spirits created by Greater Lord Rukkhadevata (whom they called Queen Aranyani) to guard the forest. They hide from adult eyes but befriend children; they love memories, fear fire and salt, and when in grave danger turn to seed. Their homeland, Vanarana, exists both in reality and as a dream place, Mahavanaranapna. At life's end an Aranara grows into a Vasara Tree.

After the cataclysm the Aranara withdrew; they had lived beside humans before the people of Sumeru stopped dreaming. They hold that adults are those who have "grown up". The Fane of Ashvattha holds the first Vasara Tree, the progenitor of the Aranara. After Kusanali erased Rukkhadevata's memory from the Irminsul, the Aranara forgot Queen Aranyani and now regard the current Dendro Archon as the Lord of Verdure.

In the last war (the cataclysm) the Aranara crushed Marana's Avatar and imprisoned it deep in Old Vanarana with four seals, and Aramuhukunda became a Vasara Tree there to hold it down; in Nursery of Lost Dreams the Traveler and Arama destroy it. Three other Aranara of that era, Aramaha, Arayama and Araji, sealed the three Ashvattha's Concourses with their own rhythms and became Vasara Trees.

76.comment: Dharma Forest: Forest Rangers and Gandharva Ville
76.content:
The Forest Rangers (also called Vanara) are civil servants who protect the forests of Sumeru: they help travellers, suppress Withering Zones and monitor beast populations. Higher-ranking members are Forest Watchers and wear lighter green. Their main outpost, Gandharva Ville, is "the City Above the Forest". They send regular reports to the researchers of Pardis Dhyai, who supply seeds and nutrients in return.

Tighnari is Forest Watcher and Chief Officer, Amir trains search-and-rescue dogs, Ashpazi runs logistics and cooks, Shirin is the doctor and Collei is a Ranger. According to Rana, the earliest Rangers were royal guards of the forest king Viaghara.

77.comment: Dharma Forest: Port Ormos and the Ardravi
77.content:
Port Ormos is Sumeru's largest port and a hub for trade and travel, beneath two giant trees with a river running to Sumeru City. Parts of it are under Akademiya supervision, yet smuggling and illegal trade are more common here than in the city and prices are lower. Most long-term residents are traders and labourers who grew up there; Eremite mercenaries from several groups work here too, and students come to relax. Kaveh designed its arch bridge.

The Ardravi valley was formed by the erosion of the great river and is Sumeru's great waterborne mercantile route, kept pure by the Forest Watchers. Vimara Village, a quiet fishing town, lies on the river between the port and the city.

78.comment: Dharma Forest: Wall of Samiel and Caravan Ribat
78.content:
The Wall of Samiel separates the rainforest from the Great Red Sand, supposedly built by Greater Lord Rukkhadevata to keep sandstorms from ruining the forest. The Akademiya maintains it and forbids damaging it. Caravan Ribat, full of Eremites, is a fortified village at its foot and the checkpoint for travel to the desert and Aaru Village.

Official map text says the wall that stops the sandstorms has also blocked the spread of wisdom's blessing to the desert. After the Chapter III events Dehya notes the Akademiya has taken a kinder view of desert folk and hopes the Wall of Samiel will from now on mark only where the sandstorms end, not where her people's hopes and dreams end.

79.content: Per the wiki's tentative chronology, Greater Lord Rukkhadevata parted ways with King Deshret and Nabu Malikata and came to the east of the Great Red Sand. She created the Varuna Contraption to terraform part of the desert into rainforest, raised the Wall of Samiel and, after the forest labyrinth was made, Viaghara was born from the moon's reflection on the water in the shape of a tiger. Her followers founded the Amurta darshan, and the sages of the Akademiya helped her manage the nation. Viaghara's successors kept the title of lord of the forest; the last of them died defending the forest when the cataclysm struck, and the Rishboland Tigers have inherited the "tiger" name since.

80.content:
Djafar Tavern (also: Djafar Restaurant): Djafar Tavern is the main place to eat and drink in Port Ormos, Sumeru's big harbour. Its owner Eymen tends the bar, promising the best wine, food and service and treating every customer like family. Merchants, tourists, sailors and former Eremite mercenaries mix here. In the Archon Quest it is where Ayn Al-Ahmar members, devotees of King Deshret, sold false information to would-be buyers.

The staff are Eymen (bartender and owner) and two hostesses, Nesmil and Roshana, who both used to be Eremites.

People: Eymen: bartender and owner. He was a travelling merchant in the desert until he made enough money to open the place. Roshana says he does not want to offend customers and will try to meet any demand. Nesmil: cheerful hostess who talks up the tavern's wine and appetizers; a former Eremite mercenary who says she left them for the tavern because of Roshana, and that she enjoys more freedom here than she would freelancing for the Akademiya. Roshana: dry, unfussy hostess who does not make cocktails or wait on customers ("talk to the bartender"), another ex-Eremite who prefers this to dealing with stiff researchers. Other people seen here include the merchants Abbanes and Behrouz and the researcher Parisa; at night the Mahamata Mahshid and the Eremite mercenary Matari are also present.

Roshana jokes that a stronger drink is enough to make researchers drop their rules. Nesmil boasts of her mercenary past but admits sea monsters are too tough to punch, and says she could handle drunks easily. Eymen's idle thoughts wonder whether he should start something more profitable.

Quests: In Lost in Prosperity (Chapter III Act I), Akademiya students in Port Ormos say that the Eremite group Ayn Al-Ahmar likes to set up shop at Djafar Tavern and will sell information on anything for half a million Mora. The Traveler and Paimon go there and Eymen shows them to a table. Ayn Al-Ahmar men (Tariq and Tumart) talk openly about reclaiming King Deshret's power. Tariq takes 500,000 Mora and hands over an address, then explains the group's faith in King Deshret and their grievance against Greater Lord Rukkhadevata. Alhaitham interrupts and calls Tariq a fraud: the address is fake, and the group lures people with promises of information so they can squeeze them for money.

After completing that quest Eymen drops his pretence when the Traveler returns: he admits he helped the outlaws because Eremites looked after him in the desert, says he now has nothing to do with them, and offers wine or, failing that, a sword as an apology (the Traveler receives the sword Harbinger of Dawn). The tavern serves only as a meeting point in the story; the quest goes on elsewhere in the port.

Event: During the Sabzeruz Festival event Chromatic Ode of Candies and Roses, Nesmil offers Sabzeruz special sweet wine to customers, and the parade's Flower Carriage is kept near the tavern at the end of its route. Roshana points out that the carriage has nothing to do with the tavern, though many first-time tourists ask about it as if it did.

Atmosphere: Noisy and cosmopolitan: sailors and merchants from many lands, mercenaries off duty, and a bartender quick to make everyone feel welcome. Business of all sorts, including dubious business, is done at its tables.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Djafar Tavern is open and unchanged.

No story content after the Chapter III quest alters the tavern. Eymen is shown running it in later event dialogue too.

81.content: Eymen (owner, bartender), Nesmil (hostess) and Roshana (hostess) run the tavern. Nesmil and Roshana are former Eremite mercenaries; Eymen was a travelling desert merchant whom Eremites once looked after. Nesmil is fond of Roshana; Roshana is blunt and does not wait on tables.

82.content:
Duat Hall (also: The Bottomless Hall): Duat Hall is a vast underground hall in the Mausoleum of King Deshret, in Sumeru's Hypostyle Desert, whose floor falls away into a bottomless void. Its name is the ancient Egyptian realm of the dead, and the Scarlet Sand Slate describes it as the place where the guilty meet their fate.

It is the first stop of the trials in Dual Evidence and joins the Great Hall of Truths on its south side. A side chamber off its east side, the Place of Swallowing, holds one of the slate's clearance trials.

Geography: Reached through an underground teleport waypoint directly south of the Mausoleum. A door to it opens only with the Ferryman's Clearance, a permission the slate grants when Dual Evidence begins. The hall is connected to the Great Hall of Truths at its south end and to the Place of Swallowing off its east side.

Opet Hall to the north looks as if it joins the Great Hall of Truths, but that route cannot be used; travellers must come through Duat Hall instead.

History: After Soheil's dismissal in Aaru Village, the slate lights up and points to Duat Hall. On entering, the party finds new writing and three points of light. The text describes the mortal plane as a river between the underworld and Aaru that must not be crossed or coveted, and tells the reader to take a vulture's form, peck at three organs, win Al-Ahmar's consent and cross as a falcon. Paimon connects the three organs to the devices Tirzad found earlier.

The three points of light correspond to the Place of Rebirth, the Place of Breath and the Place of Swallowing; clearing each lights a sigil. Once all are lit the slate announces the Great Hall of Truths.

Atmosphere: A gaping dark hall, stone floors ending at nothing, the sound of shifting sand. Paimon warns the Traveler to stay away from the drop. It feels like a threshold between worlds.

Dangers: Falling into the void is the main hazard. In play, falling only returns the traveller to the entrance without penalty; the slate's lines about judging the guilty are symbolic.

Quests: Dual Evidence (Old Notes and New Friends, part 1). The Traveler enters here after Soheil's dismissal in Aaru Village.

Without Tirzad and Jebrael arguing over the slate's meaning, the party has to read it alone; Paimon remarks that it misses their bickering and wonders how many palaces King Deshret built.

Status as of 7.1: Open to explore as of Version 7.1.

No source up to Version 7.1 that I checked changes the hall.

83.content:
Dunes of Steel: The Dunes of Steel are a subarea of the Desert of Hadramaveth in Sumeru's Great Red Sand. Canon describes them only as the stretch of the desert that connects it to Old Vanarana, the former home of the Aranara.

They were added with the Desert of Hadramaveth in version 3.4. Nothing else about their history, inhabitants or purpose is stated.

Geography: Sand dunes at the edge of the Desert of Hadramaveth, on the side that leads toward Old Vanarana in the Dharma Forest's Lost Nursery. The wiki lists no points of interest, enemies or specialties for the subarea itself.

The Desert of Hadramaveth around it is a wide sandy basin cut by many ravines (its game description speaks of scimitar-shaped ravines hiding a lost city), crossed by sandstorms, and holds Setekh Wenut as its boss and a large number of interactable records and tablets.

Places: A Ruin Golem stands in the dunes, and beneath its original position lies the Radiant Spincrystal 88, an item that unlocks the "Kingdom of Dust" soundtrack for the Serenitea Pot.

History: Canon gives the dunes no history of their own. Their only stated role is as the link to Old Vanarana, which the Aranara called home for hundreds of years before the cataclysm and which stayed engulfed in the Withering until the Nursery of Lost Dreams quest.

Atmosphere: Open, wind-swept sand with no settlement in sight, where the desert gives way toward the old Aranara nursery. Treat details beyond that as scene-setting, not canon.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the dunes are an open part of the Desert of Hadramaveth.

Nothing after their 3.4 introduction has changed them.

84.comment: Dunes of Steel: Dunes of Steel
84.content:
The Dunes of Steel are the part of the Desert of Hadramaveth that connects the desert to Old Vanarana. Canon says nothing more about them; the wiki page is a stub.

The name has no in-world explanation in the sources read. When portraying travellers, do not invent steel deposits, tribes or ruins here; stay with sand, the Ruin Golem and the way toward Old Vanarana.

85.content:
Fane of Ashvattha: The Fane of Ashvattha is a sacred grove in Vissudha Field, Dharma Forest, that holds the Ashvattha Tree, the first Vasara Tree and the progenitor of the Aranara. It also acts as the seal over the entrance to Old Vanarana, the older, sealed Vanarana. In the Aranyaka quest series the Traveler and Arama come here to make the Bija that will heal Rana.

The tree was weakened by Marana and could not bear the Bija. Arama took its place and planted a new Ashvattha Tree, and the seal at the Fane opened so the party could descend toward Old Vanarana.

Geography: A hidden forest shrine in Vissudha Field, with the Ashvattha Tree at its center and a seal over the passage into Old Vanarana. The body of water over the entrance has to be drained in the quest before the way leads further in. The wiki notes that the area's name is not shown on the map until the quest For Fruits, Seeds, and Trees is done.

Rukkhashava mushrooms grow nearby as a local specialty. In the quest the Traveler can enter the Ashvattha Tree's dream by reaching toward it, and Arama places the Tree of Dreams within Sarva.

People: The Aranara hold it sacred. Arama, a friendly Aranara who guides the Traveler, says it is her first visit. The Ashvattha Tree is the oldest of the Vasara Trees, older than any Aranara and their stories, and all Aranara descend from it.

History: Arama's account is that the first Aranara, Aramuhukunda, sprouted from a seed in a pomegranate the Ashvattha Tree produced after a great singer of the forest called the tree out of Sarva. The tree did this so that the forest's children would grow and befriend the lonely Nara, humans. Later the Aranara spread like leaves on a tree. Aramuhukunda later became a Vasara Tree in Old Vanarana to hold back Marana's avatar, and the tree there withered.

After the older Vanarana was destroyed and Marana appeared, three Aranara, Araji, Aramaha and Arayama, sealed the three Ashvattha's Concourses and turned into Vasara Trees. In For Fruits, Seeds, and Trees the Traveler carries three Vasoma Fruits from those trees to the Ashvattha Tree to ask for the Bija. Marana had corroded even the Tree's dream, and the Withering was cleared from it. The tree could not bear a Bija. Arama says she will plant a new Ashvattha Tree, the tree giving her its power, and that the seal in the Fane hides Marana's avatar in Old Vanarana, which must be destroyed for the new tree to grow.

Arama comes out of the experience with new words, memories and a changed manner of speaking, but insists she is still herself. The new Ashvattha Tree grows inside the withered trunk of Aramuhukunda's Vasara Tree in Old Vanarana's Lost Nursery.

Status as of 7.1: The old Ashvattha Tree in the Fane is spent, though the place remains sacred to the Aranara, and the seal over Old Vanarana was opened in the quest.

The new Ashvattha Tree is Arama in Old Vanarana, so the Fane's tree is a memory of the first. No later change is recorded as of Version 7.1.

Atmosphere: Hushed, mossy and watched over, with the Aranara's quiet reverence. Nara who wear the Aranara's garland are treated as children of the forest while it lasts.

86.content: Vasara Trees hold dreams and memories and are usually made when an Aranara chooses to become one. They keep some consciousness, so other Aranara treat a tree as the Aranara it once was. The three Vasara Trees of Araji, Aramaha and Arayama, tended by the concourses, each bear a Vasoma Fruit once the Withering is cleared from their dreams. The Bija is obtained by offering such fruits to the Ashvattha Tree.

87.content:
Gandha Hill: Gandha Hill is a hill in the Avidya Forest of Sumeru's Dharma Forest, the lush rainforest of the north. It has no named settlement or landmark of its own and no stated history; it is simply a stretch of rainforest slope that travellers cross.

It was added with Sumeru in version 3.0. Treat it as a quiet corner of the forest rather than a destination.

Geography: Part of Avidya Forest, the green, populous eastern rainforest that also holds Sumeru City and the Forest Watchers' base at Gandharva Ville. The wiki lists no terrain features, points of interest or local specialties for the hill itself.

An in-game puzzle near the hill has a strange plant ringed by Pyro Slimes; when the puzzle is solved a drawing lights up and points in a certain direction, as Paimon remarks. This sits near the entrance of a domain used for the recurring Fayz Trials event.

People: No resident NPCs are recorded. The random event "Unscrupulous Dealings" can begin here: a group of Fatui and Eremites, which Paimon reads as an under-the-table deal, can be found haggling; around Gandha Hill and Chinvat Ravine the wiki lists Eremite crossbowmen, linebreakers and sword-dancers, Fatui Skirmishers and a sumpter beast.

Quests: Gandha Hill is one of the places where the "Hammer of the Mushrooms" daily commission (a mushroom-knocking challenge) and the "Unscrupulous Dealings" random event can start. Both are repeatable open-world activities, not story content.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 nothing is recorded as changing here.

Atmosphere: A rainforest hillside in the green Avidya Forest. The canon disturbances recorded here are Pyro Slimes around the puzzle plant and mercenary or Fatui parties met by chance; no other mood is described.

88.comment: Gandha Hill: Etymology of Gandha Hill
88.content: The wiki notes that "Gandha" may derive from Gandhamadana, the Fragrant Mountain where celestial gandharvas live in Indian religious tradition; the Chinese name means roughly Mesmerizing Fragrance Slope. This is an out-of-universe naming note, not stated by the game.

89.content:
Gandharva Ville (also: The City Above the Forest): Gandharva Ville, nicknamed the City Above the Forest, is the main outpost of Sumeru's Forest Rangers, set in the Avidya Forest. Travellers, merchants and adventurers frequent it. It is home to the Forest Watcher Tighnari and his student Collei, and it is where the Traveler recovers after a vision in Chapter III.

Its tone is quiet and caring. The Rangers here help travellers in need, keep watch over the forest's health and treat patients, and the village is where the early threads of Sumeru's Archon Quest begin.

Geography: The village stands above the forest floor in the Avidya Forest; official map text calls it "the city above the forest". Its local specialty is the Kalpalata Lotus, and Shaggy Sumpter Beasts wander near it.

From the village the Rangers set out on patrol routes through the forest, and Collei guides the Traveler along one in Chapter III.

Places: Ashpazi, a Forest Watcher who supervises logistics and is a master chef, serves as the village's vendor; Collei is cared for in the village when her illness flares.

The same map text reads: "The city of wisdom is ours, as is the forest of ignorance. Atop the tree lies the remnants of the kingdom of lost dreams."

People: Forest Watchers (higher-ranking Rangers) and Rangers include Tighnari (chief officer), Amir (who trains the search and rescue dogs), Shirin (doctor), Iraj, Kamran and Nasrin; Collei, long a trainee, was promoted to official Forest Ranger after the 6.6 crisis. Keon, Farbod and Umm are designated Vanara; Keon is a blind elder who greets travellers by their footsteps. Visitors and workers include researchers Hayyan and Rudaba, adventurer Philby, the merchant Darina and Eremite mercenaries Futuh, Tuman and Yohanan.

Sag leads the search and rescue dog team. Before the Akasha was shut down, Keon noted fewer Dusk Birds leaving Sumeru City as Akasha use grew and hoped it meant progress; afterwards he says even more birds sing in the forest.

Governance: The Forest Rangers run the village. They are civil servants who protect Sumeru's forests, help travellers and preserve the ecosystem, suppress Withering Zones and monitor beast populations.

They send regular reports about the Avidya Forest to researchers at Pardis Dhyai, who in turn supply seeds and nutrients for ecological support. The earliest Rangers were, according to the Ranger Rana, the forest king Viaghara's royal guards.

Culture: The Rangers are devoted to protecting the forest. Locals such as Keon once blessed travellers in the name of Greater Lord Rukkhadevata; since her erasure from Irminsul in Chapter III they credit every blessing to Lesser Lord Kusanali instead.
