They are wary of the Akademiya's recruiters, as when Tighnari refuses a top-secret project.

History: Little is known of the village's origin. In the story Collei is brought here by Cyno after the Black Fire incident in Mondstadt and becomes Tighnari's trainee. Tighnari's ancestors learned of the Withering and of Irminsul from aranara.

Collei calls Tighnari her master. She was born with Eleazar and later healed when Nahida removed the Greater Lord's presence from Irminsul, which cured the disease everywhere (see quests).

The name joins the Sanskrit gandharva with the French ville and echoes gandharvanagara, an illusory city that looks real from afar. The Chinese name draws on the Lotus Sutra's parable of the phantom city, a city conjured to let tired travellers rest before moving on to their true destination.

Atmosphere: A quiet, high-up outpost where Rangers in green clothes (higher ranks wear lighter green), search dogs and visiting travellers come and go; Keon counts the Dusk Birds that pass.

Dangers: Withering Zones in the surrounding forest, whose effects only those with elemental power can withstand; Eremites hired by Dottore in Chapter III; hostile wildlife such as Shaggy Sumpter Beasts.

Travel: Gandharva Ville is the Rangers' base in the Avidya Forest; the Traveler also reaches Pardis Dhyai from it, and the road through Dharma Forest leads on to Caravan Ribat and the desert.

Quests: In Chapter III Act I the Traveler wakes here after Haypasia's incense gave them a vision; Collei shows them around on patrol, and Tighnari explains the Withering and Irminsul. Khajeh and his Akademiya retinue visit to recruit Tighnari and are refused. In Act III Collei, barred from expeditions by a worsening Eleazar, is found here, and Tighnari has left for Pardis Dhyai.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Gandharva Ville remains the Forest Rangers' main outpost, with Tighnari and Collei (now an official Forest Ranger) based there.

Eleazar was wiped out after the Chapter III Archon Quest, curing Collei. In 6.6, during the Irminsul crisis, the whole rainforest including the village was evacuated to Caravan Ribat and then Aaru Village, with Tighnari, Collei and the Rangers helping defend the evacuees; after the crisis people returned and Collei was promoted to official Forest Ranger.

90.comment: Gandharva Ville: A Forest of Change and Further Observation
90.content:
After passing through the tunnel from Cinnabar Cliff, the Traveler and Paimon follow the scholar Haypasia into a cave, where her incense gives the Traveler a vision of a white tree under a red sky and a woman's voice saying "World... Forget me...". They wake in Gandharva Ville, where Tighnari and Collei treated them. Tighnari calls it a hallucination; suspecting a lie, the Traveler asks Collei and joins her patrol the next day.

On patrol Collei tells them there have been two Dendro Archons: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, who died in the cataclysm, and Lesser Lord Kusanali, who lives in Sumeru City. She knew who the Traveler was from letters from Amber. When Paimon touches her in jest, Collei panics and flees back to the village, ill.

91.content:
Collei was born with Eleazar, a disease endemic to Sumeru that causes slow, painful death. Dottore had once suppressed her symptoms through experiments that traumatised her and made her avoid touch. In Chronic Illness the Traveler and Tighnari gather medicine ingredients and clear a Withering Zone on a patrol route. After Nahida removes the Greater Lord's presence from Irminsul in the Archon Quest, Eleazar disappears and Collei recovers.

Dottore had kept her alive by infusing her with remains of the god Nabu Malikata. In 6.6 those remains let her command hostile Jinn at Aaru Village; afterwards, at Windrise, the Jinni Liloupar absorbed them from her and died at peace.

92.content: In Silent Seeker of Knowledge the Traveler and Paimon return to find Sage Khajeh and subordinates trying to recruit Tighnari into a top-secret Akademiya project. Even mention of disappointing his teacher, Sage Naphis, does not move him, and they leave empty-handed. Tighnari then tells the Traveler to meet Rohawi in Sumeru City.

key: The Gaze From a Certain God
93.comment: Gandharva Ville: Chapter III Act III at Gandharva Ville
93.content: On the way to the village the Traveler and Paimon repel an ambush by Eremites hired by Dottore. They find Collei, whose Eleazar has worsened and who is barred from expeditions. Tighnari has uncharacteristically left for Pardis Dhyai on short notice, so they follow him there.

94.content: Keon is a blind elder Vanara in Gandharva Ville who recognises people by their footsteps and says that travellers, merchants and adventurers are frequent. Before the Chapter III climax he worried that Akasha use was growing while fewer Dusk Birds flew from Sumeru City; afterwards he says more birds sing in the forest now the Akasha is shut down, believes things will improve under Lesser Lord Kusanali, and hopes to live to see her restore Sumeru's glory.

95.content:
Garden of Endless Pillars (also: Desert Vivarium): The Garden of Endless Pillars is a one-time domain in the Hypostyle Desert of Sumeru's Great Red Sand, west of the Dune of Carouses. It is the last surviving garden of Tulaytullah, the ancient "city of sapphire", once a palace-like place under thousands of giant pillars. The city is long gone; the garden endures and is now a paradise for fungi.

The domain's in-game text says that priests and the powerful once walked freely beneath the pillars, and that all that remains of the proud city is ruin. The white tree, Irminsul, and the ley lines are credited with keeping the garden alive through the centuries of desert wars.

Geography: A garden of broken pillars in the Hypostyle Desert, west of the Dune of Carouses. Within, ruined terraces are covered with oversized mushrooms and flowering plants. The domain has a single level, called Desert Vivarium; five Pyro monuments around its entrance must be lit in order before it opens. Dendro is recommended, and a Dendro character is needed to complete it.

Inside, bouncy mushrooms and platforms of living plant growth carry visitors up through the ruin toward the top, where the last fights take place. The challenge is mechanical rather than narrative: no story is told in the domain itself.

History: The garden is what is left of Tulaytullah, a city-state said to have risen from the tears of the goddess Nabu Malikata after the fall of her fellow Angels. After King Deshret's civilisation fell, the priest Hermanubis founded the original Temple of Silence there and made it a city of wisdom, with shimmering canals, sapphire-domed buildings and gardens of padisarah and pomegranate. The Temple's departure, wars with Gurabad's kings and later conquest by foreign Khagans ended its prominence; its decline was like that of the other desert kingdoms.

Refugees from Tulaytullah and other failing desert kingdoms later founded Aaru Village. See the Tulaytullah entry for the city's full history; this domain is only its surviving garden.

In the city's later history, Humayun of Tulaytullah briefly became king of kings, and after his death foreign Khagans conquered it; a young noble, Goudarz, later rose against them. These details come from desert inscriptions and weapon and artifact texts, not from the domain.

Dangers: Fungi of several kinds: floating and grounded Dendro fungi, whirling Cryo and Electro fungi, and Hydroshrooms. They drift between the pillars and ambush anyone crossing the ruin.

Atmosphere: Pale stone columns standing in a hot, quiet ruin; spore-light and soft, strange growth where a city once stood. The sense is of a place the desert forgot, preserved rather than destroyed.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the garden is unchanged: an accessible one-time domain. No later content has altered it.

96.content: Tulaytullah, the City of Sapphire, was a city-state of the Hypostyle Desert whose renown began when Hermanubis founded the original Temple of Silence there. When the Temple's members left after wars, the city lost its defenders and fell, like the other desert kingdoms. Its surviving garden is the Garden of Endless Pillars.

97.content:
Gate of Zulqarnain: The Gate of Zulqarnain is a gate-like ruin and cavern site in Gavireh Lajavard, part of Sumeru's Girdle of the Sands. An Iniquitous Baptist, a boss of the Abyss, is found here, and the underground Subterranean Defile hides one of the Great Songs of Khvarena sought in a world quest. The wiki ties its eight-pointed star motif to Khaenri'ah.

Nothing in canon says who built the Gate or what it was for. Its name echoes the Arabic Dhu al-Qarnayn, "two-horned".

Geography: Located in the Gavireh Lajavard area of the Girdle of the Sands, a region the Adventurers' Guild commission describes as the northern desert. The Gate stands at the surface; the Subterranean Defile is the cave beneath, where the Wenut sleeps.

It is one of the subareas of Gavireh Lajavard, which also holds the Temir Mountains, Tunigi Hollow and the Realm of Farakhkert, according to the archive's Girdle of the Sands entry.

Dangers: The Iniquitous Baptist, a normal boss of the Abyss family. It uses a combination of Cryo, Electro, Hydro and Pyro, whose mix rotates daily, and has extra limbs from "evolution" through the Abyss's power. Notes elsewhere remark that Abyssal power is little different from elemental items in practice.

The same enemy type has also appeared as the Fontainian Jakob Ingold and, as Haden, a swordsmanship teacher cursed during the cataclysm; neither is connected to this site in canon.

Quests: In the world quest series Khvarena of Good and Evil, the Order of Skeptics' sage Nasejuna sends the Traveler to find the Great Songs of Khvarena. The quest As the Khvarena's Light Shows: Dukkha starts at the Gate of Zulqarnain: one Great Song is in the cavern where the petrified Setekh Wenut sleeps. Nasejuna remarks that the song has little effect even near the Wenut, and concludes it affects only things related to the Abyss.

Nasejuna turns out to have plotted with the Abyss Order and, on obtaining the last Great Song, reveals a hatred of the Pari and tries to take the songs by force with the Abyss Herald Klingsor; the Traveler defeats them and they flee. That betrayal happens at the final ruins and not at the Gate, so a character here would not yet know of it.

Status as of 7.1: An open ruin and boss site, with no inhabitants beyond the Abyss creature. As of Version 7.1 nothing found changes it.

98.comment: Gate of Zulqarnain: Great Song of Khvarena at the Gate
98.content: The Great Songs of Khvarena hold great power, but only the Pari can obtain the Khvarena's approval and unleash it through a ritual. Three songs are to be gathered; the last lies in ruins elsewhere. The one at the Gate lies in the cave near the Setekh Wenut and is found in the quest Dukkha.

99.content:
Gavireh Lajavard: Gavireh Lajavard is the mountainous western stretch of the Girdle of the Sands, a forbidden-feeling region of Sumeru added in version 3.6. Its subareas include the Gate of Zulqarnain, the Temir Mountains, Tunigi Hollow and the buried Khaenri'ahn factory Hangeh Afrasiyab. Beneath it lie ruins of the lost nation of Khaenri'ah, and above it the Order of Skeptics keep watch.

The Girdle of the Sands is described officially as a forbidden realm beneath the desert where few have set foot, holding the ruins of an ancient civilisation, the legacy of the divine and a hidden lost Darshan. Gavireh Lajavard and the Realm of Farakhkert are the Girdle's two areas.

Geography: Rugged high ground. The Temir Mountains are the main passage between the Desert of Hadramaveth and the rest of the Girdle of the Sands, and the Gate of Zulqarnain stands among them. Tunigi Hollow is a deep hollow that leads down to the Harvisptokhm, and a locked Khaenri'ahn gate lies far below at Hangeh Afrasiyab.

Notable features include Fravashi Trees, Soul Bells, Kory drums, Bright Flame Altars, Sunyata Flowers, Nirodha Fruit and Khvarena Inscription Fragments. Local specialties are Mourning Flower and Trishiraite. The boss enemy is the Iniquitous Baptist, who is also met at the Gate of Zulqarnain.

Places: The Gate of Zulqarnain, whose name the wiki traces to Dhu al-Qarnayn, the figure who built a barrier against Gog and Magog. The Temir Mountains. Tunigi Hollow, the epicentre of the Abyssal contamination during the cataclysm. Hangeh Afrasiyab, an abandoned underground Khaenri'ahn factory for processing Azosite. Pyrrho's campsite, southwest of the waypoint into the Temir Mountains, and the Molten Iron Fortress domain.

Hangeh Afrasiyab's viewpoint is called the Forge of the Abandoned Foundry, and the sealed gate beyond is titled the Gate of Everlasting Mourning. The loading-screen text calls it a ruined Khaenri'ahn workshop that "might have other titles in their language".

In the underground ruins, the wiki records a proving-grounds chamber, a pipe room, a smelting furnace room and the room where Klingsor and Nasejuna are fought, each with documents lying around. Workshop notes tie the factory's Azosite alloys to the large Mechanical Wardens, the Ruin Golem class of machine.

People: Few live here. The Order of Skeptics hold an outpost behind the Statue of the Seven, where a note orders strict control of mountain passes to ensure a ceremony and plan can be completed. The Pari Sorush joins the Traveler, and the Pari live in the nearby Vourukasha Oasis.

The NPC Pyrrho camps near the waypoint into the Temir Mountains. The Fatui have camps in the region, the subject of the world quest Investigate the Fatui Camps Marked by Sosi.

History: Tunigi Hollow was the epicentre of the Abyssal and forbidden-knowledge pollution that spread from Khaenri'ah during the cataclysm. Several gods, including Greater Lord Rukkhadevata and Egeria, came to suppress the defilement seeping from the godless nation below. Hangeh Afrasiyab, a Khaenri'ahn factory for refining Azosite, remains sealed above the lost kingdom.

Documents in the ruins describe Khaenri'ah's last days: a workshop notes an Azosite alloy intended to power the large Mechanical Wardens and expresses a hope of a "perpetual machine" built through human ingenuity rather than dogma from beyond the heavens; a bulletin notes that Knight Marshal Anfortas would act as Regent of the Regnum Concilium Ultimum while King Irmin was indisposed; a Schwanenritter commander, Hadura, orders the Wardens activated and survivors evacuated; and a journal says most people fled to the surface with the Schwanenritter, leaving a few hiding below, with rumours that those who fled above became monsters.

A monument inscription revealed in Monumental Study says that with Amrita and Khvarena the ancients extinguished phantoms mirroring the bedeviled sky, thanked the protection of the Dahri, and warned later generations not to fall to decadence. Another note attributed to an unknown hand argues that Khvarena and the Abyss belong to the same order of rules, both able to rewrite them, and that their users are all stuck in an unconscious stage of being overwritten.

Dangers: Abyssal and Fatui forces, the Iniquitous Baptist, hilichurls (including Hydro rogues), Thundercraven and Rockfond Rifthound whelps, fungi, and the remnants of Khaenri'ahn defences. Tunigi Hollow's defilement is a danger until it is cleansed.

Travel: The Temir Mountains connect the area to the Desert of Hadramaveth. The Order of Skeptics control the mountain passes. Tunigi Hollow provides the way down to the Harvisptokhm, and after the Rite of Chinvat jumping into it sends the player there.

Quests: The Splendorous Sky That Day, Asipattravana Itihasa, The Hymn of Tir Yazad (Parts 1 and 2), As the Khvarena's Light Shows and its Dukkha chapter, Monumental Study, Pale Fire, Awakening's Real Sound, Lightcall Resonance, The Recollector's Path and Investigate the Fatui Camps Marked by Sosi. These form the Khvarena of Good and Evil storyline, treated in the Vourukasha Oasis entity.

Atmosphere: Austere, mountainous and heavy with history, with Skeptic watchposts above and silent factories below.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the region is calmer and its worst defilement cleansed, with the Khaenri'ahn ruins still sealed or silent.

The Sign of Apaosha was extinguished in The Hymn of Tir Yazad (Part 2); nothing from 6.x or 7.0-7.1 changes the area.

100.content: An abandoned underground Khaenri'ahn factory for processing Azosite, with a sealed gate to the lost kingdom within. A Great Song of Khvarena is retrieved here in As the Khvarena's Light Shows by the Traveler, Paimon, Sorush and Nasejuna.

101.content: The epicentre of Abyssal and forbidden-knowledge pollution during the cataclysm; several gods, among them Greater Lord Rukkhadevata and Egeria, came to suppress the defilement. After the Rite of Chinvat, jumping into the hollow takes the player to the Harvisptokhm.

102.content:
Girdle of the Sands: The Girdle of the Sands is a remote desert subregion in the northwest of Sumeru, beyond the Temir Mountains. Here, during the cataclysm 500 years ago, Abyssal monsters poured up through a rift from the ruined kingdom of Khaenri'ah below, and the former Hydro Archon Egeria was slain there fighting them. Her remains became the Amrita, a sea of pure dew in the Vourukasha Oasis, where the Pari, flower-like bird spirits born of the divine bird Simurgh's Khvarena, still stand guard. Its two areas are Gavireh Lajavard and the Realm of Farakhkert.

It is an old war zone that never fully healed, a place of rock, swamps and sealed ruins. Travellers find the Order of Skeptics, a small band of scholars descended from rainforest Akademiya researchers, camped near the Temir Mountains.

Geography: Gavireh Lajavard ("azure desert") holds the Gate of Zulqarnain, the Temir Mountains (the main passage from the Desert of Hadramaveth) and Tunigi Hollow. The Realm of Farakhkert holds the Asipattravana Swamp, the Hills of Barsom, the Samudra Coast (the far northwest border of the Sumeru desert, with sandy beaches and clear blue water) and the Vourukasha Oasis at its heart. After the Mondstadt Prologue's final act, a Teleport Waypoint here, meant to give quick access to Fontaine, can also serve as quick access to the Sumeru desert.

The name Gavireh Lajavard comes from Persian words for "desert" and "lapis lazuli"; Farakhkert is the Middle Persian name of the cosmic sea Vourukasha. Below Tunigi Hollow lie Khaenri'ahn ruins, including the abandoned factory Hangeh Afrasiyab, which contains a sealed gate to the lost nation itself.

Places: Tunigi Hollow is the Abyssal rift opened by the cataclysm and sealed by the Harvisptokhm. Vourukasha Oasis is the Pari's homeland, with a sea of Amrita and, at its centre, the great tree Harvisptokhm. The Asipattravana Swamp lies in a thorn-filled canyon just north of the Oasis and is guarded by the Pari Mihir. The Hills of Barsom are home to a huge pine with pink foliage, the Barsom, and its familiar, the Pari Rashnu.

Hangeh Afrasiyab was the last factory in Khaenri'ah to use an entirely Azosite-powered system. Notes in the ruins mention Knight Marshal Anfortas taking the regency over the Regnum Concilium Ultimum, and a Schwanenritter garrison commander named Hadura ordering survivors evacuated. Hastily scrawled notes at a camp in Gavireh Lajavard guess that Khvarena and the Abyss are of the same order, both able to "re-write the rules".

People: The Pari are a sentient form of Khvarena in avian, flower-like bodies, each with a fated duty they carry out alone. Zurvan is the First Pari and elder; Sorush, Mihir and Rashnu are others. The Order of Skeptics, also called Shamaniyya or the Nagarjunites, is a small group of scholars (Pyrrho and Sosi among them) descended from rainforest researchers.

Humans who bond with a Pari are called Yasnapati and the bond is Laupa. Pari rejected by the Oasis after Abyssal taint turn into Fravashi Trees, and their Yasnapati are meant to bring them home. At life's end a Pari becomes a Plume of Purifying Light to be returned to the Amrita Pool.

Governance: No settled government. Zurvan, the eldest Pari, decides who enters the Oasis. She sealed it with the Great Songs of Khvarena after the Abyss attacked, and says only heroes who have formed bonds with Pari and pilgrims who wish to worship Egeria may enter. The Order of Skeptics keeps its own leader, a Nasuraia or Vijnanapati, but its last holder defected.

Culture: The Order of Skeptics holds that knowledge must be transmitted at all costs and that conflict is the natural order of Teyvat. Its ritual music, the Korybantes and Kory Drums, was once believed to be needed to bond with the Pari. The Pari use flower-themed endearments such as "good petal".

In practice Rashnu found the Skeptics' drum ceremony too noisy and tossed the drums away herself, so the bond may never have depended on them.

History: Long ago the goddess Nabu Malikata foresaw the cataclysm, made a shard of Khvarena and entrusted it to Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, who shaped it into the divine bird Simurgh. When the cataclysm came, the monsters' horde and the pollution of forbidden knowledge flowed from Khaenri'ah through Tunigi Hollow; Egeria and other gods went to suppress it, and she died there. Her body became the Amrita; Rukkhadevata grew the Harvisptokhm from it, and Simurgh sacrificed herself in the Amrita, shattering into countless Khvarena that became the Pari.

Zurvan, the first Pari, found a wounded Dainsleif and brought him to the Oasis; with scholars from the rainforest, led by a one-armed sage, they found a way into the Harvisptokhm and performed a rite that purified the land and made new Pari. Zurvan fused the strongest Khvarena into five Great Songs, scattered four and hid the fifth in the Oasis. Dainsleif left with the Traveler's sibling; some scholars stayed and became the Order of Skeptics. The Schwanenritter evacuated Khaenri'ahn refugees and used Ruin Golems against the Abyss, winning the title "heroes of Dahri".

Centuries later an Akademiya team came to explore the Dahrian ruins despite the Skeptics' warning. Klingsor, a Skeptic descended from the Schwanenritter Hadura, accompanied them, embraced the Abyss and became an Abyss Herald; Abyssal attacks then forced Zurvan to seal the Oasis and the ruins with the Great Songs. The Skeptics lost their archives to fire and let their duty to the Harvisptokhm lapse. The Oceanids, created by Egeria, came to Tunigi Hollow looking for their master, found only the tree and scattered.

Atmosphere: Bleak rock under a hard sky, canyons and thorn thickets, purple Abyssal mist where the defilement lingers, and then the contrast of the Oasis, where the Harvisptokhm now carries a glowing blue canopy. Underground, silent Khaenri'ahn machine halls and factories.

Dangers: Abyssal defilement (purple mist, gray crystals and Defiled Beacons), Abyss Heralds, the Iniquitous Baptist, Consecrated Fanged Beasts and Horned Crocodiles, rifthounds, Fatui skirmishers and hilichurls (including those corrupted by Abyssal energy).

The ruins beneath Tunigi Hollow hold monsters and Ruin Golems; Klingsor and Nasejuna were fought in a Khaenri'ahn factory. Pari that fall to Abyssal taint turn into Fravashi Trees.

Travel: Enter by the Temir Mountains from the Desert of Hadramaveth, or by the Teleport Waypoint described above. The Oasis admits only those the Pari accept. Flying as Sorush and channelling her Khvarena lets the Traveler suppress Gray Crystal barriers and deal with Fravashi Trees and Defiled Beacons, and the Yasnapati bond grants access.

Quests: The Khvarena of Good and Evil world quest series (3.6) unfolds here: The Splendorous Sky That Day, Awakening's Real Sound, Asipattravana Itihasa, As the Khvarena's Light Shows, and The Hymn of Tir Yazad (Parts 1 and 2). The Traveler becomes Sorush's Yasnapati, helps her gather the Great Songs of Khvarena, learns that Nasejuna and Klingsor sought to break the Harvisptokhm's seal and cleanse the Sign of Apaosha, and completes the Rite of Chinvat and Rite of Ab-Zohr.

Each stage: finding Pari Mihir (Asipattravana Swamp) and Rashnu (Hills of Barsom, the Kory Drum ritual), collecting five Great Songs with Nasejuna, defeating him and an Abyss Herald, placing the songs in Tunigi Hollow, then cleansing the Harvisptokhm. Zurvan tells of the cataclysm and says she hopes the Traveler will greet the masked swordsman, Dainsleif, on her behalf.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Sign of Apaosha has vanished and the Harvisptokhm has regrown a glowing blue canopy. The Pari still guard the Oasis, which stays closed to strangers. Nasejuna has fled and the Order of Skeptics has no leader.

No version up to 7.1 adds new areas here; Sorush does appear in the 6.6 Archon Quest, bringing Aranara to the Traveler during Sumeru's Irminsul crisis. Zurvan asked the Traveler to give her greetings to Dainsleif. The Harvisptokhm is purified, but the Abyss's interest in the Great Songs and the open question of the Skeptics' future remain.

103.content:
The Pari are avian, flower-like beings descended from Simurgh, created when her Khvarena combined with the Amrita. They are the only sentient form of Khvarena. Each has a fated task to undertake alone; many live only to serve it. They believe their god is Egeria, whose consciousness lies in the Harvisptokhm. They fought in the cataclysm with Khaenri'ahn warriors, a masked sword-wielder and a one-armed sage, and Akademiya scholars. Their human partners are called Yasnapati.

Pari tainted by Abyssal corruption are rejected by the Oasis and become Fravashi Trees. Sunyata flowers and Farrwicks are also descendants of Simurgh's Khvarena.

104.comment: Girdle of the Sands: Vourukasha Oasis and the Harvisptokhm
104.content:
Vourukasha Oasis holds the Amrita, a sea of pure dew made from the remains of Egeria, the Hydro Archon who ruled Fontaine for about 1,500 years and died at Tunigi Hollow in the cataclysm. Rukkhadevata grew the Harvisptokhm, a giant tree, from the Amrita to anchor Egeria's consciousness and let her absorb the defilement from the rift. Inside lies the lotus Gaokerena, where the Pari god's consciousness slumbers. Before the 3.6 quest the tree was a withered stump under the Sign of Apaosha; afterwards it has a glowing blue canopy.

Zurvan sealed the Oasis with the Great Songs of Khvarena. The Oceanids, Egeria's creations, came searching for their master, did not accept her successor Focalors, and scattered; pilgrims following their trail later established the Purification Spring.

105.comment: Girdle of the Sands: Order of Skeptics
105.content:
The Order of Skeptics, once a branch of the Akademiya, descends from scholars led by the one-armed sage Nagarjuna who came to help the Pari defeat the Abyss. They settled in the Girdle and forged bonds with the Pari. The Akademiya calls them Nagarjunites. After a disastrous Akademiya expedition into Khaenri'ahn ruins and the loss of their archives, they neglected their duty. Members included Pyrrho, Sosi, Aryadeva (who moved to Sumeru City) and Nagahvaya (now in the Temple of Space).

Nasejuna, the last Vijnanapati, was manipulated by Klingsor into believing the Skeptics' history was myth; he pretended to serve Sorush, aiming to break the seal so the Abyss could cover Teyvat, and fled when defeated. Kaveh's father once asked to join an investigation to find the Order.

106.comment: Girdle of the Sands: Tunigi Hollow and the Khaenri'ahn Ruins
106.content: Tunigi Hollow was the epicentre of Abyssal monsters and forbidden-knowledge pollution during the cataclysm; Rukkhadevata and Egeria went to suppress it. The monsters tore a great rift, which the Harvisptokhm later sealed; the Sign of Apaosha appeared above it while defilement remained. Below are Khaenri'ahn workshops, with notes on Azosite smelting, the Regent, and civilians who fled. A sealed gate to Khaenri'ah lies in the depths of Hangeh Afrasiyab, whose viewpoint is named "Gate of Everlasting Mourning". "Dahri" is the name desert texts and the Skeptics use for Khaenri'ah.

107.comment: Girdle of the Sands: Simurgh and the Great Songs of Khvarena
107.content:
Khvarena is an energy created by Nabu Malikata to oppose the cataclysm; it can purify Abyssal energy and forbidden knowledge. Simurgh was a shard of it; when Egeria's Amrita started to be corrupted she flew into the pool and shattered into countless motes. Zurvan fused the strongest Khvarena into five Great Songs. The Sign of Apaosha is a phenomenon in the sky above Tunigi Hollow, a reflection of the Abyss that corrupts the land beneath it.

Nasejuna argued that the Sign was a reflection of the "reality" beyond Teyvat's skies, and that the Great Songs could unleash it on the world; the Great Songs can only be retrieved by a Pari.

108.content:
Grand Bazaar: The Grand Bazaar is the market quarter of Sumeru City, a lively, artistic place crowded with merchants selling handmade goods. Its people are mostly ordinary folk who want a steady life rather than scholars or sages. The Zubayr Theater, Nilou's troupe, sits inside it.

It has three entrances from the rest of Sumeru City. It is where everyday Sumeru life, craft, music and dance meet, away from the scholarly world of the Akademiya.

Places: The Zubayr Theater is the Bazaar's best-known landmark, a small theater run by the playwright Sheikh Zubayr. Around it are stalls for woven goods, vases and jars, spices, toys and blankets. Treasures Street, Lambad's Tavern and the Citadel of Regzar belong to other parts of Sumeru City rather than the Bazaar itself.

People: Stallholders and passers-by fill the market: Shevirme (stall vendor), Sulaykha (blanket shop owner), Hushang (toy seller), Jut (spice merchant), Afshin (traveling merchant), Farhad (porter) and the wealthy businessman Bhabha by day. Mercenaries of the Corps of Thirty (Azra, Sahar, Taher) keep order.

The Zubayr Theater's own people also work here: the juggler Kourosh, the props engineer Najia and the manager Sheikh Zubayr, alongside Nilou. A researcher, Zohreh, is found here by day, and the NPCs Kumari, Swoof and Yusuf round out the crowd.

Atmosphere: Bustling, colourful and noisy: the Traveler's voice-over line has Paimon marvelling that the residents all seem so talented, selling woven goods, vases and fragrant spices and singing and dancing very well. It feels like a place where anyone might burst into a song or a dance.

Quests: Nilou's Story Quest "To the Wise" (Lotos Somno Chapter Act I) opens at dawn in the Bazaar. The Archon Quest "As by a God's Side" ends with the Traveler waiting for the agreed evening time and then going to the Bazaar, and later Nilou, back at the Bazaar, tells the Traveler she has sent invitations to several friends (Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises). These are Sumeru Archon Quest (3.0) events; avoid them for characters who have not witnessed them.

Nilou's story quest and the Archon Quest both revolve around an evening play and banquet at the Bazaar, so a scene set around them should treat the Bazaar as busy with preparations rather than as a plain market.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Bazaar is an ordinary working market, with no later event recorded in the pages consulted that changes it.

109.comment: Grand Bazaar: Zubayr Theater in the Bazaar
109.content: The Zubayr Theater is housed in a hollow of the great tree and is the stage on which Nilou dances. Its manager, playwright and director is Sheikh Zubayr. See the theater's own entry for detail.

110.content:
Great Hall of Truths (also: Hall of Great Truths): The Great Hall of Truths is a chamber inside the Mausoleum of King Deshret in Sumeru's Hypostyle Desert, joined to the bottomless Duat Hall on its south side. In the quest Dual Evidence the Traveler and Paimon reach it by following the Scarlet Sand Slate, and its giant central device carries them up to Aaru's Shut at the summit.

The slate describes it as the place where those who bring praises before King Deshret, show wisdom and do not fear the darkness may obtain unique gifts. In practice it is the last stage of a trial laid out in imagery of birds, rivers and sacred flame.

Geography: Part of the Mausoleum complex under the Hypostyle Desert. It is connected to Duat Hall at its south side; Duat Hall is entered through an underground waypoint directly south of the Mausoleum and needs the Ferryman's Clearance from the Scarlet Sand Slate. The central section opens onto the way up to Aaru's Shut once Dual Evidence has been completed.

Inside is one great device in the middle of the hall, surrounded by four plinths of the secret rites. Beyond a portal that opens when the plinths are operated lies a second chamber with another huge device and three places for sacred torches.

History: In the quest the Scarlet Sand Slate tells the party to prove itself in three ways: pass the river as a falcon, peck three organs, and burn the embers of the sun at three places with feathers. The trial halls Place of Rebirth, Place of Breath and Place of Swallowing each light a sigil on the slate; once all are lit the Great Hall of Truths appears. The Vahumana researcher Soheil had mocked Tirzad's paper on the Mausoleum, and the party's aim is to prove the paper true.

Operating the four plinths opens a portal, and the slate declares that the king's consent has been won and Aaru reached. Paimon is unimpressed, since the place holds only a huge device, and a new line appears on the slate: burn the embers of the sun at three places. Lighting three primal torches wakes the device. It lifts the party on an elevator to the top of the Mausoleum, where a guardian waits.

Atmosphere: A cold, vast chamber of sand-worn stone and monumental machinery. The hall feels both ceremonial and mechanical, like a throne room built to weigh visitors rather than welcome them. Paimon compares it to Stormterror's Lair in the desert.

Dangers: At the top of the elevator the party must defeat a Primal Construct, a guardian construct billed as Field Annihilation Array: The Evincing Shadow. A fall into the nearby Duat Hall's void only sends a traveller back to the entrance.

Quests: The hall is the centre of Dual Evidence, the first quest in the world quest series Old Notes and New Friends, begun at Aaru Village after Golden Slumber is done. The quest grants the achievements Walk Like King Deshret's People, The Straight Path and The Path To Enlightenment for the successive stages.

Afterwards the party returns to Aaru Village with a stone slate recovered from the summit. Soheil, once dismissive, apologises on behalf of his family and wants to study it, noting that records of the later period of Al-Ahmar's civilisation are mostly fragments. Hulwani refuses to escort researchers into the desert because the sage has forbidden entry without his permission.

Clearance on the slate is graded: the Ferryman's Clearance opens Duat Hall, and a fourth clearance found in the Place of Swallowing within Duat Hall opens all chambers in the Great Red Sand, so the hall sits at the end of a ladder of permissions. The slate's wording about the river between the mortal plane and Aaru, vulture and falcon forms and the consent of Al-Ahmar is the key to reading the whole sequence. Tirzad, whose paper Soheil had doubted, is not with the party on the climb; the Traveler and Paimon bring back proof for Soheil afterwards.

Status as of 7.1: Open to exploration. The cyclone that long crowned the Mausoleum is off for good after Dual Evidence, and Aaru's Shut can be visited through the hall's centre.

Nothing found in the sources up to Version 7.1 changes the hall or reveals more of its original purpose.

111.comment: Great Hall of Truths: Dual Evidence and the Ascent
111.content: Dual Evidence has the Traveler follow the Scarlet Sand Slate through Duat Hall and the three trial halls, then use the Great Hall of Truths to climb to Aaru's Shut. The Mausoleum's long-running cyclone stops for good, the summit is changed, and the party brings back a slate as proof for Soheil.

112.content:
Great Red Sand (also: Deshret Desert): The Great Red Sand, also called the Deshret Desert, is the vast desert of western Sumeru. Once the realm of King Deshret, Lord of Deserts, it is now a sea of dunes dotted with buried temples, ruined cities, oases and hidden machine halls. The Eremite tribes, descendants of his people, wander here, and Aaru Village keeps his memory. Beyond the Wall of Samiel on the east lies the rainforest of the Dharma Forest. Sandstorms, Ruin Golems and the old Jinn legends make it dangerous and rich in secrets.

Its four main areas are the Hypostyle Desert, the Land of Lower Setekh, the Land of Upper Setekh and the Desert of Hadramaveth. The nation's wisdom-seeking scholars have long coveted its ruins, while the desert folk remember it as a lost kingdom.

Geography: Four areas make up the subregion. The Hypostyle Desert holds Khemenu Temple, Sobek Oasis, three named dunes and the Mausoleum of King Deshret. The Land of Lower Setekh holds Aaru Village and Khaj-Nisut; the Land of Upper Setekh holds the Valley of Dahri. The Desert of Hadramaveth, the largest area, stretches west of them and holds the old city of Gurabad, the Tanit Camps and Mt. Damavand. The east is bounded by the Wall of Samiel, with Caravan Ribat at its foot.

Hypostyle Desert subareas include Khemenu Temple, Sobek Oasis, the Dune of Carouses, the Dune of Elusion, the Dune of Magma and the Mausoleum of King Deshret; Lower Setekh includes Aaru Village, Abdju Pit, Dar al-Shifa and Khaj-Nisut; Upper Setekh includes the Valley of Dahri. The Desert of Hadramaveth has eleven subareas, the most of any area: Debris of Panjvahe, Dunes of Steel (which links it to Old Vanarana), Mt. Damavand, the Passage of Ghouls, Qusayr Al-Inkhida', Safhe Shatranj, the Tanit Camps, the Sands of Al-Azif, the Sands of Three Canals, Wadi Al-Majuj and the Wounded Shin Valley. Upper Setekh is named for lying toward the sun at noon.

Places: Aaru Village is the largest human settlement in the desert and houses followers and descendants of King Deshret as well as exiled Akademiya scholars. The Mausoleum of King Deshret is a giant pyramid that is only one corner of a palace with many more temples beneath; a great cyclone long wheeled above it, shut off after the quest "Dual Evidence". Khemenu Temple is an underground temple "intimately linked to the people" where all bowed to Deshret's wisdom. Khaj-Nisut, once called the Eye of the Sands, holds Deshret's throne room. The Valley of Dahri holds a giant Ruin Golem and Akademiya investigation notes; Dar al-Shifa, now abandoned, was a hospital for Eleazar patients.

The Tanit Camps stood in the depths of Deshret Desert amid the ruins of Gurabad. Mt. Damavand, where a massive tornado whirls round the centre, is where Apep resides; its name is said to mean "the mountain from which smoke and ash arise" in the lost desert tongue. Thamud Oasis is where the electrum city of Saleh once stood. The Sands of Al-Azif are a flat region of wenut and the Wenut Tunnels. Safhe Shatranj is called the Great Rift by the Tanit, has a viewpoint named "The Palace Abandoned by the Gods", and was named The Temples Forsaken before its quest.

People: The Eremites are the desert's mercenaries, descended from the vanished civilisations. They fall into many tribes and factions, each with its own code, bound by stories passed down orally and by dance and sword traditions inherited from Deshret's age. Aaru Village's people and its Guardian, Candace, are spoken of as his descendants; Dehya and Cyno also have ties here.

The Tanit, a matrilineal tribe led by a Matriarch and Nine Elders who believed in the Goddess of Flowers, lived at the Tanit Camps and valued words and knowledge, trading crocodile goods, spices and oils. After the Hadramaveth events in 3.4 the Tanit were destroyed (see Tanit sub-entry). Vahumana researcher Tanjiyy later arrived to offer education aid and found the camps empty. Rukh Shah appoints consultants to ease disputes between Eremite groups.

Governance: Nobody governs the desert as a whole. Each Eremite tribe has its own leaders and law; Aaru Village is led by its chief, Uncle Anpu, and protected by its Guardian, Candace; its "Village Keepers", such as Khalil, are exiled Akademiya scholars whom the village shelters. The Akademiya in the rainforest maintains the Wall of Samiel. Dehya charges that the sages used the wall to keep the Eremites out of Sumeru and treated the desert folk as tools, undeserving of the Akasha's wisdom.

After the Chapter III Archon Quest events the Akademiya's grip loosened. A Tanit merchant's letter, found after Act V, hopes for easier trade and says banned books are being released; the General Mahamatra Cyno is to oversee education aid.

Culture: The Eremites honour Deshret's art of archery and sword-dancing, the latter now an art as well as a combat style; Eremite weapons can host fragments of ancient desert spirits that awaken in peril. Desert people value oral history; the Tanit in particular prized books smuggled from the Akademiya library. A saying traced to the Eremites describes someone who "isn't afraid of dying so that they might truly live".

The sun-and-eye emblem of Deshret appears throughout desert architecture. The eye symbol is a light-blue eye in the middle of a dark ten-pointed sun. Legends of the thousand and one Jinn, Deshret's servants, and of the magic bottle form a folk mythology.

History: Long ago the desert was the domain of the gods Nabu Malikata, Greater Lord Rukkhadevata and King Deshret, the Three Eternal Companion-Gods; Deshret and Nabu Malikata had earlier built the city of Ay-Khanoum together. Nabu Malikata died, and Rukkhadevata left to build a rainforest civilisation while Deshret kept the desert. He pursued a dream paradise through forbidden knowledge until the knowledge ruined his people, brought the Withering and drove him to sacrifice his life. His vassal city Gurabad had already fallen, destroyed by the Jinni Liloupar's revenge.

Deshret made a deal with the Dendro Dragon Apep, who would consume his body after his death. With Nabu Malikata gone he built the Eternal Oasis as her cemetery, and later created Aaru, a culmination meant to protect his people from age and decay. When the disaster came, Rukkhadevata returned to help and had priests build temples with the power of life to mitigate it, but only Deshret's sacrifice ended it. His civilisation splintered into city-states ruled by humans.

Gurabad was founded by the shepherd Ormazd with the help of Liloupar; her plan against him unfolded across three generations: Ormazd and his children were poisoned, Parvezravan (Kisra) took the throne, and her grandson Shiruyeh's Brass Mask revolt let her sink most of the city into an abyss by Abyssal power. Deshret punished Liloupar by splitting her soul into seven parts given to his seven sages. Later kingdoms (Saleb Dowleh, Muzaffar, Tulaytullah and others) built new Gurabads and sank into the sand; the Old Blind Poet and others finally retreated to Aaru to await Deshret's return. About 400 years ago the Temple of Silence left the rainforest for a large underground temple near Thamud Oasis. Around 20 years ago Kaveh's father, an Akademiya scholar, died in the desert after running into quicksand.

Atmosphere: A scorching, sand-scoured expanse where the wind builds and erases dunes, gold-red light, silent stone gates and vast temples half buried in sand. Aaru Village's refugee shelters are crowded and neighbourly; the temples feel solemn and watchful.

Dangers: Sandstorms in the Desert of Hadramaveth, atmospheric vortices, tumbleweed, loose sand piles that hide enemies, and wenut such as the Setekh Wenut. Ancient devices protect the ruins: Primal Constructs, Ruin Golems, Primal Beams and barriers that need clearance from the Scarlet Sand Slate. Eremite bands, Treasure Hoarders, hilichurls (called Majuj in the desert), Fatui and Abyss remnants also roam. Eleazar and forbidden knowledge are quiet dangers near old Deshret sites.

Algorithm of Semi-Intransient Matrix of Overseer Network guards the Dune of Elusion. Jinn shrines allow the Jinni in the Magic Bottle to dispel vortices or call and calm sandstorms once upgraded.

Travel: Most travellers enter from Caravan Ribat through the Wall of Samiel, or from Aaru Village; waypoints and Sobek Oasis serve as rest stops. Wadi Al-Majuj and the Temir Mountains lead on to the Girdle of the Sands. Sumeru City is reached through Caravan Ribat and the rainforest.

Four-Leaf Sigils work in the desert too, and Anemo can disperse loose sand. The Magic Bottle jinni predicts approaching sandstorms.

Quests: Chapter III Act IV, "King Deshret and the Three Magi", takes the Traveler, Cyno and Dehya to Aaru Village and Caravan Ribat investigating missing Village Keepers and a false claim that King Deshret is resurrected; Act V gathers the desert allies. Desert world quests such as "Secret of the Scorching Desert" and the Hadramaveth series (3.4: "Wisdom Has Built Her House, She Has Hewn Out Her Seven Pillars", "The Dirge of Bilqis") expand the story of Deshret's kingdom, Gurabad and the Tanit, and "Homecoming" (3.6) brings the Traveler to Apep at Mt. Damavand. In 6.6 the Archon Quest returns: "As All Falls to Emptiness" (Song of the Welkin Moon Act IX) and "Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana" (Act X) move Sumeru's people into the desert, reawaken Liloupar at Safhe Shatranj, and open Aaru from the Mausoleum to take over from Irminsul.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Great Red Sand has come through the Irminsul crisis of the 6.6 Archon Quest. During it the rainforest's people were evacuated to Caravan Ribat and on to Aaru Village, Jinn sandstorms besieged the desert until the reawakened Jinni Liloupar calmed them, and the Seven Pillars opened Aaru, whose reconfigured system now collects and stores the information Irminsul once held. The Tanit tribe remains destroyed.

Opening Aaru freed Heryshaf, Sobek and Thoth from their imprisonment (Nefer answered Thoth's three questions) and released the countless souls of the Golden Slumber to the ley lines, ending King Deshret's afterlife. Afterwards Thoth and Heryshaf chose to stay at the Temple of Silence for the time being, and Liloupar later faded away at Windrise in Mondstadt after absorbing Collei's god remains. Separately, a 5.0 patch adjusted terrain in the Desert of Hadramaveth, and the 6.5 Temple of Space includes a Desert Pavilion built in the style of the desert temples; neither changes the desert's story.

Aaru Village still shelters its Village Keepers and refugees. In 6.6 Tighnari, Collei and Dori defended it against Jinn attacks until Collei, guided by Nicole's voice, recited a prayer written by Nabu Malikata that made the Jinn submit. During the same crisis a Fatui detachment led by Pantalone, disguised as a subordinate of Dottore, crossed the desert and trapped the Traveler inside desert ruins.

113.comment: Great Red Sand: King Deshret and the Three Eternal Companion-Gods
113.content:
King Deshret, the Lord of Deserts, also called Al-Ahmar and Amun, ruled the desert alongside Greater Lord Rukkhadevata and Nabu Malikata, the Goddess of Flowers, as the Three Eternal Companion-Gods. Each held a different realm: banquet, authority and life. He loved Nabu Malikata. When he pursued forbidden knowledge to defy the Heavenly Principles, Rukkhadevata left; Nabu Malikata ultimately gave her life for the ritual. Mourning, Deshret became the Mourning King, secluded himself, and built the Primal Constructs and the mechanism at Khaj-Nisut in pursuit of an eternal "golden slumber". He is said to have separated his mind from his body, leaving a golden husk in the mausoleum.

Deshret refused a "gift" from Celestia (implied to be a Gnosis). He divided his power among retainers, the Seven Pillars: Heryshaf (his deputy and chief of the Pillars), Sobek and Thoth (with Heryshaf the "Three Retainers"), the sage Hermanubis, the constructs Bennu and Shesepankh, and Apep, who never accepted the title. He later banished Heryshaf, Sobek and Thoth to Aaru. Remus, a god whose homeland Deshret conquered, refused to serve him and left Sumeru. He ended his own life to stop the disaster, and Apep consumed his body, which corrupted her. Apep believes he planned it as a fail-safe.

114.comment: Great Red Sand: Gurabad and Liloupar
114.content:
Gurabad, the "city of brass" or "City of Kings", was a vassal city in the southwest of the Desert of Hadramaveth. A shepherd, Ormazd, united the tribes with the help of Deshret and the Jinni Liloupar, but he grew tyrannical and kept slavery. Liloupar plotted his city's fall across generations. Her daughter Shirin, tricked, served poisoned honey that killed Ormazd and Shirin's siblings; her son Kisra became King Parvezravan, forced Shirin to make mindless Jinn to power machines that replaced slave labour, and faced the Brass Mask rebellion led by his own son, Shiruyeh. Liloupar used Abyssal power and most of the city sank into a chasm; a plague then killed half the survivors.

The Council of Nobles refused to fund infrastructure while desertification, shrinking oases and poverty (in Panjvahe, for example) fed unrest, and the clergy blamed lack of faith in Deshret. The revolt lasted thirteen days. Later rulers rebuilt Gurabad to claim the title "king of kings". The plague that followed was called "Shiruyeh's Plague", and the name Shiruyeh came to be associated with cowards and exiles.

115.content:
Aaru Village is the largest human settlement in the desert, holding Deshret's followers and descendants and Akademiya exiles. It stands as the last embers of his civilisation, guarded by Candace and led by its chief, Uncle Anpu; its Village Keepers are exiled Akademiya scholars. The Old Blind Poet and others settled here to await his return. Caravan Ribat is the checkpoint on the road to the forest.

It is built around an old border fortress from the time of Gurabad. Refugees tired of the warring desert kingdoms, led by a blind heir of Tulaytullah (the Old Blind Poet), renounced kings and founded it, naming it after Aaru, the "ancient dream of the gods"; Candace says its earliest people came from Deshret's city of Akhtamun. In Chapter III, radicals exploit rumours that King Deshret is returning to abduct the Village Keepers. In 6.6 it housed evacuees from the rainforest during the Irminsul crisis.

116.comment: Great Red Sand: The Tanit and the Tanit Camps
116.content: The Tanit were a nomadic Eremite tribe, led by a matriarch and Nine Elders, who dwelled in Tanit Camps in the south of the Desert of Hadramaveth. They wandered the desert, mistrusted the Akasha and relied on smuggled Akademiya books. Their enemies were traitors, not outsiders. They also raised captured children as Falcons. Late in their story Babel allied with the Fatui to remove rival elders and, once Jeht and the Traveler found the Orchard of Pairidaeza, tried to kill the Traveler to claim the Eternal Oasis. Informed of the betrayal, Jeht and the Traveler destroyed the tribe, leaving only a few survivors. The Vahumana researcher Tanjiyy later found the camp empty.

117.comment: Great Red Sand: Apep and Mt. Damavand
117.content: Apep, the Dendro Dragon Sovereign, once ruled Sumeru and nurtured the first elemental lifeforms in her inner world, the Heart of Oasis. Her pursuit of forbidden knowledge to fight the Heavenly Principles contaminated her and her creatures; Tumors of the Withering are those lifeforms at the end of their lives. She holds court beneath the Desert of Hadramaveth and, in the quest "Homecoming", appears at Mt. Damavand. After Kusanali purged forbidden knowledge, a void remained; the Traveler and Nahida helped restore the Heart of Oasis, and Apep chose to rest and watch. In 6.6 she sheltered the unconscious Nahida in the Heart of Oasis, sharing her Dendro energy, and later returned her to the Mausoleum of King Deshret.

118.comment: Great Red Sand: Eremite Spirits and Legends
118.content: The Eremites are Sumeru's only authorised mercenary organisation. They hail from the fallen civilisations of the Great Red Sand and are very loosely organised: anyone can join, though traditionally only desert folk could. Rukh Shah is one exception. Some borrow power from fragments of ancient desert spirits that live in their weapons; the spirits wake in danger and, it is said, demand blood. They work all over Teyvat and partner with the Adventurers' Guild.

119.comment: Great Red Sand: Khemenu Temple and the Ruin Devices
119.content: Deshret's temples are guarded by ruin devices: Everlight and Neverlight Cells, Primal Beams, fan blades, sandglasses, plinths and barriers, each requiring a clearance level from the Scarlet Sand Slate, a tablet that unlocks Deshret's technology. Khemenu Temple, entered after the quest "An Introduction to Indoor Archaeology", is one of the countless temples where people lowered their heads to praise his wisdom.

120.content:
Grove of Dreams: The Grove of Dreams is an underground cavern in Apam Woods, in the Dharma Forest of Sumeru. Arapandu describes it as a place where one may enter dreams.

It connects to the Ruins of Dahri to the west and holds one of the "branch and leaf" energy sources of the Varuna Contraption. Like Vanarana, it exists in a real and a dream version; the Traveler switches between them by playing the Rhythm of the Great Dream on a Vintage Lyre at a Silapna.

Some enemies do not appear in the dream version.

Geography: Entered through a stone-littered opening in the ground, reached by following a large tree root north of the Slumbering Roots quest marker. The twisting roots of the great tree make finding anything there hard.

Local flora include Nilotpala Lotus and Rukkhashava Mushrooms. Hazards are floating and winged fungi, Cryo Whopperflowers, and ruin machines (Ruin Drakes, Cruiser, Destroyer).

People: Arakunti, one of the Aranara who tend the Varuna Contraption, withdraws here and hides unless Aranara music is played. He speaks cryptically, saying one might be a tree, rain, a dream of Vana or the strings of an instrument.

Arakunti sends word to Arapandu that he is fine and that the Grove looks after him; Arapandu had asked the Traveler to check on him.

History: The Grove shelters one component of the Varuna Contraption, the device Greater Lord Rukkhadevata built to bring timely rains. It had gone unmaintained, and part of its restoration is done here.

Quests: Slumbering Roots, part of Varuna Gatha: the Traveler follows Arakunti into the Grove, plays the Rhythm of the Great Dream at Silapna, and in the dream turns three leaves toward the branch.

Atmosphere: Root-tangled and dim, a place where waking and dreaming sit close together.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 unchanged; nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content was found.

Nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content was found that changes it. Its Varuna Contraption branch belongs to the same system whose main contraption is at The Rain's End.

121.content:
Gurabad (also: City of Brass, City of Kings): Gurabad, called the City of Kings and the city of brass, was a great ancient city in the southwest of Sumeru's Desert of Hadramaveth. It prospered as King Deshret's favoured vassal, then fell: the shepherd-king Ormazd betrayed the Jinni Liloupar, who took revenge over three generations, ending with much of the city swallowed by a chasm and a plague. Later kings kept trying to restore it. Its ruins are now largely abandoned.

Its downfall is told in the book The Tale of Shiruyeh and Shirin and in the quest Memories of Gurabad. Because holding Gurabad later became a way to claim the whole desert, the ruins are woven into many other stories: Tulaytullah, Ay-Khanoum, Makhaira, Faramarz and the Eremites.

Geography: The ruins lie in the south-west of the Desert of Hadramaveth, in the Great Red Sand. A great gate and a large Ruin Golem of Khaenri'ahn make, identical to the one at Devantaka Mountain, stand among the remains. The Debris of Panjvahe, in the same desert, was a poor district served by a river valley that once irrigated it.

Most of the original city fell into a deep chasm. Surface ruins and underground chambers hold records, such as the notes called Zandik's Legacy (which mention an Akademiya expedition to Gurabad in the distant past and say parts Zandik found near Ardravi Valley could repair Gurabad's machines) and the inscriptions called Records of Gurabad.

History: A shepherd, Ormazd, won the favour of King Deshret and the Jinni Liloupar and used her blessing to unite the desert peoples, founding Gurabad after Nabu Malikata's death. Liloupar expected him to end slavery; he kept it. Her sense of betrayal made her plot the city's ruin across three generations. She had her daughter by Ormazd, Shirin, bring poisoned honey to a banquet: Ormazd and Shirin's siblings died, Shirin lost her mind, and her husband Kisra (Liloupar's own son, raised as Ormazd's heir and titled Parvez) became king as Parvezravan. He used Jinn-powered machines made by Shirin to replace slave labour, and the resentment of those left jobless fed the "Brass Mask" rebellion of Khorramdin, in truth Parvezravan and Shirin's banished son Shiruyeh. The Great Revolt followed; Liloupar used Abyssal power, turned Parvezravan into a monster and let much of the city fall into the earth. A plague then killed about half the inhabitants.

Before the fall the city was declining: deserts spread, oases shrank, harvests failed, and areas like Panjvahe stayed poor. The Council of Nobles refused to pay for infrastructure or welfare, nobles ignored lower-ranking officials such as General Hibehrous, and the clergy blamed weak faith in Deshret. The Great Revolt lasted at least thirteen days. The plague became known as Shiruyeh's Plague and Shiruyeh as the Lord of Pestilence; his name came to mean coward or exile.

Gurabad fell before King Deshret's forbidden-knowledge incident. After the original city and Deshret were gone, rising desert leaders rebuilt Gurabad to claim its prestige as the former favoured vassal and style themselves "king of kings".

Later kings: Inscriptions in the Mausoleum of King Deshret and artifact lore outline the later reclamations. Kavusbay claimed to be Shiruyeh's heir; Shah Ramshahr, who seems to have usurped him, drained the people to enrich his capital and raised seven towers near seven cities, among them Ay-Khanoum, Tulaytullah and Saleh. After Ramshahr, his son Artaxir died, Turan Khagan of Saleh was branded a traitor and executed with his sons, and Humayun of Tulaytullah ruled briefly until his death in the Jinn Uprising. Garshasp of Ay-Khanoum moved the capital away and later died; the young noble Goudarz of Tulaytullah then won a victory, renamed himself Saleb Dowleh and restored Gurabad as capital. After ten years of peace his family quarrelled; the Dey Muzaffar of Orghana (now Port Ormos), invited as an ally, betrayed him, burned Gurabad and killed him, then built his capital elsewhere in the desert and never went back.

To avoid the same end, Muzaffar told his son Zumurud to have many heirs; Zumurud reportedly had 99 children, including Badanah, Muzzudin and Hanzada Sultan, and the desert kingdoms enjoyed something like a golden age. Badanah, a tyrant, ruled Gurabad through violent conquests and made Tulaytullah and Saleh vassals. Tulaytullah's elite gave him the sword-dancer Makhaira, who fell in love with his son Faramarz and plotted with him to kill Badanah in a staged hunting accident. Faramarz later lost his throne to a conspiracy of city-dwellers and slave-warriors and was exiled to the rainforest. See the Tulaytullah entry for the rest.

People: Ormazd (shepherd-king), Liloupar (Jinni, partner and avenger), Shirin (daughter and unwitting poisoner), Kisra Parvezravan (Liloupar's son, Shirin's husband, then king) and Shiruyeh (leader of the Brass Mask rebels, also known as Khorramdin). The Jinni Ferigees suspected what Liloupar did, but the people never knew.

Status as of 7.1: Gurabad is an abandoned ruin. Some Eremites live in parts of it, and others come on expeditions to hunt for the city's treasures.

The ruins hold the Ruin Golem and relics of several failed revivals. Liloupar's long imprisonment is part of its legacy and appears in the Sumeru Archon Quest King Deshret and the Three Magi, where Memories of Gurabad also explains the city's fall. Nothing found up to Version 7.1 reports a later change to the site.

Dangers: Eremites; Ruin Guards and Ruin Golems; unstable ground and the chasm that swallowed the city.

Atmosphere: A wind-scoured wreck of cracked stone and brass, a place the desert folk tell cautionary stories about. The city is remembered as proud and wealthy, and its ruins feel like a warning about broken promises and exploited labour.

122.content: Shirin was Liloupar's daughter by Ormazd and married Liloupar's son Kisra, adopted by Ormazd. After the poisoned banquet she went mad and, under the new king Parvezravan, created mindless Jinn to power his machines. Their son Shiruyeh, banished as a threat, led the Brass Mask rebellion as Khorramdin with Liloupar's backing. In the end Liloupar's Abyssal power turned Parvezravan into a monster and brought down the city; Shirin and Shiruyeh were lost with it. In popular memory Shirin is blamed.

123.content: Badanah, last tyrant of Gurabad in this chain, was killed in a staged hunting accident by his son Faramarz and Makhaira. Faramarz's reign was unstable: he abdicated to his uncle Balash, was exiled by his uncle Goraz, restored after Goraz died, fought rebels and uncles, and finally poisoned Makhaira with viper venom. Dethroned for good, he went to the rainforest.

124.content:
Gurabad's Ruin - Temple of Deshret (also: Temple of Gurabad, Temple of Deshret, Gurabad's Ruin): Gurabad's Ruin - Temple of Deshret is a temple complex on the outskirts of the fallen city of Gurabad, in the canyon country of the Desert of Hadramaveth. It is full of sand-driving machines and sealed rooms, and two hidden chambers on its upper and lower levels hold murals about the shepherd-king Ormazd and the Jinni Liloupar. It is explored in the quest The Temple Where Sand Flows Like Tears.

The Tanit tribe regards the ruins as cursed and taboo. Jeht, who counts as half an outsider, goes in with the Traveler to find a fragment of the Mother of the Jinn.

Geography: A temple with an upper and a lower level, and a giant central device. It lies in Safhe Shatranj, a canyon the Tanit call the Great Rift, in the southwest of the Desert of Hadramaveth; before the quest the area is called The Temples Forsaken and drifts of sand block the way.

Drifts of loose sand can only be cleared by operating the temple's devices: a machine blows sand in a set direction, and a hard blow can turn it to a new direction and make runes flow. Sealing machines, gates and a collapsing section create a chain of linked puzzles across the complex.

Places: The main temple centres on a giant device, which the quest has the party touch more than once as the sand-sealing machines are woken and the sand is made to flow. Opposite the square is a smaller ruin that holds Liloupar's Cell. Two sealed mural rooms, one on each level, are the temple's best known features.

The upper-level murals show Ormazd, then Ormazd with Liloupar. The lower-level murals show Huvashtra, the tyrant Ormazd overthrew, and Ormazd with Liloupar twice more. The paintings depict Liloupar in a loose pinkish style; apart from that, her appearance is largely unknown.

History: Tradition among the desert folk says Gurabad was the work of the shepherd Ormazd, who with King Deshret's grace and Liloupar's help overthrew the tyrant Huvashtra and gathered the desert's wandering tribes. Liloupar later brought ruin on the city across three generations in revenge for his corruption, and King Deshret punished her by splitting her into seven fragments hidden in the Great Red Sand.

A tablet found after the second mural room opens gives Ormazd's own words: once a humble shepherd, he credits Deshret for his forces, says Deshret sent the great Jinni from the City of the Moon Maiden to help build Gurabad, and dedicates half his kingdom to Liloupar and half to the king. He also speaks of a coming sacrifice of a thousand slaves. Jeht remarks that whoever first built the place must have believed their works would last forever.

Culture: For the Tanit tribe the ruins are bad luck. Their guide Azariq stops short of going deeper than the temple's gate. Jeht quotes the Tanit proverb that the closer the home the more reticent the heart, and Matriarch Babel's maxim that true gold has deep roots in soil and spring.

Atmosphere: Wind-scoured stone, drifts of sand and ancient machinery that wakes when touched. The viewpoint's name for it is the Palace Abandoned by the Gods, and the desert songs say long-lived giants once lived here before being cast into a rift in one night.

Dangers: Eremites, Primal Constructs and fungi are among the enemies in the surrounding canyon. A forgotten mechanical guardian called Anoushbord confronts the party at the smaller ruin opposite the square, where the bottle holding Liloupar's fragment lies.

Quests: The Temple Where Sand Flows Like Tears is the second part of the world quest series The Dirge of Bilqis. The Murals of Gurabad, an unofficially titled hidden exploration objective, becomes available once The Dirge of Bilqis is finished; it requires finding six Mysterious Stone Slates, three per door, and awards two Precious Chests and the achievement The Nameless City's Past.

After the quest the Tanit's search continues with Dune-Entombed Fecundity, and the Traveler later learns more of Gurabad's fall in Memories of Gurabad, begun at the chessboard of Safhe Shatranj.

The reason for the visit is political. Matriarch Babel wants a Jinni to restore fertility to the tribe's soil and to carry the party through the seals of the Eternal Oasis, and Azariq says this particular Jinni still keeps her intelligence. A Jinni gives a human her true name to form a contract, and Jeht warns that Jinn are said to hate humanity. Liloupar dismisses the Tanit's schemes, but offers her true name to the Traveler alone.

Status as of 7.1: Accessible and cleared of sand. Nothing found up to Version 7.1 reveals later change here.

125.comment: Gurabad's Ruin - Temple of Deshret: The Murals of Gurabad
125.content: After finishing The Dirge of Bilqis, the Traveler can find slates I to III to open the upper-level door and slates IV to VI to open the lower-level door of the temple. The murals show Ormazd, Ormazd with Liloupar and the defeated tyrant Huvashtra. A tablet in the lower room gives Ormazd's account, in which Deshret's grace let him unseat Huvashtra, the Jinni came to help, and he promised his kingdom to Liloupar and the king alike.

126.content:
Hangeh Afrasiyab (also: Forge of the Abandoned Foundry, Gate of Everlasting Mourning): Hangeh Afrasiyab is an abandoned underground factory of the lost kingdom of Khaenri'ah, hidden under Gavireh Lajavard in Sumeru's Girdle of the Sands. It once processed Azosite, an energy block drawn from ley lines, and deep inside is a sealed gate to the lost nation itself. In the quest As the Khvarena's Light Shows it holds the last Great Song of Khvarena, and Nasejuna reveals he has been using the party.

Dahri is an archaic Sumeru name for Khaenri'ah, so the quest calls this an underground Dahrian factory. By Nasejuna's reading of the records it belonged to the Schwanenritter, the knight order that fought the monsters of the cataclysm.

Geography: Two map levels, upper and lower, in Gavireh Lajavard. The main hall is the energy control hub, with relays sealed in Gray Crystals, a furnace for smelting Azosite, an elevator to the deepest level and a control room above. Mourning Flowers and Trishiraite are local specialties; the Gate of Everlasting Mourning viewpoint overlooks the sealed gate.

The gate bears the eight-pointed star of Khaenri'ah, and a statue in the factory resembles a Black Serpent Knight. The interior has the same industrial, brass feel as the Ruin Golems and the testing facility at Madinat al-Nuhas, and the wiki sets all of them on a grand scale. Inside are a pipe room with logs, a smelting furnace room on an upper floor, and the room at the foot of the elevator.

History: Azosite was made here by extracting pure elemental energy from ley lines and smelting it into Energy Blocks. A mutilated set of notes says the royal workshop Gnade had gone out of use and this was probably the last workshop with a full Azosite-powered system. Nasejuna, citing records, says it was owned by the Schwanenritter, as was the proving ground at Madinat al-Nuhas, and that they resisted the monsters that came from below in the cataclysm 500 years ago.

An old journal found here tells of most people fleeing to the surface with the Schwanenritter while some stayed to hide; it reports rumours that those who went above fell sick and turned into monsters, and ends in hopelessness. A bulletin says that because King Irmin was indisposed, Knight Marshal Anfortas had declared himself Regent. An unfinished letter to the Marshal argues that the kingdom's prosperity came from stealing secrets from beyond the skies and that human will, not dogma, should drive technology.

According to the wiki, Rene, a researcher from Fontaine, visited around the time of the cataclysm. His investigation notes record that Azosite was stable and safe but lacked any will, since it was pure elemental force, and he compared it to the difference between a Hydro Slime and an Oceanid. A second set of torn pages by him states that Khvarena can reverse Abyssal influence and wonders whether Azosite smelting could be applied to Khvarena or to the potent energy called Amrita. These are the speculations of an outside scholar.

Dangers: Ruin Guards, Ruin Defenders, Ruin Cruisers, Ruin Destroyers and Ruin Graders guard the mechanisms, and hilichurls and mitachurls have wandered in. At the bottom, the Abyss Herald Klingsor and Nasejuna attack the party.

Quests: As the Khvarena's Light Shows (Khvarena of Good and Evil, part 2) leads the Traveler, Paimon, Sorush and Nasejuna here to seek the fifth Great Song of Khvarena. Nasejuna opens doors, links circuits with Farrwicks to power three relays and then the central control device, and rides the elevator down with them.

At the bottom Nasejuna drops his pose, calls Sorush an idiot of a Pari and says he plans to reverse the Rite of Chinvat using the Songs, releasing the Abyss and restarting the old wars. He claims the Skeptics' history is invention and the Dahri records are the true story, that those who resisted the defilement were the Skeptics' real ancestors, and that the Akademiya erased them. The Traveler and Sorush refuse to hand over the Songs. Nasejuna calls in Klingsor; both are beaten, but Nasejuna slips away, and Paimon later notes that they cannot trust his claims.

Status as of 7.1: Abandoned. Some machinery still runs and the main gate toward Khaenri'ah is sealed. Nothing found up to Version 7.1 changes this.

127.comment: Hangeh Afrasiyab: Gate of Everlasting Mourning
127.content: A grand gate leading to the world beneath the soil, sealed tight. Its viewpoint text adds that the once prosperous kingdom behind it has long since turned to rubble.

128.content: Nasejuna, who calls himself Vijnanapati of his Order, lured Sorush into the Rite of Chinvat to get at the Great Songs and had arranged for Klingsor to be waiting at the factory. He wanted to reverse the rite, which would unseal the Abyss, and believed the Dahri records over the Skeptics' own. Both he and the Abyss Herald are defeated, and he escapes.

129.content:
Harvisptokhm (also: God of the Pari, Mother Tree of All Seeds): The Harvisptokhm is the giant tree in the middle of Vourukasha Oasis in Sumeru, the Pari's homeland, and serves as the God of the Pari. It grew from the remains of Egeria, the former Hydro Archon, and keeps her consciousness tied to the mortal world while suppressing an Abyssal rift.

Its interior can be entered through a hole at Tunigi Hollow or from the top of its stump. Inside lies a giant lotus, the Gaokerena, in which the God of the Pari's consciousness slumbers.

Before the Khvarena of Good and Evil quests it looked like a withered stump with the Sign of Apaosha, an Abyss-reflecting phenomenon, looming above; afterwards it has a glowing blue canopy.

Geography: Stands at the centre of Vourukasha Oasis, in the Realm of Farakhkert of the Girdle of the Sands. Tunigi Hollow, the old site of the Abyssal rift, opens into it. Around it lies the Amrita, a sea of pure dew made from Egeria's remains.

After the Rite of Chinvat is performed, jumping into Tunigi Hollow takes the player to the Harvisptokhm instead. The name echoes the Zoroastrian tree of all seeds growing in the cosmic sea Vourukasha.

People: The Pari are the oasis's guardians and regard it as their god. Elder Zurvan sealed the Oasis with the Great Songs of Khvarena after an Abyss attack and admits only heroes bonded with Pari and pilgrims who come to worship Egeria. Sorush, Mihir and Rashnu are Pari in the quest line.

The Oceanids, created and served by Egeria, rejected the ideals of the new Hydro Archon Focalors and came looking for their master at Tunigi Hollow. Finding not what they hoped, they scattered; people followed their pilgrimage trail, which led to the Purification Spring domain.

The name Harvisptokhm echoes the Zoroastrian tree of all seeds, which grows with the white Haoma (Gaokerena) in the sea Vourukasha; the game's naming of the lotus Gaokerena follows that source.

History: During the cataclysm, gods including Greater Lord Rukkhadevata and Egeria went to Tunigi Hollow to suppress the Abyssal defilement from Khaenri'ah below. Egeria was slain in the battle and her body became Amrita. Rukkhadevata grew the Harvisptokhm from it to anchor her consciousness, so it could absorb the defilement from the rift and keep the seal.

In Khvarena of Good and Evil the Traveler, with Sorush and the other Pari, gathers the Great Songs of Khvarena and cleanses the defilement through the Rite of Ab-Zohr; the Defiled Chambers, the Gaokerena and the Flower of Sanctity are part of that climax. After The Hymn of Tir Yazad (Part 2) the Sign of Apaosha is sealed.

Religion: The Pari treat the tree as their god and Egeria's remnant; pilgrims come to worship her. The Great Songs of Khvarena and the Rite of Chinvat, Ab-Zohr and Tir Yazad are the ritual vocabulary of the quest line.

Dangers: Before the quest, Abyssal defilement and its monsters surrounded the rift; afterwards a Consecrated Fanged Beast guards the former rift and reappears. Interior chambers were defiled during the quest.

Atmosphere: Hushed and sacred: pure dew, a god in slumber and a people who keep vigil over a grief older than most living memory.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the defilement has been cleansed and the seal holds; the tree is a living, restored sacred site. Nothing found in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content changes it.

130.content: The giant lotus inside the Harvisptokhm, where the God of the Pari's consciousness is said to slumber. In The Hymn of Tir Yazad the Traveler defends the Flower of Sanctity there against Abyssal creatures while the power of Amrita lends help.

131.comment: Harvisptokhm: Egeria's Remains and the Amrita
131.content:
Egeria was the Hydro Archon and God of Justice who ruled Fontaine until 500 years ago, killed at Tunigi Hollow during the cataclysm. Her body became the Amrita, from which the tree was grown; Focalors succeeded her.

Her consciousness is kept in the mortal world by the tree. The Pari and the Oceanids are among the peoples she created.

132.content:
Hills of Barsom (also: Barsom): The Hills of Barsom lie just north of Asipattravana Swamp in the Realm of Farakhkert, in Sumeru's Girdle of the Sands. They are home to the Barsom, a huge pine with pink foliage, and to its familiar, the Pari Rashnu, who sleeps there.

The hills were the setting of the Order of Skeptics' old musical ritual with the Pari and are the start of the world quest "Awakening's Real Sound" (3.6), part of the Khvarena of Good and Evil series.

The name echoes the barsom, a ritual implement used by Zoroastrian priests in sacred ceremonies, according to the wiki.

Geography: A rise of ground dominated by the Barsom tree, a towering pine with pink foliage. The area sits just north of Asipattravana Swamp, and the Samudra Coast and a cave by the water lie close by.

The quest "Awakening's Real Sound" also has the party search a cavern whose walls carry the drum scores, with Thundercraven Rifthound Whelps inside. The five Kory Drums, one for each of five elements, are items found around the Girdle of the Sands.

People: Rashnu, a Pari called the Familiar of the Barsom, lives in and around the tree, usually asleep. Nasejuna, the Order of Skeptics' Nasuraia (Vijnanapati), brings the Traveler to the hills and cares about the Order's traditions; Sorush, the young Pari who calls the Traveler her Yasnapati, comes to wake Rashnu and take her to the Vourukasha Oasis.

Rashnu is sleepy and blunt. Before she is woken she says Barsom is a peaceful place for good sleep, that Pari sleep differently from humans, and that sleep lets her focus on what the roots and branches say. She calls the Kory Drums a human instrument that is extremely noisy.

History: By the Order of Skeptics' account, their predecessors, after helping the Pari quell the disaster of the cataclysm, befriended them. Barsom's familiar liked music, so the Skeptics made the Kory Drums; to make the bond ("Laupa") official, five drums had to be gathered and played to scores. The drums were later lost and Barsom's familiar stopped answering them.

The truth, revealed in "Awakening's Real Sound", is different: Rashnu found the human drumming too noisy and threw the drums to different places so she could sleep. Nasejuna is dismayed that his records were wrong; Sorush says the scattering may have been meant to test who was fit to be a Yasnapati. Rashnu agrees to travel with Sorush to the Vourukasha Oasis, and after The Hymn of Tir Yazad (Part 2) she greets the Traveler there as one of Sorush's companions and gives credit for extinguishing the Sign of Apaosha to Sorush and her helpers.

The Barsom viewpoint ("Elder Pine Atop the Wastes", unlocked after the quest) says the spirit within the pine has sheltered a great many warriors returning from their trials, though nobody remembers the details of the ancient compact. The Kory Drums are named after the five skandhas of Buddhist thought (form, perception, formation, sensation, consciousness) in the game's naming, and the wiki ties the whole ritual to the union between the Order and the Pari.

Quests: "Awakening's Real Sound" begins here (3.6). Julien's "An Artist Adrift" also starts nearby, at a cave between the Samudra Coast and Asipattravana Swamp, once "The Splendorous Sky That Day" is complete.

Dangers: Thundercraven Rifthound Whelps in the drum-score cavern; the wider Girdle of the Sands is not safe. The tree and its familiar are not hostile.

Atmosphere: Quiet and sleepy. The giant pink pine towers over the hills, and the Pari who dwells in it dislikes noise; her only stated complaint is the drumming.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Rashnu has left her post to join Sorush at the Vourukasha Oasis, though the Barsom remains.

The Kory Drums have been recovered and played once; the Order of Skeptics' version of the ritual has been corrected, but Nasejuna's unanswered questions about the Skeptics' traditions are left for Rashnu to answer "later, perhaps".

133.comment: Hills of Barsom: Kory Drums and the Skeptics' Ritual
