133.content: Mysterious drums said to symbolise the union between the Order of Skeptics and the Pari. There are five, one per element (Rupa, Samjna, Sankhara, Vedana, Vijnana), each with a score that must be played in order. The scores are carved in stone and survived the sandstorms; the drums themselves were lost until the Traveler found them. In truth Rashnu scattered them because they were noisy.

134.content: A Pari known as the Familiar of the Barsom. Sleepy, honest and uninterested in "human business". She answers Sorush, whom she recognises, agrees to go with her to the Vourukasha Oasis, and says that sleeping is also a duty. Her Zoroastrian-derived name refers to the yazata of justice, according to the wiki.

135.content:
House of Daena: The House of Daena is the great library at the centre of the Sumeru Akademiya in Sumeru City, the largest library in all of Teyvat. It was once reckoned the repository of all knowledge in the world because of its unmatched collection, but the Akasha System has since taken that role. It still stands as a symbol of Sumeru, the Nation of Wisdom.

Officially only students and teachers of the Akademiya may borrow its books. It is run by a Grand Conservator, who is responsible for acquiring new material and maintaining the existing collection.

Places: An elevated platform in the middle of the library carries a lift. After the events of the Archon Quest "Jnagarbha Day" it can rise to the Grand Sage's office or descend to the confinement room.

Books on its shelves include the Scroll of Streaming Song, The Folio of Foliage and The Tale of Shiruyeh and Shirin, plus quest volumes such as An Ode to Khvarena, The Lay of Al-Ahmar and The Shepherd and the Magic Bottle.

People: The librarian Katayoun and the matra Shohre work here, with students and researchers such as Hunayn, Sanad, Gregor, Jafar and Nargess. After the Archon Quest the mahamata Panah is found here.

The next Grand Conservator is expected to be Vikram or Rifaet. The character Shatir calls Lisa "Mondstadt's Grand Conservator" and says she would have been his first pick for the Sumeru post had she stayed.

Governance: Run as part of the Akademiya under a Grand Conservator; only its students and teachers may borrow books.

History: Once the world's bank of knowledge, it was superseded by the Akasha System, but the old library remains in use.

In the Archon Quest the Traveler and Alhaitham enter it during the Akademiya's Jnagarbha Day, and the Grand Sage Azar intercepts them there and has the Traveler detained. Later Alhaitham is found in the library arguing with Kaveh, who has returned from the desert to discover that the sages have been overthrown.

Atmosphere: Vast, hushed and scholarly, an old stack of shelves and reading rooms where researchers work by day and night; a symbol of Sumeru's reverence for learning.

Quests: Appears in the Archon Quest chapter "Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises" (Jnagarbha Day and its aftermath). These events are a major spoiler for characters who have not witnessed them.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the library stands as it did at the close of the 3.0 Archon Quest; no later change is recorded in the pages consulted.

136.comment: House of Daena: Etymology of Daena
136.content: The name draws on the Zoroastrian concept of daena, insight and revelation, which the wiki glosses as "that which is seen or observed."

137.content:
Hypostyle Desert: The Hypostyle Desert is the central part of Sumeru's Great Red Sand, the land of King Deshret's ruined civilisation. It contains the giant Mausoleum of King Deshret, the underground Khemenu Temple and the resting place of Sobek Oasis. The ancient city-state of Tulaytullah once stood here.

The name is an architectural term for a hall whose roof rests on rows of pillars, fitting the area's pillared temple ruins. The Golden Slumber quest series (3.1) runs through it.

Geography: A vast field of dunes and oases with a few plateaus. On a plateau north-east of the Sobek Oasis waypoint stands a stone tablet whose carved words promise that the golden sandstorm and burning sun will exorcise the darkness on behalf of the reader, guiding a spirit that perished here back to the Orchard of Pairidaeza. The Garden of Endless Pillars, a one-time domain, lies west of the Dune of Carouses.

The Mausoleum is a giant pyramid; the Scarlet Sand Slate says it is only one corner of the palace, with many more temples beneath it. A great cyclone sat on top of it for a long time until the quest Dual Evidence switched it off for good.

Places: The Mausoleum of King Deshret, a golden husk left by the king, where his intelligence is not held. Khemenu Temple, an underground temple east of the Mausoleum. Sobek Oasis, a rest stop. The site of Tulaytullah, now at the Garden of Endless Pillars. The Altar of Mirages, which may be where Ay-Khanoum's remains lie.

In the Scarlet Sand Slate's description, Khemenu Temple is not the largest of the desert's countless temples but is intimately linked to the people, who enter, lower their heads and praise King Deshret's boundless wisdom. Its wall murals depict the king's reign.

The Garden of Endless Pillars has one level, Desert Vivarium, and the wiki notes that five Pyro monuments must be lit to open it and that a Dendro character is needed to finish it.

People: The Eremites roam the area, and the Tighnarians were once associated with Tulaytullah. The followers of King Deshret live mostly at Aaru Village in the Land of Lower Setekh, not here. Travelling adventurers sometimes rest at Sobek Oasis, as one of Cyno's character stories notes.

In the Golden Slumber quests the archaeologist Tirzad, the Eremite Jebrael, his daughter Jeht and the merchant Nachtigal travel in the desert with the Traveler. Fatui soldiers and the Eremite Samail appear in The Secret of Al-Ahmar.

History: Tulaytullah, the City of Sapphire, rose to prominence in the desert after King Deshret's civilisation fell. The priest Hermanubis founded the original Temple of Silence there and made it a city of wisdom, and the Temple kept the knowledge that survived the king's fall. After wars between city-states and Eremite tribes, the Temple's members left, and the city declined like the other desert kingdoms.

Legend says the city arose from the tears of Nabu Malikata. Ay-Khanoum, the Amphitheater City, was built for the Jinn by Nabu Malikata and King Deshret, and its name means Moon Maiden in the Jinn's old tongue; it was likely in this desert. A few generations after Gurabad's fall, Ay-Khanoum was ruled by Garshasp, who went on to unite several desert cities.

Tulaytullah's elite later paid tribute to Gurabad's kings; a power struggle followed the death of the king Badanah, and refugees from Tulaytullah and other declining desert kingdoms eventually founded Aaru Village. Layla's blue hair and pointed ears are said to mark her descent from Tulaytullah. The Eremite Shimti tribe traced its ancestry to the city; the Iab tribe massacred them about twenty years before the present day.

Dangers: Primal Constructs (Repulsors, Prospectors) in the ruins, Fatui and Eremite groups, scorpions and desert beasts, sunstroke, thirst, and the Mausoleum's old defences. The Garden of Endless Pillars domain has fungi.

Travel: Teleport waypoints are unlocked by stepping through Khemenu Temple and the Mausoleum. Travellers rest at Sobek Oasis. The Scarlet Sand Slate opens many of the temples and chambers.

Quests: Golden Slumber (3.1): An Introduction to Indoor Archaeology, The Secret of Al-Ahmar and Dreams Beneath the Searing Sand lead through Khemenu Temple and the Mausoleum to Khaj-Nisut. Others tied here include Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana, A Tower Unto Wisdom and Folly, Headlong Into the Sands, Darkness Looming and Invisible Barrier.

Atmosphere: A hush of pillars, gold light and wind over dunes, with Khemenu's murals and the giant cyclone's old roar giving way to quiet oases. The Mausoleum feels like a monument to a dream that outlasted its dreamer.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the desert is open and the Mausoleum's cyclone is gone.

Nothing from 6.x or 7.0-7.1 changes the area.

138.content: An ancient city-state of the Hypostyle Desert, once a city of wisdom founded around the Temple of Silence by the priest Hermanubis. It declined during the wars among desert city-states. Its refugees helped found Aaru Village.

139.content: A city built for the Jinn by King Deshret and Nabu Malikata, whose name means Moon Maiden in the Jinn's ancient language. Now in ruins, likely in the Hypostyle Desert; the Altar of Mirages may mark its remains.

140.content:
Kalimi Exchange (also: Kalimi stock exchange): The Kalimi Exchange is Sumeru City's stock exchange and marketplace, on Treasures Street. One can buy futures contracts here, and a bulletin board beside the building posts goods for sale. The Mahamata Barmak, a researcher with an economics degree, monitors it for illegal or fraudulent practice. A man who calls himself a millionaire, Hatim, stands outside during the day.

In Port Ormos, the Wikala Funduq trade supervisor Dilawar tells casual traders to "try your luck" at the Exchange, while warning that profit does not come easily.

People: Barmak is a Mahamata, an Akademiya official, posted at the Exchange. He welcomes "all law-abiding businessmen", says illegal trade is strictly prohibited, and says that as an economics researcher no speculation gets past him. In his private thoughts he is irritated by cocky youngsters who think they can get away with anything on his watch. Hatim is a self-proclaimed millionaire seen outside by day and inside Puspa Cafe at night. He calls the Exchange a place where people's strength, courage and insight are tested, and complains that its forecasters are amateurs.

Hatim claims to be the descendant of the oldest aristocratic family of the Great Red Sand, whose treasury holds the Dendro Archon's legacy and King Deshret's relics; he says the Homayani family have nothing on his. Others do not believe he is rich. He says his aim is to increase the family fortune so that his children never have to become merchants.

Quests: Hatim is the client of the repeatable Daily Commission Gold Devouring and Mora Gathering, in which he chases a "Golden Dish", a meal he believes raises diners' affinity for Mora. Follow-up versions have him lose everything, make a small profit, go bargain-hunting for Apple Cider, or strike a fortune that takes him to Lambad's Tavern. The commission is a gameplay feature rather than major lore.

Atmosphere: A bustling, orderly market: notice boards, people comparing forecasts and Barmak's watchful eye. Confidence and bluster are common; reliable fortunes are rare.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Exchange is open and unchanged.

No quest or event up to 7.1 changes the Exchange, Barmak or Hatim. Per the wiki's etymology note, Kalimi is a Telugu word meaning riches or wealth.

141.content:
Khaj-Nisut (also: Eye of the Sands, King Deshret's throne room): Khaj-Nisut ("Eye of the Sands" on the map before the Golden Slumber quests) is the throne temple of King Deshret, also called Al-Ahmar, buried in the Great Red Sand of Sumeru's desert. It is invisible until a visitor passes three trials, and the temple is built to recognise who is acknowledged: the scarlet slate that a visitor carries opens its doors, and its mechanisms test clearance. Inside, an immense empty throne sits at the top of a descent through lower halls. In the Golden Slumber quests the Eremite Samail was tricked onto the throne, entered the "Golden Slumber" that King Deshret's followers believe in, and Jebrael followed him in to stop him as the temple sealed behind them.

The name is Egyptian-derived for "appearance of the king", and the Chinese name uses a term for the manifestation of the sacred. The Scarlet Sand Slate calls it the sacred realm that all King Deshret's people aspired to reach, and warns that whoever acquires Al-Ahmar's wisdom loses their bodily form and cannot tell of it. The surrounding ruins are also the City of Gold domain, which the domain text describes as a stronghold once defended by seven battlements that crumbled overnight when King Deshret fell.

Geography: Khaj-Nisut lies in the Land of Lower Setekh, part of the Great Red Sand, in Sumeru's desert. An oasis in front of it is a resting place for travellers. The temple does not exist on the map or to the eye until the visitor has passed the three trials set around it and operated a Plinth of the Secret Rites; then it manifests. Inside it is a descent, not a climb: a lower floor, further halls below it, then a lift that carries visitors up to the throne room under the dome of Khaj-Nisut.

The Scarlet Sand Slate's guidance for Khaj-Nisut says the throne sits under the dome and that "to ascend to a high place, one must first look down". The ruins are reached from the same desert as the Mausoleum of King Deshret and Opet Hall, whose underground map points visitors toward Khaj-Nisut; the slate lists them as stages of one journey (Abdju Road, Khemenu Temple, the Mausoleum, Opet Hall, Khaj-Nisut, Duat Hall and onward). The wiki lists the point of interest as a subarea of the Land of Lower Setekh, while the Mausoleum is placed in the Hypostyle Desert; the quests treat them as parts of one complex.

Places: Entrance gateway and oasis: the oasis outside is where travellers refresh themselves before paying tribute. Lower floor and descent: halls with mechanisms (Plinths of the Secret Rites, a central device that must be set in action in three steps). Throne room: the throne of Al-Ahmar on the upper floor, beside a statue of Heryshaf (as pictured on the wiki).

The City of Gold domain is set in these ruins; its in-game description speaks of a desiccated temple on sundered rocks, "more akin to a tomb for an age of radiance long lost", where gold-eyed warriors once stood guard over watchtowers. Returning to the throne room after the quest, a visitor can reach it again as an ordinary exploration site.

People: Samail of the Thutmose, an Eremite faction that wants King Deshret's lost power, and Jebrael, once his partner as one of the "twin blades of Thutmose" and now a father, reach the throne in the story. Jeht (Jebrael's daughter), the Akademiya researcher Tirzad, the Traveler and Paimon enter with Benben, a small Primal Construct that responds to the ruins. Nobody lives in Khaj-Nisut. The only residents are the Primal Constructs and mechanisms of King Deshret's age and, during the quest, Samail's Eremite mercenaries and Fatui Skirmishers.

The Fatui are interested in the power of King Deshret and are found in the desert ruins in general. A missive signed by Samail that players can read in a tent in The Secret of Al-Ahmar says that conditions for opening the path are close and that Khaj-Nisut remains "an essential part of the puzzle".

Governance: King Deshret ruled from here in the sense that the throne is his, but the texts treat the building more as a place of acknowledgment than as an administrative centre. The slate's inscription on Opet Hall says blessings gathered there reach the throne directly, and the devout would gain honour of access to the throne room; the Khaj-Nisut inscription says only those acknowledged may set foot and gaze on the temple of King Deshret.

History: Khaj-Nisut belonged to the civilisation of King Deshret, the Lord of Deserts, in the age before and during the Archon War. In the Golden Slumber quests (3.1) it is rediscovered: first the Mausoleum, then, after a series of trials, the temple itself. The throne is empty, and the "wisdom" of Al-Ahmar that texts promised there is not an object but a prayer.

The slate says whoever obtains the wisdom of Al-Ahmar loses their body and cannot report it, which fits what the quest then shows. The Key of Khaj-Nisut sword (added to the game as a weapon) carries a legend of a key that sealed a homeland and hid a desert tower and "paradise of dreams" under illusions when the nations scattered; the story is told as a tale of a prince and a blind poet and does not describe this building directly.

A quest item named Khaj-Nisut, found in a chest during Dune-Entombed Fecundity: Part III, is a chess piece placed in the temple of Gurabad, built as a miniature of the Khaj-Nisut "which once belonged to King Deshret". The 6.6 Archon Quest does not return to the building itself, but it settles the fate of what its throne led into: Heryshaf reveals that the Golden Slumber is preserved within Aaru, and when the Seven Pillars open Aaru to help Sumeru against the Irminsul crisis, the souls held in the Golden Slumber return to the ley lines, ending King Deshret's afterlife for good. Jebrael's soul is among them.

Quests: Golden Slumber (World Quest series, 3.1), especially The Secret of Al-Ahmar and Dreams Beneath the Searing Sand. The follow-up series Old Notes and New Friends begins with Dual Evidence, which grants the Ferryman's Clearance for Duat Hall and the Great Hall of Truths in the Mausoleum.

Returning to the throne room after completing Dreams Beneath the Searing Sand grants a small reward (the achievement "Encore!" and a chest). The slate's "Clearance of Khaj-Nisut" is granted during The Secret of Al-Ahmar.

Dangers: Primal Constructs and the building itself. In the quest, after Samail enters the Slumber, the temple turns hostile and the visitors have to flee through the lower floors while a "sea of consciousness" pursues them; if it touches a visitor the escape restarts in the game's time trial. Outside, Samail's Eremites and Fatui Skirmishers patrol the ruins during the quest.

Atmosphere: Scale and silence. Gold and red stone worn by wind, deep halls lit by floating energy, a throne too large for a human body. The sense is of a place built to make a visitor feel they must earn their presence, and then of a building that still listens: mechanisms answering the slate, doors closing behind you.

Travel: Visitors need the Scarlet Sand Slate (obtained in Lost in the Sands) and, for the inner halls, the clearance that Tirzad's slate unlocks. The temple reveals itself only after the three trials and the operation of a Plinth of the Secret Rites. The Eremites and Fatui make the approach unsafe during the quest. Aaru Village, a refuge of King Deshret's descendants, is the nearest settlement and the base for expeditions.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the throne is empty and the temple is sealed after the Golden Slumber events. Jebrael and Samail never returned in body; Jeht kept her father's axe and went looking for the Tanit. In 6.6, when the Seven Pillars opened Aaru, the souls trapped in the Golden Slumber, Jebrael's among them, were released to the ley lines, and Jebrael spoke briefly with Jeht before departing.

No later canon through 7.1 changes the building itself, but the Golden Slumber that its prayer opened no longer exists as a refuge for souls. The City of Gold domain (3.3) remains in the surrounding ruins.

142.comment: Khaj-Nisut: Dreams Beneath the Searing Sand
142.content:
In the last chapter of the Golden Slumber, Jebrael and Jeht, the researcher Tirzad, the Traveler and Paimon travel to the oasis for Khaj-Nisut while the Eremite Samail's men attack the camp. A coded letter says Al-Ahmar's throne shows itself to those who pass three trials. After the trials Khaj-Nisut manifests; the party activates its mechanisms, rides the lift to the throne room and finds the throne empty. Samail arrives holding Jeht and demands the prayer needed to sit on the throne.

Jebrael recites a song that Jeht's mother Ufairah had deciphered from Al-Ahmar's texts. Samail sits on the throne, repeats the prayer and goes still: he has entered the Golden Slumber, a one-way trip. His mercenaries are beaten, but the temple turns against the visitors and Samail's voice speaks through it. Jebrael, who understands that the consciousness left in the Slumber can only be stopped from inside, goes into it while the others flee; Samail tells him he will soon become part of "us", and Jebrael answers that he is there to stop him. The door closes behind the fleeing party. Back at Aaru Village, Jeht keeps his axe and her mother's notes and plans to look for the Tanit tribe, which she learned was her father's. Tirzad prepares a paper and leaves the original slate with the Traveler.

143.comment: Khaj-Nisut: The Scarlet Sand Slate on Khaj-Nisut
143.content: The slate Tirzad brings is an etched relic of King Deshret's civilisation that commands devices in his ruins. It has "clearance levels" unlocked by lighting symbols in different places; the clearance of Khaj-Nisut is granted during The Secret of Al-Ahmar. Its text on Khaj-Nisut says an oasis lies before the temple, that the illusion appears at the end of a threefold trial, that it is the sacred realm that all King Deshret's people hoped to enter, and that recitation of the prayers opens the way to a "golden slumber where wisdom gathers"; whoever gets the wisdom loses a body and cannot tell of the wonders. The slate is the in-game reason players can see the ruins at all.

144.content: Thutmose is a group of Eremites, devout believers in King Deshret, who sought the secret of Al-Ahmar with help from researchers and even the Fatui; their base is at Lamb-Devourer Rock. Samail and Jebrael, both originally of the Tanit tribe and the survivors of an expedition to the ruins of Gurabad, founded or joined it and were known as its twin blades. Jebrael left after the birth of his daughter Jeht; the Golden Slumber quest says Samail killed Ufairah, Jeht's mother, because he saw her love as an infection weakening Jebrael. See the characters' own entries for their lives.

145.content:
Khemenu Temple (also: Temple of Secret Rites): Khemenu Temple is a buried temple in the Hypostyle Desert of Sumeru's Great Red Sand, underground to the east of King Deshret's Mausoleum. It is not the largest of the desert's temples but it is linked to the people: the Scarlet Sand Slate says all would enter and bow their heads to praise Deshret's wisdom. Its murals depict his reign.

The temple is explored in An Introduction to Indoor Archaeology, the second part of Golden Slumber, by the scholar Tirzad's team with the Traveler. It appears on the map once the quest is done.

Geography: Four map levels: the Entrance Hall, an Underground Area, the Underground Depths and a Chamber of Secrets. The slate tells a visitor to leave Abdju Road and walk toward the sunset along the axis. People painted images on the shrine walls with plant juice and ore powder, and sand does not cover them as it does footprints.

Features include a Plinth of the Secret Rites, Sacred Seals, Primal Beams, Everlight and Neverlight Cells, a Primal Sandglass and a Soulferry device. A Time Trial Challenge and Seelie are also here. The doors inside have three corners, which Paimon and the Traveler notice match the shape of the strange machine Benben.

Places: Inside is a mural of a sun and an eye above seven pillars and many small figures. Behind it a passage opens upward when Tirzad bumps into the wall. The temple also holds a vessel, a boat, in a dry room, and mechanisms using fans, torches and an elevator.

History: The slate calls Khemenu Temple modest in size but close to ordinary people, a place where all entered and praised Deshret. The temple belongs to the realm of King Deshret, whose civilisation is gone; generations of Vahumana researchers have studied the desert's ruins.

Murals in the temple depict the king's reign. Tirzad reads them as the ordinary people kept small beneath a king over seven pillars of authority. Jeht answers that the picture feels peaceful and orderly, and Jebrael points to the hope that bound the people of the sand to Deshret and their hope of overcoming the calamity. The quarrel is never resolved.

Tirzad, who calls himself an Indoorsology researcher, hopes the temple will supply material for his paper. In Dual Evidence his finished paper is named 'The Golden Slumber: A Study on Governance in the Later Period of Al-Ahmar's Civilization and Stages of Survival', which Soheil doubted until the Traveler's report vindicated it.

Atmosphere: Dry stone halls and painted walls under the desert, with large fans, torches and sliding doors.

Dangers: A Primal Construct is the temple's elite enemy, and wind from Large Fan Blades blocks passage until it dies down. The slate says the temple on Abdju Road, the approach to Deshret's territory, has collapsed pillars and has become a home for scorpions and lizards.

Quests: In An Introduction to Indoor Archaeology Tirzad's team (Jeht, her father Jebrael and Benben) camps at an oasis and enters the temple. Benben opens the first door by itself. The party lights Primal Torches to open further doors, reaches a mural, and a sliding wall reveals a rising path to the next stage, The Secret of Al-Ahmar.

Jebrael hands Tirzad's stone slate to the Traveler to use as a guide. Mirsad, Omid and Nachtigal remain behind at the oasis, and Jebrael buries part of the team's supplies as insurance before they go in.

Status as of 7.1: Open. Nothing found up to Version 7.1 changes the temple or answers the questions about its murals.

146.comment: Khemenu Temple: Benben and the Temple Doors
146.content: Benben, a strange three-cornered machine, earlier made the stone slate light up in Golden Slumber, and in the temple opens Khemenu Temple's first door by itself, with Jeht guessing it is drawn to the doors' triangular shape. Tirzad's professional scorn for Benben is a running joke.

147.content:
Lamb-Devourer Rock: Lamb-Devourer Rock is a desert rock formation in the Land of Upper Setekh, in the Great Red Sand of Sumeru. It conceals the secret base of the Thutmose, a group of Eremites.

The base is reached in the world quest Hidden Mercenaries, where the Traveler follows Soheil's old notes about a place where Thutmose would appear and vanish.

The quest has the Traveler learn the base's password by quietly following a patrolling Eremite, open the hidden door and search for valuables to bring back to Soheil.

Geography: A rock outcrop in the Land of Upper Setekh, with a hidden door that opens to a password-triggered device. The base lies behind it.

People: The Thutmose are Eremites who are devout believers of King Deshret. Seeking the secret of Al-Ahmar, they have gathered knowledge and collaborators from many sources, from Sumeru researchers to the Fatui. Jebrael and Samail were once called the twin blades of Thutmose. This is background from the Eremites' profile, not from the quest.

Paimon first assumes the hideout must be long abandoned but finds the Eremites still around, and notes that Soheil's notes say they would appear and disappear suddenly.

Quests: Hidden Mercenaries, in the Old Notes and New Friends chapter (part of Soheil's Wish), begins with Aaru Village. Steps: approach the rock, enter the secret base, look for valuables, hand slates to Soheil.

Dangers: Armed Eremites patrol the area; the quest uses stealth rather than direct combat.

Atmosphere: Tense and furtive: sun-baked rock hiding a secret base, with Eremites who patrol the surroundings.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 no change to the base was found.

No 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content was found that mentions the base. The quest's gameplay opens the hidden door by speaking a password, learned from an Eremite Axe Vanguard on patrol.

148.content:
Lambad's Tavern (also: Lambad Tavern): Lambad's Tavern is the main tavern and restaurant of Sumeru City, close to the lively Treasures Street. Its owner Lambad says he was a legendary sailor who sailed far and wide; the map description notes it is hard to tell how exaggerated that is, but the food makes the cuisine part of the claim believable. It sells food, ingredients and recipes.

Its signature dish is the Lambad Fish Roll, which Lambad says he devised in his youth by combining grilled fish he tasted in Mondstadt, Liyue and Inazuma with Sumeru's pitas.

Places: A ground-floor bar and dining room with an upstairs section. A noticeboard outside advertises a daily special and the line that a wonderful day starts with a drink.

The upstairs booth seating area was redesigned and refitted by Kaveh. After an accident in the tavern a few days earlier, the tableware was replaced: Kshahrewar researchers commissioned craftspeople to make it, and Haravatat researchers designed the patterns.

People: Lambad runs it. By day the researcher Jafar sits here; by night come the Corps of Thirty mercenary Hakan, the Eremite mercenary Lemta and, upstairs, the researchers Khaldun and Yavanani, the international student Gregor and the boat captain Shams.

After going bankrupt, Kaveh spent his time drinking here, where he met Alhaitham again and was invited to live with him.

Quests: No quest is set mainly here; it appears in the background of Kaveh's history with Alhaitham.

Atmosphere: Warm and talkative, smelling of grilled fish and fresh bread, with Lambad ready to tell a sailing tale.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tavern is open as before; the pages consulted record no later change. Players who reach Reputation Rank 4 in Sumeru get a 10% discount there.

Further details: Stock refreshes daily or weekly, depending on the item. The tavern's name in Chinese is Lambad Tavern. In his idle line Lambad says he went on his fair share of crazy adventures back in the day, and in dialogue he claims to have passed storms more wrathful than the Raiden Shogun and glaciers steelier than the Tsaritsa's heart.

149.content:
Land of Grounded Dreams: The Land of Grounded Dreams is the deepest part of Old Vanarana in the Lost Nursery, in Sumeru. It is the battlefield where the last war against Marana ended and where the Traveler defeats Marana's Avatar in the Aranyaka.

It is unlocked in the quest For All Children Who Long for Life, the third part of Nursery of Lost Dreams. After Marana's Avatar falls, Arama plants themselves here and becomes the new Ashvattha Tree.

The site is shown in two states, corrupted by the Withering and purified.

Geography: A cavern reached from the deepest part of Old Vanarana, after the earlier seal and nursery caves. It holds a small pool from which Marana's Avatar rises, and withering growths scattered around it.

The Withering's decay accumulates here as in the earlier quest, and Arama's protective aura lessens it for the Traveler.

People: Arama guides the Traveler here, saying the Withering has fully corroded the old place and that they can now resist Marana. Aramuhukunda, according to Arama, had turned into a Vasara Tree on this spot to suppress Marana's Avatar. Arakavi, Arapacati, Arapandu and Arana also appear in the quest.

Arama says Marana corroded the Vasara Tree that was meant to grow here and took its bodily form, and that if left unchecked Marana would eat away all life.

History: Arama says this is where the last war ended: Marana's Avatar was crushed and imprisoned with four seals. The Vasara Tree Aramuhukunda became was meant to hold it down.

In the Aranyaka, Marana's attempt to rise again meets the Traveler and Arama. Arama explains that destroying the avatar is needed so the new Ashvattha Tree may be born and the Bija formed.

Quests: For All Children Who Long for Life: follow Arama, destroy the tumors of the Withering in turn, defeat Marana's Avatar and its final form, then play the Rhythm of the Great Dream. Co-op is disabled for it.

Dangers: Marana's Avatar and rifthounds, with Decay from the Withering.

Atmosphere: Heavy and grieving, a site of an ended war, then a quiet place of planting once the avatar is gone.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the avatar is defeated and the new Ashvattha Tree grows from Arama; no later changes found.

The quest's trial battle limits the party to a level 80 version of the Traveler, and the site's achievement is The End of Annihilation. Both are gameplay details.

150.comment: Land of Grounded Dreams: Marana's Avatar
150.content: Marana's Avatar is the body Marana took by corroding the Vasara Tree in the Land of Grounded Dreams. The Traveler and Arama destroy the spirit containers (tumors of the Withering) to damage it, and then defeat it so the new Ashvattha Tree can be born.

151.content:
Land of Lower Setekh: The Land of Lower Setekh is the part of Sumeru's Great Red Sand where most people of the desert live. Its centre is Aaru Village, the largest human settlement in the desert, home to the followers and descendants of King Deshret and to scholars exiled from the Akademiya. It also holds Khaj-Nisut, King Deshret's throne-room temple, Abdju Pit, the abandoned hospital Dar al-Shifa and the hidden base of the real Temple of Silence.

Setekh echoes the Egyptian god Set, associated with deserts and storms. The area's official viewpoints are titled The Barren Land Where Sand Dances and Verdant Fields' Vantage Point.

Geography: Dunes and oases south of the Wall of Samiel and Caravan Ribat, with Aaru Village at its heart. Abdju Pit is a deep sinkhole at the sands' edge, Khaj-Nisut lies in ruins hidden under the sand, and Thamud Oasis is where the city of Saleh once stood. The Temple of Silence's real base is an underground temple near Thamud Oasis.

Aaru Village's water comes from an ancient stepwell below the village; the White Lift, an elevator built by a former Kshahrewar Village Keeper, lowers to the surface of the water; before it, one could reasonably draw about a bucketful at a time.

Places: Aaru Village, around an old fortress. Khaj-Nisut, once called the Eye of the Sands, the King's throne-room temple. Abdju Pit. Dar al-Shifa, a ruined hospital for Eleazar patients. The Temple of Silence, an underground temple. Thamud Oasis.

Official text for Khaj-Nisut says this is no place for ordinary mortals: only those who have been acknowledged may set foot there and gaze on the temple of King Deshret. It was unnamed on the map as the Eye of the Sands until The Secret of Al-Ahmar, and its throne-room ruins appear only after the three trials of Dreams Beneath the Searing Sand.

The fortress inside Aaru Village dates to the time of Gurabad and was built under a "paranoid prince" to guard the border between the desert and rainforest civilisations; a wiki item note identifies it as the Border Fort that appears as a chess piece in Safhe Shatranj, and it is the Village Chief's House today.

People: Aaru Village's people are followers and descendants of King Deshret together with exiled Akademiya scholars. Candace, whose companion story supplies one account of the village's origins, is associated with it; the Eremites, the Temple of Silence's members (including Cyno and, as its appointed leader, Sethos) and Kshahrewar Village Keepers all appear here.

Layla's blue hair and pointed ears mark a lineage descended from Tulaytullah's refugees. The Eremite tribes include Thutmose, whose secret base is in the neighbouring Land of Upper Setekh.

Governance: Aaru's founders swore off the rule of kings, and the old fortress now serves as the Village Chief's House. The Temple of Silence, which still exists as an independent body here, has begun re-establishing relations with the Akademiya after the events of Oathkeeper.

Culture: The founders named the village Aaru after the "ancient dream of the gods" and preserve the embers of Deshret's civilisation while awaiting the return of Al-Ahmar.

History: After King Deshret's death his civilisation broke into warring city-states, and refugees eventually left the desert to build Aaru. The founders were led by a blind poet of Tulaytullah. Candace's account is that the earliest inhabitants were survivors of the city of Akhtamun.

The Temple of Silence was founded by Hermanubis after the king's death and settled at Tulaytullah. Its members were betrayed by the city's elite and shunned by rainforest people, and about 400 years ago they set up the large underground temple near Thamud Oasis. In the Akademiya, the Temple later became a vestigial office responsible for custody and disposal of sensitive information.

Dangers: Sandstorms, ancient guardian constructs in the pit and temple, Eremite groups, the Fatui, and monsters such as spinocrocodiles and red vultures in the oases.

Travel: The route from the rainforest passes Caravan Ribat and the Wall of Samiel, then crosses the dunes to Aaru Village. Aaru Village is the base for expeditions elsewhere in the Great Red Sand.

Quests: Golden Slumber (3.1): Lost in the Sands, An Introduction to Indoor Archaeology, The Secret of Al-Ahmar and Dreams Beneath the Searing Sand. Also in this area: Cry From the Eleazar Hospital, Desert Bloom, Dual Evidence, Hidden Mercenaries, Sage of Sages, The Exile (Sprouting and Blooming), A Gifted Rose series, Warehousing Business and others (titles only).

Atmosphere: A refugee settlement of cautious, close-knit people around a fortress and a stepwell, ringed by red dunes.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Aaru Village and the surrounding ruins are open, and the Temple of Silence is again cooperating with the Akademiya.

Nothing from 6.x or 7.0-7.1 changes the area.

152.comment: Land of Lower Setekh: Aaru Village
152.content: The largest human settlement in the desert, home to followers and descendants of King Deshret and exiled Akademiya scholars. It is built around a Gurabad-era border fort and gets its water from a stepwell.

153.comment: Land of Lower Setekh: Dar al-Shifa
153.content: A now-abandoned hospital that specialised in treating Eleazar. Old notes suggest one doctor used patients as test subjects for dangerous treatments.

154.comment: Land of Lower Setekh: Temple of Silence base
154.content: An organisation keeping knowledge from King Deshret's era. The Akademiya office of that name is a remnant; the real Temple operates underground near Thamud Oasis.

155.content:
Land of Upper Setekh: The Land of Upper Setekh is a desert region in Sumeru's Great Red Sand, named because it lies in the direction of the sun at noon. Its landmark is the Valley of Dahri, where a giant Khaenri'ahn Ruin Golem sits among Akademiya research notes, and it also holds Lamb-Devourer Rock, the secret base of the Eremite tribe Thutmose.

"Setekh" is the Egyptian name of the god Set, associated with deserts, storms, disorder and foreigners. The region's world-quest series is thin: the only quest under its category is Afratu's Dilemma.

Geography: A rocky desert area with its own Statue of the Seven. A cavern north of the statue and a spot northeast of it hold parts of the Ruin Golem, with Akademiya reports left on them. The Valley of Dahri is a wind-eroded valley, and its viewpoint is titled The Giant of the Wind-Eroded Valley.

Common enemies in the valley include floating Anemo, stretchy Geo and whirling Pyro fungi, Dendro samachurls and hilichurl fighters. Elite enemies are Ruin Guards and Wooden Shieldwall Mitachurls, and the local specialty is the Scarab.

Places: The Valley of Dahri, with its Ruin Golem. Lamb-Devourer Rock, a Thutmose hideout reached in Hidden Mercenaries. The area's Statue of the Seven stands beside the cavern with the Ruin Golem's parts.

The Ruin Golem holds cockpit and arm passages. The wiki's Afratu's Dilemma steps have the Traveler enter the golem by hiding from its shots, pass through its arm, reach the cockpit and break three instances of Suda's Flow.

Burned medical records found in the valley describe sufferers of Eleazar with peeling skin, excess hair and severe facial ulceration, some with language impairment, and say the first cases received centralised treatment on orders from above.

People: Eremites of the Thutmose tribe hide at Lamb-Devourer Rock; a character named Afratu appears in the world quest, and its first step is to talk to a researcher. Hilichurls (called Majuj by desert people) roam the valley.

Akademiya investigators left notes here, and the wiki lists them as an earlier team of researchers; one hidden page is attributed to Zandik.

History: Akademiya reports found at the Ruin Golem record the team studying the machine, medical reports on the Majuj and on Eleazar sufferers, and an order from the Temple of Silence that all machines from Khaenri'ah be sealed in the format of the Revelatory Monument. Suda's Flow is the sages' name for a perturbation of elemental veins used as a seal.

One torn page, attributed to Zandik, says the machine's weapons could be repaired from salvaged parts and calls Suda's Flow nothing but sediment from elemental disturbance, which he finds laughable as a seal. The researcher hid the page and kept his measurements quiet from other team members.

Dangers: Ruin Guards, Mitachurls, fungi, the golem itself in the quest, and Eremite hideouts. Desert exposure is the general risk.

Travel: The region is part of the Great Red Sand and is reached overland from its other lands; the Statue of the Seven is the local waypoint.

Quests: Afratu's Dilemma (3.1) starts at the Valley of Dahri: the Traveler helps a researcher enter the Ruin Golem and breaks the Suda's Flow seals. Hidden Mercenaries (part of Old Notes and New Friends) leads to Lamb-Devourer Rock, where the Traveler enters Thutmose's base, finds valuables and hands slates to Soheil.

Atmosphere: Wind-carved rock and the silent bulk of a machine from a vanished kingdom, with notes and burned records scattered in the sand.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the region is an open desert area with its Ruin Golem still immobile.

Nothing from 6.x or 7.0-7.1 changes it.

156.comment: Land of Upper Setekh: Valley of Dahri
156.content: A wind-eroded valley with a giant Ruin Golem. Akademiya investigators left reports on the machine, medical notes on the Majuj and on Eleazar sufferers, and a hidden note from Zandik about the Khaenri'ahn machine and elemental flows.

157.comment: Land of Upper Setekh: Lamb-Devourer Rock
157.content: The secret base of the Eremite tribe Thutmose, found during the world quest Hidden Mercenaries.

158.content:
Liloupar's Cell (also: Liloupar's Gaol, Jinni's prison): Liloupar's Cell is a ruined prison in Safhe Shatranj, in the Desert of Hadramaveth, where the most dominant fragment of the Jinni Liloupar was kept. Its viewpoint calls it a prison that has become an oasis: a green spot with a big tree and a river. In The Temple Where Sand Flows Like Tears the Traveler and Jeht find a bottle here, and when it is touched the plants wither and Liloupar's voice speaks from it.

Liloupar is the Jinni who destroyed Gurabad in revenge across three generations. King Deshret split her into seven fragments and had divine sages hide them in the Great Red Sand; this cell held the strongest one.

Geography: A small ruin opposite the square of the Gurabad temple, in the canyon the Tanit call the Great Rift. Before the bottle is touched it is a lush spot with a big tree beside a river. A viewpoint here is named Liloupar's Gaol. Afterward its look changes and the oasis is withered.

It is one of several places in Safhe Shatranj, which also holds a chessboard field the desert tribes call by that name, scattered obelisks with inscriptions, and ruined temples. Researchers think Safhe Shatranj was once a training field for ancient war machines.

People: Liloupar speaks from the bottle as the Mother of the Jinn, a title she mocks. She is proud, theatrical and sharp-tongued, and calls Jeht a sand-licking lackey before warming to her. She says she could take any shape to please her master if her soul were not sundered. She offers her true name to the Traveler, whom she calls her lord, and declines to serve the Tanit matriarch.

Jeht recognises the name from tribal books and fears the contract, since a Jinni's true name lets a human command her and the tales say the Jinn eventually take vengeance. Liloupar scoffs that hate is too strong a word, as one does not hate a poisonous insect or toad, and says she likes the Traveler. Her fragment is a pair of orbs in a floating bottle in the present day.

History: Liloupar was born from water lilies in the streams that followed Nabu Malikata's footsteps, lived in Ay-Khanoum, and served King Deshret after Nabu Malikata died. She aided the shepherd Ormazd in founding Gurabad, fell in love with him, and when he became a tyrant she cursed his house with three generations of ruin. The city finally fell to an abyssal calamity. Deshret punished her by splitting her soul.

The cell therefore belongs to the aftermath of the fall of Gurabad. Jeht has read in tribal books of a wicked spirit named Liloupar who drowned Ormazd and his household in honey; the fuller account is in the Gurabad entry. Other fragments turn up elsewhere, as at Mt. Damavand and through the chessboard of Safhe Shatranj.

Other names for her appear in the texts. She is called the Mother of the Despicable in a quest, Daughter of the Water Lily in the tale of Shiruyeh and Shirin, and Jinn-Mother in a record of the ancient oases. The wiki notes that the spelling Liloufar survives in that book while newer texts use Liloupar.

Dangers: A Primal Construct guardian, Anoushbord - Forgotten Mechanical Guardian, attacks as the party reaches the bottle. Beyond the cell, in Pairidaeza Canyon, the party meets an opposing band of Eremites.

Quests: The Temple Where Sand Flows Like Tears (The Dirge of Bilqis, part 2) takes the Traveler here. After the bottle is claimed, the series continues with Dune-Entombed Fecundity, where more of her soul is collected, and Memories of Gurabad, where Liloupar parts from the party to face the Abyssal power she once released. The bottle stays with the Traveler as a gadget that does what it did when Liloupar was inside.

Status as of 7.1: Withered and quiet. Liloupar's fragment no longer lies here, and the bottle that held it stayed with the Traveler.

159.content: King Deshret split the Jinni into seven fragments after the fall of Gurabad, and divine sages hid them in the Great Red Sand. The Traveler gathers them across The Dirge of Bilqis and Memories of Gurabad, and her magic bottle becomes a gadget with the benefits she once gave.

key: Your Past Is Like a Garden
160.content: By the events of A Divergence Leading to Oneself (Luna VII, Version 6.6) Liloupar is awake again and calms the Jinn and sandstorms the Fatui disturbed before travelling with the Traveler's group across Sumeru. In Your Past Is Like a Garden she asks Collei, who carries remnants of Nabu Malikata, to let her absorb them; Collei agrees, and Liloupar fades away to rest content.

161.content:
Lokapala Jungle: The Lokapala Jungle is the northern, coastal stretch of Sumeru's Dharma Forest. It begins at the enormous glowing mushrooms of Mawtiyima Forest, runs past Chatrakam Cave and the extravagant Palace of Alcazarzaray, and ends near Bayda Harbor, the port that looks across the water to Fontaine. Its name is Sanskrit for "guardian of the world".

Mawtiyima Forest is the jungle's best-known place: an area of fluorescent mushrooms whose official description calls it the forest defending northern Sumeru, once tainted by filth that corroded the whole world and later purified.

Geography: The area spans the north coast of the Dharma Forest, starting at Mawtiyima Forest, near Minlin and Chenyu Vale, and ending on the western slope of a nameless mountain west of Bayda Harbor, where it meets the Desert of Hadramaveth and the Realm of Farakhkert. Local specialties are Rukkhashava Mushrooms, Kalpalata Lotus, Nilotpala Lotus and Padisarah.

Mawtiyima Forest's monumental fluorescent mushrooms form a canopy of light that hides the sun and moon; the Electro Regisvine is its normal boss. Chatrakam Cave, a fungus-filled cave system, lies deeper in, with the Realm of Khab entered from it.

Places: Mawtiyima Forest, the glowing mushroom forest. Chatrakam Cave, the damp cavern. The Palace of Alcazarzaray, a lavish palace in the woods owned by Dori and designed by Kaveh. Bayda Harbor, the coastal port facing Fontaine.

The Palace of Alcazarzaray is shown with a purple garden before it, where flowers dance and warblers sing; a viewpoint (Memory of Alcazarzaray) frames it as a setting for a lovely encounter. Bayda Harbor is directly across from Fontaine, according to the quest Recollections of a Fontainian.

People: Aranara live in the forest, hard for most adults to see. At Bayda Harbor the NPCs include Shajar, the Port Master; Adel, a Mahamata; and Honorine, a Fontaine engineer. Eremites, hilichurls, Fatui and treasure hoarders also turn up.

The merchant Dori owns the palace, and the architect Kaveh designed it, which ties both to the jungle. The Vanara, who consider mushroom picking a duty, are the main people who enter Chatrakam Cave.

History: The Palace of Alcazarzaray was Kaveh's commission from Dori, who asked only that it be large and extravagant. Late in construction the Withering spread overnight, wrecked the worksite and made it unsalvageable. Dori did not want to continue, but Kaveh had invested too much and took a loan from Dori to rebuild it, which left him heavily in debt. It is regarded as his masterpiece.

Mawtiyima Forest, according to official text, was tainted by the filth that corroded the whole world and then revivified and purified. The Mawtiyima energy form is said to fight the Withering to keep the forest healthy and to communicate with the Aranara.

Dangers: Mushrooms of many kinds, including poisonous ones, floating and other fungi, Mirror Maidens, Fatui Cicin Mages and Fatui Pyro Agents, treasure hoarders, Eremites, hilichurls, and the Electro Regisvine.

Mawtiyima Forest is where the Withering shows up in its exploration features (the wiki lists The Withering among the forest's exploration objects).

Mawtiyima's other exploration features include Valaya floating-ring puzzles, Tri-Yana Seeds, Stone Pillar Seals, a Seed Mirror, a Phantasmal Gate, Auspicious Branches and bouncy mushrooms; poisonous mushrooms grow in the forest, and a viewpoint named Aranaga's Little Garden carries the line "Here, the pomegranate sings and the apples clap."

Travel: Bayda Harbor connects Sumeru's coast to Fontaine by sea. Overland, Mawtiyima Forest is the way toward the northern border near Minlin and Chenyu Vale.

Quests: The Risen Moon Chapter (Archon Quest) enters the Realm of Khab via Chatrakam Cave. World quests listed in the wiki category include Aranakin's Old Friend, Aranaga's Memory, Aragaru's Drawing, Garcia's Paean, Wealthy Merchant, For a Dream I Tarry and Memory's Final Chapter; only their titles were reviewed.

Atmosphere: Dense and luminous, with mushroom canopies glowing overhead and a humid forest floor. Mawtiyima's grass seems to glow as if the place were aware of visitors.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the jungle is open to explore and nothing in later story content has altered it.

Nothing from 6.x or 7.0-7.1 changes the area.

162.content: Dori owns this lavish palace, which Kaveh designed. Dori asked only for something large and extravagant, giving Kaveh near-total freedom. When the Withering destroyed the worksite near completion, Kaveh borrowed from Dori to rebuild, leaving him deeply in debt.

163.content: A forest of enormous fluorescent mushrooms in northern Sumeru. Mawtiyima is described as an energy form born of the forest's ancient dreams and memories that fights the Withering and can apparently speak with the Aranara.

164.content: A harbour town across the water from Fontaine, with a Port Master (Shajar), a Mahamata (Adel) and a Fontainian engineer (Honorine) among its residents.

165.content:
Lost Nursery (also: Nursery of Lost Dreams): The Lost Nursery is a small area in Sumeru's Dharma Forest that contains Old Vanarana, the Aranara's home for hundreds of years before the Cataclysm. It is unlocked in the Aranyaka world quest series, Part III ("Nursery of Lost Dreams"), when the Traveler, Paimon and the Aranara Arama enter to destroy Marana's Avatar. Before that the area is choked by the Withering.

Old Vanarana is where the Aranara fought the invaders of the Cataclysm and afterwards sealed away a piece of Marana, the force of death. The seals weakened with time, so the dying Fane of Ashvattha, the Aranara's tree-shrine, could no longer bear Bija, the fruit. Reaching the avatar in the heart of Old Vanarana, defeating it, and planting a new Ashvattha there is the entire story of the area.

The ending costs the Aranara dearly: Arama becomes the new Ashvattha Tree, and Arana gives away its memories to form the Bija, so afterwards Arana does not remember the Traveler.

Geography: The Lost Nursery lies in the Dharma Forest and, as of 3.0, was the smallest area in the game. Old Vanarana is its subarea; below it lie the underground chambers where the seals were kept. Before the quest "For Fruits, Seeds, and Trees" is finished, stepping into the area is treated as out of bounds, and Paimon pulls the Traveler back.

Notable spots are Sand-Embraced Home (reached by going down from the north teleport waypoint of Old Vanarana) and the Land of Grounded Dreams at the bottom of the tunnel, where Marana's Avatar lies. A viewpoint in the Archive for Old Vanarana is hidden until a later Aranyaka quest is complete.

Places: Old Vanarana is the main settlement ruin; the tunnel beneath it was drained of sand by Arama; Sand-Embraced Home is the last chamber, guarded by Aramuhukunda himself; the Land of Grounded Dreams is where Marana's Avatar is destroyed and where Arama is later planted.

According to the wiki's lore page, seals included an entrance called the Door of Vana linking the Fane of Ashvattha to Old Vanarana; three Inscriptions of Remembrance made by Aramaha, Arayama and Araji, who later became Vasara Trees; several Ararakalari (Aranara mystic arts) such as Healthy Dendrograna, Claustroflora and Stone Pillar Seals; and the final one at Sand-Embraced Home.

People: Arama, the Aranara who befriended the Traveler in Vanarana, leads the descent and eventually becomes the new Ashvattha Tree. Aramuhukunda, the first Aranara "born" and the one the Traveler met at the festival, guards the final seal and opens it when he sees the quest is to destroy Marana's Avatar. Arana appears with Arama at the end.

Aramaha, Arayama, Araji and Aradasha are named as creators of earlier seals. Marana's Avatar itself is a quest-exclusive boss; the Aranara regard Marana as the voice that says all good things must vanish.

History: The Aranara lived in Old Vanarana, created by the Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, for hundreds of years before the Cataclysm. When invaders from the Abyss came, they fought them there, and ruin machines still litter the old tunnels. Afterwards the Aranara moved to a new Vanarana, hid it in a dream, and sealed Marana's Avatar deep under Old Vanarana with four layers of seals.

Over time Marana's corrosion leaked out regardless, producing the Withering that gradually weakened the Fane of Ashvattha and made it unable to bear Bija. In Aranyaka Part III the Traveler and Arama broke the seals and reached the Land of Grounded Dreams.

In "For Fruits, Seeds, and Trees," Arama guides the Traveler and Paimon to the Fane of Ashvattha, which is weakened, and they enter its dream and remove a Withering Zone; after they give it Vasoma Fruits the Fane tells Arama to make the ultimate sacrifice. In "For the Children of the Past" Arama shields the party from the Withering, they break seals by finding three Inscriptions of Remembrance and burning seven Stone Pillar Seals, then Arama drains the sand from a huge tunnel; a Ruin Grader attacks at the bottom and Arama binds it. In "For All Children Who Long for Life" Marana's Avatar moves its soul into Withering Zones three times; each is destroyed, and the core is destroyed for good. Arama then dives into the ground to become a sapling, and Arana, who is giving up its memories, asks the Traveler who they are once the Bija forms. The rhythm of the Great Dream is played again to make the Bija grow.

Atmosphere: Before it is cleared, the nursery is a withered, silent, dangerous hollow; afterwards the old Vanarana begins to rejuvenate, slowly and quietly, with a young tree and an echo of a village that once rang with Aranara songs.

Dangers: Before Part III the Withering here is among the strongest in the game (tied with Mawtiyima, starting at four bars of its gauge). Enemies in Old Vanarana include hilichurls, shooters and berserkers, slimes, Stretchy Pyro Fungus, Rockfond and Thundercraven Rifthounds, Blazing Axe Mitachurl and Ruin Guards, plus Ruin Machines left from the Cataclysm.

Travel: The route in is through the Dharma Forest; before the quest series the area is blocked by the game's out-of-bounds rule. The Aranara protect travelers with a shield during the descent.

Quests: Aranyaka Part III, "Nursery of Lost Dreams": "For Fruits, Seeds, and Trees," "For the Children of the Past," and "For All Children Who Long for Life" (3.0). The wiki shows a later Archive viewpoint for Old Vanarana that appears only after a later Aranyaka quest.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Marana's Avatar is gone, Old Vanarana is slowly renewing, and Arama grows as the new Ashvattha Tree, though traces of the Withering remain.

Arana lost memories of the Traveler and of Rana and the children of Vimara Village in order to make the Bija.

166.content: Marana's Avatar is the physical form of Marana (death, in the Aranara's telling) that the Aranara imprisoned in Old Vanarana after the Cataclysm. It attacks with Withering waves and lasers and moves its soul into Withering Zones; the Traveler and Arama destroy those zones and then the core. Its destruction means the Withering cannot form significantly again, though traces remain.

167.content: Sand-Embraced Home is the deepest chamber of Old Vanarana, where Aramuhukunda guarded the final seal. He opens it for the Traveler and Arama so they can face Marana's Avatar.

168.content:
Madinat al-Nuhas (also: City of Brass): Madinat al-Nuhas is an underground Khaenri'ahn complex beneath the Samudra Coast in the northwest of Sumeru's desert, once used to test weapons, above all Ruin Machines. It is powered by Azosite like Hangeh Afrasiyab and contains an unfinished prototype Ruin Golem. The Traveler reaches it in As the Khvarena's Light Shows: Nirodha.

Nasejuna calls it the proving ground of the Dahrians, and an order found inside shows it was used to hold off the monsters of the cataclysm.

Geography: The entrance is at the west end of Asipattravana Swamp, behind vines marked by a Mysterious Amrita Seal and a mechanical door. The facility extends under Samudra Coast, a sandy shore with clear blue water on the far northwest border of the Sumeru desert. Its interior shares the industrial, brass-coloured feel of the Ruin Golems and the Azosite factory.

The ruin has a control centre with relays, a left-hand door that leads to the proving ground, and a chamber with a Ruin Cannon. The Golem is an incomplete prototype, and the Great Song of Khvarena is said to lie within it.

History: A testing facility for Ruin Machines in the days of Khaenri'ah. According to Nasejuna's copied records, it was later altered into fortifications from which monsters could be attacked, but this saw little use. A surviving order from Garrison Commander Hadura of the Schwanenritter reads that workshops and similar areas were unsuited to the large-scale operations of the Mechanical Wardens, so he commands the self-defence systems to be activated and survivors evacuated to the surface before resistance continues.

Azosite energy blocks power the machines; the Traveler must find and install them to bring the facility to life. Nasejuna says the Schwanenritter owned this proving ground and the Azosite factory at Hangeh Afrasiyab alike.

Nasejuna points out the oddity that the Dahrians, who set off the defiling disaster, built machines to fight monsters; the quest leaves it unanswered. Engineering notes at Hangeh Afrasiyab add that Azosite alloys were meant to clear the energy-efficiency bottleneck of the large Mechanical Wardens, which links power research there to the machines tested here.

Atmosphere: Metal corridors, brass-coloured machinery and old relays: a place built to test weapons rather than to live in.

Dangers: Ruin Guards, Ruin Cruisers, Ruin Destroyers, Ruin Defenders and a Ruin Drake: Skywatch rise in waves when the proving ground's systems are woken. The Golem prototype's core must be destroyed with the Ruin Cannon.

Quests: As the Khvarena's Light Shows: Nirodha is one of the three subquests of the series Khvarena of Good and Evil. Nasejuna and Sorush lead the Traveler and Paimon through the gate, and by powering the circuits, defeating the defence waves and firing the Ruin Cannon the party reaches the Great Song of Khvarena stored in the Golem. The quest earns the achievement Behold My Righteous Strike! at one stage.

Nasejuna says it is his first time inside a Dahrian ruin; he has the notes called Rene's Investigation Notes as his guide. A Luxurious Chest can be found after the Golem is opened.

Status as of 7.1: Abandoned and quiet. Nothing found up to Version 7.1 changes the site.

169.content: A tattered note on the left side of the proving ground chamber is an order from Garrison Commander Hadura of the Schwanenritter. It tells the reader to activate the self-defence systems and quickly evacuate the survivors upward while the Mechanical Wardens, the Khaenri'ahn name for the Ruin Golems, carry on the fight.

170.content:
Mawtiyima Forest (also: Mawtiyima): Mawtiyima Forest is a forest of enormous fluorescent mushrooms at the start of Sumeru's Lokapala Jungle, in the Dharma Forest. Giant mushroom caps form a canopy of light that hides the sun and moon. The forest is guarded by Mawtiyima, an energy form made of its ancient dreams and memories, and it is the home of Aranaga's little garden, where the Aranara tend their friends the flora and fungi.

Its monumental plants grow nowhere else. The Expedition text calls it the dense forest that defends northern Sumeru, once tainted by the filth that corroded the entire world and only returned to its giant form after much revivification and purification.

The Aranara and Mawtiyima appear to communicate. In the world quest "The Final Chapter" (3.0), the last part of the Agnihotra Sutra series, the Traveler helps three Aranara cleanse the forest's heart of the Withering.

Geography: Lokapala Jungle begins here, close to Minlin and to Chenyu Vale's Southern Mountain, and runs along the north coast of the Dharma Forest toward the west slope of a nameless mountain near Bayda Harbor, where it joins the Desert of Hadramaveth and the Realm of Farakhkert. Inside the forest, under the fungal caps, lies the hidden Mawtiyima point.

Wiki-listed features include the hovering Valaya rings, Tri-Yana Seeds, Stone Pillar Seals, Seed Mirrors, bouncy mushrooms, poisonous mushrooms and Phantasmal Gates; local specialties are Rukkhashava Mushrooms and Kalpalata Lotus. A viewpoint at Aranaga's little garden is described as a place where "the pomegranate sings and the apples clap."

People: Aranaga, Aranakin and Aragaru, three Aranara, tend the forest. Aranaga calls the Mawtiyima Forest his garden and says Mawtiyima protects it and its flora and mushroom friends. Khayyam, an NPC who camps in the forest, cannot recall something he is trying to remember and is thankful that the forest has been revived.

The Aranara speak in a halting, childlike manner and call the Traveler "Nara"; for them Mawtiyima is a being they protect and are protected by. Memory is central to them: they say a new life is nourished by memory, that death is only a loss of memory, and that what they have lived through will be forgotten but will remain in the soil and roots of the forest.

History: The Aranara's tale says that in the first moon the fungi woke, in the second the branches, and in the third the flowers, until Marana crept out of the moons' shadows and devoured Mawtiyima. The forest was later healed with the help of the Traveler and the Aranara's Kusava, a seed-and-fruit carrying the Aranara's memories and power.

In The Final Chapter the Traveler and Paimon follow Aranaga to find the Yajna Grass, perform the Arahaoma ritual under the moon, and offer the elixir to Jamikayomars, which unlocks the entrance to Mawtiyima. Inside, they destroy three Withering Branches and then a last Tumor of the Withering after fighting fungal beasts, using the Kusava's power of dreams. Afterwards, the three Aranara stay with the awakened Mawtiyima, which has stories to tell them.

Nara Varuna, a mysterious person who keeps a place in the memories of many Aranara, is said to have left behind the energy that feeds the forest. The Aranara plan to meet the Traveler again at the Festival Utsava, and Aranakin gives them a song so they will not be forgotten.

Dangers: Slimes, fungi, hilichurls, Treasure Hoarders and Eremites roam; the elite enemies include Fatui Cicin Mages, Mirror Maidens and Fatui Pyro Agents, and an Electro Regisvine is the area boss. Before the cleansing, the Withering in the forest was among the strongest in the game.

Quests: "The Final Chapter" (3.0) is the main quest here. After "Memory's Final Chapter" a hidden quest has the Traveler speak to Khayyam the next day at his camp, where he thanks them for the forest's revival and gives them a gift. "Homecoming" (a 3.6 Nahida story quest) also mentions a group of fungi found near Mawtiyima Forest, one of which Nahida revives.

Atmosphere: Glowing grass, giant caps that block sun and moon, and a sense that the forest knows you have arrived. Paimon remarks on entering that the grass is glowing and that the place feels aware of them.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the forest is healthy and open. The Withering was driven out in The Final Chapter, though the memory of that struggle is fading for the Aranara.

171.content: An energy form created by the forest's ancient dreams and memories. It keeps the forest alive, fights the Withering and appears to communicate with the Aranara, who treat it as a she. Paimon's "Morty Arena" is a mispronunciation, not a name. In the ancient tongue the name meant "human death." Its inner place is sealed until The Final Chapter, when the Arahaoma is offered to Jamikayomars.

172.content:
Mt. Damavand (also: Mount Damavand, Damavand): Mt. Damavand is the huge hollow mountain at the centre of the Desert of Hadramaveth in Sumeru's Great Red Sand. A massive tornado whirls over its middle, and the sandstorm around it never stops. In the lost language of the desert dwellers its name means "the mountain from which smoke and ash arise". Beneath it lie the Orchard of Pairidaeza, also called the Eternal Oasis, and ancient palaces and pipelines.

Wandering desert tribes believe the Eternal Oasis is hidden inside; they are right. The mountain is explored in the world-quest chain "The Dirge of Bilqis" (3.4).

The Celestial Nail page connects the great crater, the withered Irminsul beside the Eternal Oasis, and the permanent central tornado with a nail that fell here and desertified a once-lush land. In Nahida's story quest "Homecoming" (3.6) the Dendro Dragon Apep is revealed to live in that storm.

Geography: Wadi Al-Majuj, a canyon area, lies south of the mountain, and the Passage of Ghouls connects that wadi to the Sands of Al-Azif. The loading screen says the mountain is surrounded by countless complex and crumbling gullies and canyons spreading in all directions. Underneath it are ancient palaces and intricate pipelines "where the age-old dreams of the gods and their servants are buried".

The Orchard of Pairidaeza can be entered only through Deshret's Glass Goblet, a chamber below the mountain whose central platform is the oasis's entrance; Bayt Al-Hayah, the "House of Life", is a cavern network beneath Wounded Shin Valley that leads into it. The Orchard holds a withered Irminsul tree beside its central island and three chairs for the three God-Kings of Sumeru.

History: Legend says King Deshret found a divine nail and used its power and the Jinn to build the Eternal Oasis here as a cemetery for the Goddess of Flowers, Nabu Malikata, freezing a single moment of her world in place forever. Water, animals and trees are all held motionless, and the water can be walked on. The oasis and its machines were kept by the great Jinni Ferigees.

The Records of Mt. Damavand are broken tablets that become readable as the Traveler fixes pipes in the quest "Dune-Entombed Fecundity". They tell of a priesthood worried that the Orchard's water output was falling and the outer oases shrinking, that Lady Ferigees was growing weaker and no longer answered calls, and that sand now clogged the pipes. Jinn fragments implanted in the machinery made irrigation efficient, yet the priests wondered whether the Jinn also age. Ferigees refused large-scale repairs because they would disturb the Goddess of Flowers' tomb.

Legend says Ferigees destroyed herself to protect the city of Gurabad. A later loading screen says she has fully dissipated, and that the Orchard is likewise heading for an inevitable end. An older text claims her slumber continues in the depths; the two accounts conflict (see uncertainties).

Dangers: Caravans vanish in the sandstorms, so few are willing to visit this desert. Damaged Records found in the Passage of Ghouls tell of an investigation team that ran out of food and water while looking for the path to the Eternal Oasis and finally prayed to the Goddess of Flowers to carry their souls there. Inside the mountain are Geo fungi and ancient mechanisms.

The Traveler's route down the mountain, in "Dune-Entombed Fecundity: Part I", involves an abandoned Eremite camp, mysterious mechanisms and junction puzzles, and fights with Stretchy Geo Fungi and Geoshrooms.

Quests: "The Dirge of Bilqis" (3.4) leads the Traveler, with Jeht, Azariq, Babel and the Jinn Liloupar, down into the mountain. "The Eternal Dream, Ever Lush" has the Traveler visit the Eternal Oasis with Jeht. In "Homecoming" (3.6), Nahida and the Traveler go to the sandstorm to speak to Apep.

Atmosphere: A permanent storm around a hollow mountain; deep below, the Eternal Oasis is frozen in a single moment, with even its water held still.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the mountain still sits in its storm. Apep, the Dendro Dragon, remains in it.

Ferigees is gone, and the Eternal Oasis is no longer hidden from the Traveler.

173.comment: Mt. Damavand: Apep in the Storm
173.content: In "Homecoming" (3.6), after Nahida learns that fungi she has been reviving were once elemental lifeforms living inside Apep, she and the Traveler cross the Desert of Hadramaveth to the sandstorm. Apep notices them at once, emerges, and tells them to leave, rejecting Nahida's claim of coming to heal her; she calls both Nahida and Amun no different, being gods who lean on the glow of the heavens. The wiki says one nail fell over this mountain and turned its forests into the Great Red Sand, from which Apep and her children survived.

174.comment: Mt. Damavand: The Orchard of Pairidaeza
174.content: An enclosed garden under Mt. Damavand, built by King Deshret on a divine nail as a memorial to the Goddess of Flowers, with everything in it frozen. Entered only through Deshret's Glass Goblet. Three chairs stand at its centre for Sumeru's three God-Kings, with abbreviated names in Deshret Script; one chair carries the name of Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, which the world has otherwise lost. The name Pairidaeza is Avestan for an enclosed garden.

175.content:
Old Vanarana (also: Nursery of Lost Dreams, Vanarana of the past): Old Vanarana is the original home of the Aranara, the small forest spirits of Sumeru, lying below the Fane of Ashvattha in the Lost Nursery of Dharma Forest. It was their home for hundreds of years before the cataclysm. Afterward the Aranara sealed Marana's Avatar in its depths. The Withering engulfs it at first, stronger than in most places, until the Traveler and Arama destroy the Avatar in the Aranyaka quest Nursery of Lost Dreams.

The path in is the Door of Vana, the gate from the Fane of Ashvattha, which the quest opens. After the Avatar's destruction Old Vanarana begins to regrow.

Geography: A subarea of the Lost Nursery in Dharma Forest, with a purified and a corrupted version, the latter shown on the map as withered. It is unlocked in For Fruits, Seeds, and Trees. Arama later drains the sand from a chamber, revealing a massive tunnel.

The ruin has a chamber with seven Stone Pillar Seals, a massive tunnel full of scattered Ruin Machines, and a deep place called the Land of Grounded Dreams where Marana's Avatar waits. Sand-Embraced Home, where the last seal was guarded, lies within.

People: Old Vanarana belongs to the Aranara. The friendly Aranara Arama is the Traveler's guide. Aramuhukunda, the first Aranara and a Vasara Tree, appears to unlock the last seal.

Three Aranara, Aramaha, Arayama and Araji, made Inscriptions of Remembrance for the first seal and later became Vasara Trees in Ashvattha's Concourses. Aradasha's Stone Pillar Seals, Aramaha's Healthy Dendrograna and Arayama's Claustroflora help to form the third seal through Ararakalari.

History: After the cataclysm the Aranara locked Marana's Avatar deep in Old Vanarana with four layers of seals. The first was the Door of Vana, the gate between the Fane of Ashvattha and the ruin. The second was three Inscriptions of Remembrance. The third was a set of Ararakalari, including Healthy Dendrograna, Claustroflora and Stone Pillar Seals. The fourth was at Sand-Embraced Home, guarded by Aramuhukunda himself.

Over time Marana's corrosion leaked out despite the seals. In Nursery of Lost Dreams the Traveler and Arama undo all four seals and enter the Land of Grounded Dreams, and the Aranara tell how they fiercely fought the cataclysm's invaders. Ruin Machines and riftwolves in the tunnel are remnants of that invasion.

Marana's Avatar tries to hide its soul in three Withering Zones, each of which has to be cleared before its core can be destroyed. Afterward Arama dives into the ground as a sapling and becomes the new Ashvattha Tree, removing the Withering from Old Vanarana. The Traveler and Paimon play the Rhythm of the Great Dream again to let a Bija fruit form; Arama has forgotten them. The viewpoint of the Nursery of Lost Dreams appears only after a later quest, 'Hello,' 'Thank You,' and the Final 'Goodbye'.

Atmosphere: Before the quest: a withered ruin under sand, choked by the Withering. Afterward: a place that begins to recover, as the viewpoint's text says, 'like a stream purifying itself or a withered tree sprouting once more.'

Dangers: Hilichurls, Mitachurls, slimes, Rockfond Rifthounds and Thundercraven Rifthounds, and Ruin Guards roam. A Ruin Grader activates at the tunnel's bottom and proves unusually resilient until Arama binds it. The Withering is stronger here than in most places, so Arama shields the group from its effects.

Quests: Nursery of Lost Dreams is the third part of the Aranyaka world quest series, in three quests: For Fruits, Seeds, and Trees; For the Children of the Past; and For All Children Who Long for Life. The Traveler and Arama break the seals, defeat Marana's Avatar and plant the new Ashvattha Tree here.

Arama goes ahead with a shield against the Withering. In the third quest the Avatar moves its soul among three Withering Zones before being destroyed for good.

Status as of 7.1: Purified and recovering. Marana is gone for the foreseeable future, though traces of the Withering remain.

No later change is recorded up to Version 7.1.

176.content: Marana's Avatar is the embodiment of the Withering that the Aranara sealed in Old Vanarana after the cataclysm. In Nursery of Lost Dreams it attacks the party and relocates its soul to different Withering Zones. When all three are cleared the Traveler destroys its core.

177.content:
Opet Hall: Opet Hall is an underground chamber just north of the Mausoleum of King Deshret in Sumeru's Hypostyle Desert. The Traveler enters it in the world quest The Secret of Al-Ahmar, part of Golden Slumber.

The Scarlet Sand Slate describes it as a place where many blessings gathered that reached King Deshret's throne directly, and where the devout won the right to the throne room. Its name recalls the Opet Festival of ancient Thebes.

Geography: Lies north of the Mausoleum, with a lower level reached through tunnels on either side of the main entrance. Its south side appears to join the Great Hall of Truths, but that way cannot be used and visitors must come through Duat Hall.

The hall has the usual King Deshret ruin machinery: primal torches and sconces, primal embers, primal obelisks, sacred seals, an Everlight Cell, a Plinth of the Secret Rites, a verity cell and a primal sandglass.

History: In The Secret of Al-Ahmar, Tirzad's expedition (Jeht, Jebrael, Benben and the Traveler) works through the Mausoleum. After being separated, they learn Benben has been taken. The Traveler fights Samail and the Fatui and recovers it, then goes deeper through the ruins, lighting torches to open the way. The wiki places this last stretch of the quest in Opet Hall.

A rock wall breaks to reveal a Primal Construct, and a second symbol lights on the Scarlet Sand Slate, projecting a map. Tirzad reads the inscriptions as praise meant to whitewash Deshret's rule, a position that contradicts what he said earlier. The group then agrees to get back to the oasis camp where Nachtigal's merchants were left.

Atmosphere: Hot, echoing stone, torchlight and pale sand dust. The mood in the quest is half academic bickering, half unease at being followed by Fatui and Eremites.

Dangers: Listed enemies are Eremites, Fatui Skirmishers, Fatui Cicin Mages and Primal Constructs.

Quests: The Secret of Al-Ahmar is the third part of Golden Slumber. The hall also features in the Chessboard of Safhe Shatranj.

During the quest Samail, who calls himself of the Thutmose, speaks to Jebrael as an old comrade, and Jeht learns that her father was once one of the Thutmose; Jebrael says Samail killed Jeht's mother. These conversations belong to the quest and to Jebrael and Samail's entries rather than to the hall.

Status as of 7.1: Open to explore as of Version 7.1.

No source up to Version 7.1 that I checked changes it.

178.content:
Overgrown Valley: The Overgrown Valley is a green, canyon-like subarea of the Veluriyam Mirage, the bottle-shaped domain from the limited-time Version 3.8 event Secret Summer Paradise. It is the home of the Choo-Choo Cart rail line and its three keepers, the brothers Ferdinand, Jeroney and Haddo. It existed only as an event area and is not part of the permanent map.

The valley is reached in Act I of the event, when Klee mentions that a giant canyon has appeared where the group was investigating. Its attractions are built around rails: carts powered by Hydro Eidolons run through it, and a thrill ride called the Torrential Twister is its centrepiece.

Geography: A valley of vines, hills and cave mouths inside the Mirage, crossed by rail tracks and junctions for the Choo-Choo Cart. A cave in the southeast has two chambers shown in the wiki gallery. Local specialty: the Kalpalata Lotus. Like all of the Mirage, it sits inside a bottle; the inside is much larger than the outside.

The tracks have to be switched at junctions to reach different parts of the valley, and the carts are powered by Hydro Eidolons. The Mirage as a whole is described in canon as one gigantic Preprint, a flat blueprint made solid by a projector, and structures here appear to follow the same principle.

People: Three brothers in Adventurers' Guild uniforms keep the line running: Jeroney, the careful one with black glasses; Haddo, the designer, called "the sickly brother"; and Ferdinand, the sturdier brother.
