Like every resident of the Mirage except Idyia, they are Hydro Eidolon replicas of real people who once visited the bottle.

Idyia told the group that the three had been rescued from a sandstorm while on an adventure. Their jobs, in Ferdinand's words, are "brain" (Jeroney), "designer" (Haddo) and "brawn" (himself); the Hydro Eidolons do the actual heavy lifting. Because the brothers are replicas, they carry the dreams and trades of their human originals but not their memories or full personalities, which have to be taught.

Quests: In Zip Along (According to Safe Cart Operating Procedures), the Traveler's group (with Klee, Kaeya and Sangonomiya Kokomi) rides the Choo-Choo Cart along the rails, frees a Hydro Eidolon from a Preprint, finds Jeroney at a junction, helps Haddo power the tracks and tests the Torrential Twister. Kaeya meanwhile collects one of the Mirage's missing components. This is event-only content that ordinary Teyvat characters do not know about.

The quest comes in the first act, An Invitation From Afar!, after Glaze Domain, Multum in Parvo and before Fairground Gathering, Summer Lights Illuminated. The components gathered across the Mirage are gifts earlier visitors left Idyia, which she uses to keep the central wheel of the Mirage turning.

The Mirage's rules also shape play here: Hydro Eidolons, nicknamed Water Droplets, often disguise themselves as scenery and cannot speak, so they invite strangers to help by gesture; some freeze in fear near enemies or high places. None of the valley's residents can be read by Nahida's ability, which the wiki notes as an oddity of the Mirage.

Atmosphere: Clattering carts, bright rails curving between hills, and cheerful, slightly overworked guild-uniformed caretakers. The mood is a theme-park ride with real mechanical stakes: playful and sunny.

Dangers: Light combat: hilichurls, Large Anemo and Large Pyro Slimes, Winged Dendroshrooms, Stretchy Anemo Fungi, and Hydro Mimic Cranes disguised as ordinary scenery. The greater hazards in play are missed rail switches.

Travel: Reached by walking or riding the Choo-Choo Cart from the Silver Bottle Courtyard. Outsiders enter the Mirage itself through a Magic Invite or a summoned bottle, as Klee and the group did.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 canon, the Overgrown Valley is part of a time-limited area from Version 3.8; no later story returns to it.

It features in no content after the Secret Summer Paradise event. Treat it as a place visited by the Traveler and a few companions in the summer of that event.

179.comment: Overgrown Valley: The Brothers of the Choo-Choo Cart
179.content: Ferdinand (strong, cheerful), Jeroney (the brains, black glasses) and Haddo (the designer, frail) run the cart line in the Overgrown Valley as Hydro Eidolon replicas of three real adventurers. Ferdinand jokes that the carts operate around the clock and that serious repairs are needed only when Haddo designs new track. Jeroney is found high up and reminds visitors to use safety ropes.

180.content:
Pairidaeza Canyon: Pairidaeza Canyon is a point of interest in Sumeru's Great Red Sand, a canyon that cuts through Wadi Al-Majuj in the Desert of Hadramaveth. It was added in Version 3.4.

Parts of the canyon lie open to the sky and hold some Eremite camps; other parts run underground and contain a basin of shallow water. The canyon leads into Liloupar's Cell.

Geography: A cut through the desert terrain of Wadi Al-Majuj, with an exposed, sunlit stretch and a darker underground stretch with a shallow water basin. Its inner end connects to Liloupar's Cell.

People: Some Eremite camps stand in the open parts of the canyon.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the canyon is an ordinary explorable point of interest.

Canon says little about it: no history of the canyon is recorded.

Its Chinese name means Oasis Canyon; the English name is a transliteration. Apart from Liloupar's Cell beyond it, nothing ties a quest or character to the canyon.

Atmosphere: Scenes here can contrast bright, exposed desert rock and Eremite camps with cool, damp underground passages.

181.content: The canyon is the approach to Liloupar's Cell. That site's appearance changes once it is discovered during the quest The Temple Where Sand Flows Like Tears, per the wiki's Liloupar's Cell page.

182.content:
Pardis Dhyai (also: Garden of Deep Thought): Pardis Dhyai is a research site for Amurta scholars, set in a flowering garden in the Ashavan Realm of Sumeru. Its official description calls it the garden of deep thought, a paradise for people of goodwill. Tighnari is met here, and it is a gathering point for the Traveler's allies.

Its name roughly means garden of meditation: pardis from the Persian word for a garden (related to the word paradise) and dhyai probably from a Sanskrit root meaning to contemplate.

Places: A garden of countless flowers with a greenhouse; the plant Padisarah grows here. Karkata, a mechanical being, can be found in the greenhouse by day as a small cube, and wandering outside at night once Tighnari's story quest "The Unanswerable Problems" is complete.

People: Researchers and students include Hazm, Isami, Kemia, Ashshab, Dana and Jaleh, with the forest ranger Izad, the merchant Furat and the Eremite mercenaries Safiyya and Shahin. Tighnari is met here during the Archon Quest.

Karkata was built by the researcher Abattouy, who left the Akademiya after it banned the study of mechanical beings. After he died, Karkata kept trying to repair him with parts taken from passing convoys, which is part of what the Traveler and Tighnari untangle in "The Unanswerable Problems".

Quests: In the Archon Quest "As by a God's Side" the Traveler finds Tighnari here, a Fatui attack on the site is repelled, and the allies settle the plan for the evening. "Garden Memories", the last part of Tighnari's first story act, ends with a meeting here.

Atmosphere: Quiet and green, a place of scholarly calm in contrast to the market bustle of Sumeru City.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it remains a research garden; no later events at it are recorded in the pages consulted.

Further details: The map entry for Pardis Dhyai doubles as a viewpoint called The Garden of Deep Thought, and the wiki notes that Karkata's name comes from the Sanskrit word for crab. In the Archon Quest, after tracking the Doctor with Dehya and following Fatui soldiers to Port Ormos, the Traveler hurries back and defeats attacking Fatui here.

key: Chromatic Ode of Candies and Roses
183.comment: Pardis Dhyai: Chromatic Ode of Candies and Roses at Pardis Dhyai
183.content: During the limited-time flagship event "Chromatic Ode of Candies and Roses" (5.1), friends gather at Pardis Dhyai to prepare Nilou's birthday celebration, and in the part "Give Her Memories" the group meets there again before Nilou is found. The event is no longer available, so most characters will not know of it.

184.content:
Passage of Ghouls: The Passage of Ghouls is a passage sunk between two cliffs in the Desert of Hadramaveth, in Sumeru's Great Red Sand. It links Wadi Al-Majuj, a canyon area south of Mt. Damavand, with the flatter Sands of Al-Azif.

It is a corridor rather than a destination, and the most memorable thing in it is the pair of damaged records left by an investigation team that never made it to the Eternal Oasis.

Geography: A narrow, depressed pass between two cliffs. Wadi Al-Majuj, with its large canyon, lies to one end, and the Sands of Al-Azif, one of the flatter areas of the desert with roaming Wenut and the tunnels beneath, lies to the other.

The pass sits within the web of canyons that surround Mt. Damavand, where sandstorms make travel dangerous. The Desert of Hadramaveth is the area with the most subareas in the game, eleven in the wiki's count.

History: Damaged Records found here are the notes of a team that was ordered to find the path to the Eternal Oasis, the Orchard of Pairidaeza. They mention serious losses, supply lines cut by storms, and food running out so that they thought of catching nearby Wenut to eat. A hunting party was lost to the sandstorm and no more were sent.

By the end the team had run out of water and had bled their sumpter beasts, scouts were still hunting for a way back, and the writer left their fate to "the sleeping mistress of the Oasis" if she exists at all. A second record is a prayer to the Goddess of Flowers to carry the abandoned's souls to the Eternal Oasis.

The name is an out-of-universe nod to ghouls, shapeshifting, flesh-eating creatures of pre-Islamic Arabian folklore said to haunt remote desolate places, often near graveyards; the game text read gives no in-world reason, and the Chinese name translates roughly as Narrow Passage of the Deceased.

Dangers: The hazards of the Desert of Hadramaveth in general: sandstorms, scarce water and food, and roaming Wenut on the neighbouring sands. No enemy list is recorded for the passage itself.

In gameplay a Ruin Grader can be fought near the passage, and the Remarkable Chest it guards holds the blueprint for the Serenitea Pot furnishing "Iron, Sand, Treasure". That is a game mechanic, not story.

Atmosphere: A cliff-walled corridor in a storm-ridden desert, made grim by the notes of people who did not get through.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 nothing is recorded as changing here.

185.comment: Passage of Ghouls: Damaged Records of the Passage
185.content: Two fragmentary notes. The first describes an expedition ordered to find the path to the Eternal Oasis that has lost people, supplies and its hunting parties to the storms and now has little hope. The second prays to the Goddess of Flowers to bring the abandoned to the Oasis.

186.content:
Pavilion of Hermits: The Pavilion of Hermits is the fairground subarea of the Veluriyam Mirage, the bottle-domain from the limited-time Version 3.8 event Secret Summer Paradise. It is always night there, and a vast tent of fairground attractions stands at its centre. Maymunah, a scholar-replica who dreams of running her own festival, manages it. It was event-only and is not on the permanent map.

Its main story is the Act II quest Fairground Gathering, Summer Lights Illuminated, in which the Traveler's group, Eula, Collei, Idyia and Maymunah repair the tent's fallen lights, find a trapped Lawrence cousin of Eula's, and free the Hydro Eidolons trapped in the tent.

Geography: A lantern-lit fairground under a permanent night sky, with a big central tent, Gleaming Lamps, and a light board whose three lamps turn from white to colour as they are repaired. The area is unlocked by starting the Act II quest.

Preprints are scattered around the grounds: solving them removes the bubble from a Luxurious Chest and repairs the three lamps of the light board. The tent holds domain-style challenge content in game terms, though the story calls the whole Mirage a Domain.

People: Maymunah, an Akademiya-robed Spantamad scholar, manages the grounds. Lafeinte the "Blade Dancer" and Basima, a scholar with a game of her own, are other residents. All are Hydro Eidolon replicas of real visitors who once passed through the bottle.

The real Lafeinte, per his wiki profile, was a Fontaine swordsman of several centuries ago who went into exile after the Maison Gardiennage sought him. The real Basima was an Amurta scholar who vanished, returned after ten years with the Bing-Bang Finchball, and later used it to turn rivals into friends. The replicas hold none of these memories. Lessig, a real man from the Lawrence Clan, is not a replica: he came to the Mirage seeking to restore his clan's honour.

Quests: In Fairground Gathering, Summer Lights Illuminated, Maymunah leads the group into the abandoned tent, where something fell from the central hub and knocked down the Crystal Light, trapping Hydro Eidolons and Lessig. The group fixes the lights floor by floor. Lessig, helped by Idyia's candy, admits he was wrong; Maymunah gives the group the central hub component, a candy box.

Maymunah tells the group the collapsed stage reminds her of helping her father with festival work in the Sumeru Grand Bazaar, and that she came to the Mirage to run her own festival and become her true self, though managing it is harder than she expected. Lessig apologises to Eula and says he had come to Sumeru to restore the glory of the Lawrence Clan, but learned that nobody cares. The next morning he confesses that he had touched the water orb at the heart of the domain, which caused the chaos, and offers to help repair it.

In game terms the light board is a puzzle: three white lamps must be turned to colour, and one is repaired by a Hydro Eidolon the group saved earlier in the event. Paimon remarks that the multicoloured light is an ingenious design. The Mirage's unusual status is noted in the wiki: story characters call it a Domain, but the game does not treat it as one in the usual sense.

Atmosphere: Carnival lights against a permanent night: an amusement park run by replicas of people who left.

Dangers: Mostly light combat with hilichurls, hilichurl shooters, Dendro and Hydro Samachurls and a Stonehide Lawachurl. The tent itself was dangerous during the collapse of its lights.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 canon, the Pavilion of Hermits is a time-limited area from Version 3.8; no later story returns to it.

After the event, Maymunah says stall requests are piling up faster than she can arrange them, so the fairgrounds are busy again.

187.comment: Pavilion of Hermits: Maymunah the Fairground Manager
187.content: Maymunah is a Hydro Eidolon replica of a Spantamad-trained scholar, dressed in Akademiya robes with a hat bearing the Spantamad darshan symbol. She is overworked: stall demand exceeds space, and she jokes that her predecessor fled back to Sumeru. She hopes to run her own festival.

188.content:
Pharos Lighthouse: The Pharos Lighthouse stands at Port Ormos in Ardravi Valley, Sumeru. Kaveh's companion dialogue calls it a paradigm of Sumeru's architecture.

Architects like Kaveh are responsible for renovating and restoring it so it keeps its form. The wiki notes its name probably alludes to the Lighthouse of Alexandria, also called the Pharos.

Port officials and a lighthouse guardian are listed as stationed at this location (see people).

Geography: Located at Port Ormos in Ardravi Valley, in the Dharma Forest.

People: Araby is listed as the Lighthouse Guardian. Reza is the Port Master and Masrur the Deputy Port Master; Vasco, an adventurer, is also listed there.

Kaveh's remark comes from his companion voice-over at Friendship Level 7; see his own entry for his background.

History: Canon gives no founding story. It is described as something that must be renovated and restored over time.

Atmosphere: A lighthouse at a harbour town, valued enough that architects keep it restored.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 no change to the lighthouse was found.

No 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content was found that mentions it.

189.content:
Place of Breath: The Place of Breath is a small chamber branching off Sekhem Hall in the Mausoleum of King Deshret, in Sumeru's Hypostyle Desert. Solving its puzzles during Dual Evidence grants Clearance Level 3 of the Scarlet Sand Slate.

The slate says that those who ascend to Aaru will no longer sigh, their words will come out all joy, and their ears will be filled with Deshret's great deeds and glad bird-like singing. It names the sophophilic as those who pass its trial and win ever-lasting bliss.

Geography: Enter Sekhem Hall, preferably by its waypoint, take the first hallway on the right and turn left where a primal sconce stands; a primal ember shows the way. The wiki places the chamber on Sekhem Hall's east side while another page says west, so the direction is not settled.

Clearance Level 3 allows the Traveler to use Obscuring Cells and Verity Cells found elsewhere in the desert.

History: One of the three chambers the slate points to after the party enters Duat Hall. Clearing it lights one of the three sigils; the slate's final text says those who finish it will gain everlasting bliss.

Its ancient purpose is not described; the slate's wording is poetic. The name pairs with the other two trial places, which are named for Rebirth and Swallowing.

Atmosphere: A quiet side chamber, contrasting with the hall's grandeur; the slate speaks of sighs and birdsong.

Quests: Dual Evidence (Old Notes and New Friends, part 1).

Along with the Place of Rebirth and the Place of Swallowing, it forms the three trials the quest requires before the Great Hall of Truths appears.

Status as of 7.1: Open to explore as of Version 7.1.

No source up to Version 7.1 that I checked changes it.

190.content:
Place of Rebirth: The Place of Rebirth is a trial chamber southwest of the Mausoleum of King Deshret in Sumeru's Hypostyle Desert. Solving its puzzles in the quest Dual Evidence lights the second clearance level of the Scarlet Sand Slate.

The slate says that those who ascend to Aaru will burst into living flame again like the sun after countless nights, and will no longer know the tragedy of age and decay. In an earlier passage it names the resilient as those who pass the trial of Rebirth and gain an unalterable form.

Geography: Lies southwest of the Mausoleum. Players enter from the Dune of Magma and explore underground until a waypoint appears; a small tunnel inside a ruin near a Dendroculus leads to the chamber.

It is one of three trial chambers, with the Place of Breath off Sekhem Hall and the Place of Swallowing off Duat Hall.

History: Dual Evidence has the slate point at three places. Clearing the Place of Rebirth lights one of the three sigils (Paimon comments differently depending on which chambers the Traveler has already cleared). The slate's Clearance Level 2 lets the Traveler operate large fan blades elsewhere in the Great Red Sand.

Lighting the first primal torch in the chamber makes running water audible, which Paimon takes to be a hidden mechanism responding.

Atmosphere: A hidden, intimate chamber reached by a narrow tunnel, with the sound of water running behind stone.

Quests: Dual Evidence (Old Notes and New Friends, part 1). Some of the slate's clearances are also obtained outside this chamber in Golden Slumber and Old Notes and New Friends.

Completing all of the slate's clearances other than the City of Gurabad grants the achievement Walk Like King Deshret's People.

Status as of 7.1: Open to explore as of Version 7.1.

No source up to Version 7.1 that I checked changes it.

191.content:
Place of Swallowing: The Place of Swallowing is a small chamber branching off Duat Hall in the Mausoleum of King Deshret, in Sumeru's Hypostyle Desert. Completing its puzzles during Dual Evidence grants Clearance Level 4 of the Scarlet Sand Slate.

The slate says that those who ascend to Aaru will forget hunger and thirst, and even if they sup on pomegranate juice they do so for pleasure rather than survival. It names the abstinent as those who pass its trial and never fear hunger or thirst.

Geography: Branches off the east side of Duat Hall. The Fourth Clearance found here allows the Traveler to interact with all chambers in the Great Red Sand.

The chamber is part of a ladder of permissions: the Ferryman's Clearance opens Duat Hall, and this clearance extends it further.

History: One of three chambers the slate points to after the Traveler enters Duat Hall. Paimon notes it as they approach and remarks they no longer need Tirzad or Jebrael to read the slate. Clearing it lights a sigil, and the slate's final text says those who finish it will never fear hunger or thirst.

The pomegranate image is only in the slate's text, and the quest does not explain it.

Atmosphere: Close and stony beside the vast void of Duat Hall; the sense of fasting and thirst is only in the slate's words.

Quests: Dual Evidence (Old Notes and New Friends, part 1).

With the Place of Rebirth and the Place of Breath it completes the three trials; once all sigils are lit the slate announces the Great Hall of Truths.

Status as of 7.1: Open to explore as of Version 7.1.

No source up to Version 7.1 that I checked changes it.

key: The Harbor Betwixt the Two Trees
192.content:
Port Ormos (also: The Harbor Betwixt the Two Trees): Port Ormos is the largest port in Sumeru and the nation's hub for trade and travel, in the Ardravi Valley beneath two giant trees with a river running to it from Sumeru City. Parts of it are under the Akademiya's supervision, but smuggling and shady dealing are more common here than in the capital. Prices run lower than in Sumeru City, Eremite mercenaries from many factions pass through, and students come to blow off steam.

Most long-term residents are traders and laborers who grew up in the area. Some students consider the port good luck.

Geography: Port Ormos lies in Ardravi Valley, in the Dharma Forest, beneath two enormous trees; the river between them runs from Sumeru City to the harbour. Docks are divided into the Northern Docks, Eastside Docks and Westside Docks, with an Upper Tier above, and the Pharos Lighthouse stands near the harbour.

Kaveh is credited with designing and building the port's arch bridge. A trading company advertises that it has opened a route to Dornman Port in Mondstadt.

Places: Djafar Tavern, where Eremites gather and rumours spread; Shapur Hotel in the Upper Tier, owned by Shapur and managed by Sareh; Pharos Lighthouse, guarded by Araby; the Port Master, Reza, and his deputy Masrur; and shops and stalls selling fish, spice, jewellery and goods.

Notices at the Port Ormos Bulletin Board include advertisements from trading companies. Jewelry shop owner Royinjan and Jazari (after the Vimana Agama quests) are among the people tied to world quests here.

People: Port Master Reza handles tax levies and customs and complains that reform of foreign trade is slow; Masrur is his deputy; Shyam is the sheriff. Merchants include Berbere and Rama (spices), Dilawar and Gauhar (trade supervisors) and Alexandra and Przheva. Eremite mercenaries and captains, such as Feroz and Matari, are present among the docks.

Farahnaz is a researcher who tells the Orghana story. Eymen tends the bar at Djafar Tavern with the hostesses Nesmil and Roshana, and Pooria is a goldsmith. Cats Sisi, Lale, Rozan and Nargis also live around the port.

By dock: the Northern Docks hold the sheriff Shyam, the fisherman Kira, the sumpter beast keeper Salm, the street performer Taraneh and the snake handler Gulabgir; the Eastside Docks the porter Sanjay, the crafts merchant Shadi and the book collector Siger; the Westside Docks the ship technician Anand, the dockworker Bita, the cashier Fariba, the merchant ship captain Xiaodong and the Mahamata Mahshid. Araby guards the Pharos Lighthouse.

Governance: Reza says his office levies taxes and runs customs, and smuggling is the most common offence; he asks people to report violators and to flag down Eremites for help with fugitives. Parts of the port are supervised by the Akademiya. The Corps of Thirty garrisons Sumeru City's own small port, which a guard there says is far easier to police.

Reza adds that occasional fugitives try to flee through the port, and says bystanders should leave them to the Eremites patrolling nearby.

Culture: A trading culture of bargaining, fishing and rumours; Sumeru's students come here when academic life gets stressful. Official text jokes about swapping boring lectures for floral-honey wine and a voyage across seven seas.

History: Farahnaz says Port Ormos was originally Orghana, the city of the Twenty-Nine Deys, pirate captains who allied to share power fairly and keep peace. Infighting weakened them, and a powerful sea monster wiped them out. A book, The Shepherd and the Magic Bottle, instead names Orghana as the Deys' city but mentions Port Ormos separately, and its credibility is questioned.

The book is set fifteen years after the port was built, when a boy from the Gravelsong Dunes finds a magic bottle with a jinni in it. It is possible Port Ormos was built on the older city and Farahnaz uses the modern name. The name Ormos is Greek for a cove or small bay; it may also nod to the Kingdom of Ormus.

Atmosphere: A busy harbour beneath two giant trees, with merchants and porters on the docks, Eremite mercenaries on patrol, students taking a break from lectures, and, officially, a tempting promise of wine garnished with floral honey.

Dangers: Smuggling, scams and fugitives; Eremite factions with radical views; and the Fatui, who figure in a world quest here.

Travel: A river runs from Sumeru City to the port. A trading company's notice on the Port Ormos Bulletin Board says it has opened a route to Dornman Port in Mondstadt for a fruit business; a reply doubts whether fruit is worth importing over such a long voyage.

Quests: In the Archon Quest "Lost in Prosperity" the Traveler and Paimon reach Port Ormos looking for the Akademiya's missing item, overhear students, and watch Alhaitham quarrel with the Eremite group Ayn Al-Ahmar, who set a fight for a week later at the pier before Pharos Lighthouse, then wait for Eremites at Djafar Tavern. They help Alhaitham win the merchant Dori's trust and meet her contact in a warehouse. The next quest, "Ever So Close", brings the fight with Ayn Al-Ahmar and its leader Mizri.

World quest The Price (3.0) involves the merchants Alexandra and Przheva, two low-ranking Fatui who want to leave the organisation by faking their deaths with the Traveler as witness, and a person named Nika. The Kaveh hangout quest "A Refuge in the Sands" (3.7) begins here at the port.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Port Ormos remains Sumeru's main port, busy with trade and customs. No disaster at the port is shown.

Its trade reaches abroad: a trading company advertises a route to Dornman Port in Mondstadt, and Reza says new regulations limit foreign trade to Port Ormos.

193.comment: Port Ormos: Lost in Prosperity at Port Ormos
193.content:
The Traveler and Paimon learn at the port that extremist Eremite groups, among them Ayn Al-Ahmar, claim the long-dead King Deshret will revive. Alhaitham from the Akademiya quarrels with Ayn Al-Ahmar, and they set a fight for a week later at the pier in front of Pharos Lighthouse. He reveals that the missing item is a Knowledge Capsule, but will talk only after the Traveler becomes a customer of Dori, a shrewd merchant who is wary of Akademiya people because most of her wares break Akademiya regulations.

In Ever So Close, Dori's help reveals that Ayn Al-Ahmar's leader Mizri holds the Divine Knowledge Capsule. At the fight Mizri goes berserk after using it; Alhaitham cuts his Akasha Terminal link, the Matra take him away, and Mizri murmurs the words "World... Forget me". Alhaitham quietly keeps the capsule.

194.comment: Port Ormos: Orghana and the Twenty-Nine Deys
194.content: Orghana, the city of the Twenty-Nine Deys, is said to be Port Ormos' predecessor. The Deys were pirate captains who allied to divide power fairly. Infighting led to instability and a powerful sea monster wiped them out. The accounts differ on whether Port Ormos stands on the same site.

195.comment: Port Ormos: Reza, the Port Master
195.content: Reza is Port Ormos' Port Master, in charge of tax levies, customs and trade. He calls the port Sumeru's key trade hub and says the most common offence is smuggling; anyone seen with suspicious cargo is probably a smuggler. He wearily admits that reform of the foreign trade sector is very hard.

key: Chromatic Ode of Candies and Roses
196.comment: Port Ormos: Subzeruz Ships During Chromatic Ode of Candies and Roses
196.content: During the limited-time event Chromatic Ode of Candies and Roses, Port Master Reza remarks that so many ships have arrived at Port Ormos for the Sabzeruz festival.

197.content:
Puspa Café (also: Puspa Cafe): Puspa Café is a coffee shop with a long history on Treasures Street in Sumeru City. Its map text calls it a place serving authentic Sumeru-style coffee and a rare social space where people from all walks of life like to gather. Enteka is its acting manager, and she reads customers' fortunes in the coffee grounds.

It is a spot for conversation, storytelling and Genius Invokation TCG games, and its shop is open at any hour.

Places: A single café with a counter and a shop. The stall is open at all times and restocks daily with desserts such as baklava, candied ajilenakh nut and padisarah pudding, plus coffee beans, and it also sells recipes for several sweets. A message board stands outside, to the left just before the entrance.

Regulars mention a card table where the card game is played.

People: Staff are Enteka (acting manager), Maddah (the resident storyteller) and Gata, a young cat. Customers vary with the time of day: Iris (a researcher) by day; Nayab (a relaxed Matra), Izem (a veteran of the Corps of Thirty), Zohreh (a researcher), Sanad (a student), Mawyo (a self-described freelancer) and the self-styled millionaire Hatim at night.

Enteka says she can make a coffee to any taste, however offbeat, and asks first-time customers whether they like it sweet or bitter, strong or mild. She says Gata is not yet a year old, is curious, and jumps up to watch whenever she reads the grounds; patting her is welcome.

Hatim and Mawyo also appear on Treasures Street by day or night, at different times. The board's posts name Cyno, Nilou, Kaveh, Alhaitham and Dori in passing.

Governance: Enteka is acting manager 'for the time being', as the board puts it. The original owner went missing on a desert expedition three years before a Kalimi Exchange notice on the café, which the wiki cites. The reason Enteka holds the post is not explained.

Culture: Coffee, cards and talk. Regulars include students preparing for the Akademiya entrance exam, who value the friendly atmosphere and the seniors they can ask for guidance. Enteka's fortune-telling from coffee grounds is a house speciality.

The message board mixes humour and gossip: a repentant player who invented a non-existent card to cheat others and was set straight by Cyno; the 'Puspa Card Club' recruiting Genius Invokation players, with Enteka asking its founder to at least buy a coffee; a storyteller advertising the next instalment of the legend of Antara, answered by Enteka offering free coffee if he stops posting ads; and a veteran of the Corps of Thirty noting that he gets the same coffee and hears the same story every day.

Two posts show how scholars treat the place. An unsigned debate between voices identified with Kaveh and Alhaitham, about art and commerce, ends with Enteka reminding them of a monthly tab; a message seemingly from a noble asks to put it on Dori's tab. A Matra notice warns that forbidden knowledge obtained illegally can cost a student the right to study at the Akademiya, and that Canned Knowledge smuggling has been reported. These are board posts, not quest events. The name Puspa is Sanskrit for 'flower' or 'blossom' (wiki note).

Atmosphere: Warm, talkative and slightly old-fashioned: the smell of coffee, a storyteller repeating familiar tales, card players arguing over decks, and a cat underfoot.

Dangers: None are described. The only caution is a joke that Enteka accepts no liability for losses from tips posted on the board.

Travel: Puspa Café is on Treasures Street in Sumeru City. Its message board is just outside the door.

Status as of 7.1: Open and operating as of 7.1, as far as the sources show. Enteka is still acting manager.

198.content:
Enteka is the acting manager of Puspa Café and runs its shop. She introduces herself as Acting Café Manager at the customer's service. She reads coffee grounds, and the map text says her readings are rumoured to be more accurate than the professional diviners at the bazaar. No fuller profile exists.

In her thoughts she wonders whether Gata is shedding a lot. On the message board she writes the Acting Manager's replies: polite but dry, teasing customers and reminding patrons to pay.

199.content: Gata is the café's young cat, under a year old by Enteka's account, curious and affectionate. Nilou's board message shows she is fond of Gata, and Enteka says Gata seems fond of her too.

200.comment: Puspa Café: Puspa Café Message Board
200.content: Posts cycle at random each time it is read, with replies from the acting manager. Topics are card games, scholars' arguments, tabs, exam advice, storytelling, smuggling warnings and the price of Ajilenakh Nuts during bandit trouble in the desert. One post warns of a Rishboland Tiger in the northwest forest at night.

201.content: Maddah is the café's resident storyteller. A board post credits him with skilful pacing despite old-fashioned tales, and he advertises the continuing legend of Antara, to Enteka's irritation. A post in the same debate claims people now take their information from Akasha and overlook such craft.

202.content:
Qusayr Al-Inkhida' (also: Qusayr Al-Inkhida, Royal Lodge of Conceitedness): Qusayr Al-Inkhida' is a ruined palace in the Desert of Hadramaveth in Sumeru's Great Red Sand. It has an Eremite camp and caverns below it that lead toward Deshret's Glass Goblet, but canon tells almost nothing about its history.

Its name is Arabic for something like Small Palace of Deception according to the wiki; that is a name, not a story.

Geography: A subarea of the Desert of Hadramaveth with a ruin that has a high platform. Collectibles include a Radiant Spincrystal on that platform and a Remarkable Chest holding the blueprint for the furnishing The Art of Retaining Water. Torn pages of A Thousand Nights lie near Eremite camps.

The caverns under the palace, called Bayt Al-Muazzam, lead into the cavern holding Deshret's Glass Goblet. They are unlocked during Dune-Entombed Fecundity: Part I of The Dirge of Bilqis.

People: Eremites camp in the ruin. Some of the pages of A Thousand Nights (II and III) that complete a book are found beside them.

Atmosphere: A weathered palace in open desert, a place with a camp rather than a story.

The wiki notes that the Desert of Hadramaveth has more subareas than any other area, eleven in all. The area's event description speaks of a lost city and a wandering tribe sheltering among scimitar-shaped ravines, and of stories erased by sandstorms; this palace is one of the many ruins in that setting.

Quests: No quest is based here. The caverns beneath it are unlocked during Dune-Entombed Fecundity: Part I, as the party seeks the Eternal Oasis in Mt. Damavand.

Status as of 7.1: Open and unremarkable. Nothing found up to Version 7.1 adds lore.

203.content: Bayt Al-Muazzam is the wiki's name for the caverns under Qusayr Al-Inkhida' that lead into Deshret's Glass Goblet; the name means House of the Glorified. Its viewpoint is called the Temple of Buried Dominion.

204.content:
Razan Garden: Razan Garden is a serene garden inside the Akademiya in Sumeru City, along the path up the Divine Tree. It is reached by the right or left doors inside the Akademiya and is dotted with gazebos and decorative padisarah plants. Researchers and students come here to read, talk or think, and an Akademiya public message board stands in the garden.

The people here are mostly scholars: Darya, Farghani, Homayun, Makhfi, Muganna and Qushji are listed as researchers, and Arina and Armin as students.

People: Muganna is a gloomy researcher who calls the garden the place where silence will ultimately reign and thinks that everyone dies, gods included. Homayun, a researcher, worries about pollution in the rainforest and mentions requesting earlier research from the House of Daena; he hopes to think uninterrupted here. The others are ambient residents without individual stories.

Homayun's lines change after the Archon Quest chapter that reveals the fate of the Dendro Archon: before it he speaks of honouring Greater Lord Rukkhadevata by caring for the rainforest, afterwards of the Dendro Archon in the same way. During the Akademiya Extravaganza event he grumbles about the commotion.

Atmosphere: Still and green, a pocket of calm within the Akademiya's grand architecture, where the occasional passer-by is a scholar lost in thought rather than a tourist.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Razan Garden is unchanged.

No quest in canon through 7.1 is set here; it is an ambient location.

205.content:
Realm of Farakhkert: The Realm of Farakhkert is the northwestern area of the Girdle of the Sands in Sumeru, added in version 3.6. It holds Vourukasha Oasis, the sealed homeland of the Pari, as well as the thorny Asipattravana Swamp, the pine-covered Hills of Barsom and the sandy Samudra Coast at the far northwest border of the Sumeru desert.

The name probably derives from the Middle Persian name of the Vourukasha, the mythic sea. The Chemin Oublie tunnel, which connects this area to Fontaine's Romaritime Harbor, begins here.

Geography: Samudra Coast has sandy beaches and clear blue waters at the northwest edge of the desert. Inland, the Hills of Barsom lie just north of Asipattravana Swamp, and the swamp itself lies just north of Vourukasha Oasis. The area's local specialties are Mourning Flower and Trishiraite.

Wiki-listed exploration items include Amrita Mayflies, Bright Flame Altars, Fravashi Trees, Gray Crystals, Kory drums, Nirodha Fruit, Ruebright Bloom, Soul Bells, Sunyata Flowers and the Sorush gadget. Notable collectables include Korybantes, Khvarena Inscription Fragments, Plumes of Purifying Light and the Udumbara Pistil.

The wiki files the quest Awakening's Real Sound, which concerns Rashnu at the Hills of Barsom, under Gavireh Lajavard's quest category, a reminder that the Girdle's two areas share one storyline and that quest lists cross the boundary.

Places: Vourukasha Oasis, where the Pari live around the Harvisptokhm tree. Asipattravana Swamp, a thorn-filled canyon swamp guarded by the Pari Mihir. The Hills of Barsom, home to a huge pink-leaved pine, the Barsom, and the Pari Rashnu. Samudra Coast, the beach on the far northwest. Chemin Oublie, the tunnel to Fontaine.

The Order of Skeptics historically performed a musical ritual with Korybantes around the Barsom, believing it helped form a bond ("Laupa") with the Pari. In practice, the quest Awakening's Real Sound reveals that Rashnu found the noise bothersome.

People: The Pari are the main inhabitants: Zurvan the elder, Mihir, Rashnu and the young Sorush who joins the Traveler. The Order of Skeptics' researchers and their Yasnapati bonds are historically tied to the Pari.

Pari are the sentient form of Khvarena and each has a responsibility to fulfil alone; they are the subject of the Vourukasha Oasis entity.

History: The area is the setting of the Khvarena of Good and Evil quests of 3.6. The Harvisptokhm, grown by Greater Lord Rukkhadevata from the remains of the former Hydro Archon Egeria, keeps the defilement of the Abyssal rift at Tunigi Hollow in check; the Pari guard it.

The wiki lists a note in the underground Khaenri'ah ruins, signed by the Schwanenritter garrison commander Hadura, ordering the Mechanical Wardens' defences activated and survivors evacuated; the wiki's Farakhkert page places this note in the proving-grounds chamber of those ruins.

Dangers: Abyssal purple mist, Pari twisted by defilement, and Abyss monsters tied to the Tunigi Hollow rift; Chemin Oublie holds Hydro slimes and Hydro hilichurl rogues.

Travel: Chemin Oublie is the walking route to Fontaine's Romaritime Harbor. Samudra Coast is at the far northwest border of the desert. Vourukasha Oasis is sealed and admits only bonded heroes and pilgrims worshipping Egeria, except as the story opens it for the Traveler.

Quests: Heart of Amrita, An Artist Adrift (Parts 1 to 3), As the Khvarena's Light Shows: Nirodha and Samudaya, and The Recollector's Path (Parts 2 to 6). The Khvarena of Good and Evil quests that run through here also touch Gavireh Lajavard; they are summarised in the Vourukasha Oasis entity.

Atmosphere: Hushed and sacred around the oasis, harsh in the thorn-choked swamp, and bright on the open beach where the sea shows through the desert's edge.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the realm is calm, with the Sign of Apaosha gone and the Pari resting.

Nothing from 6.x or 7.0-7.1 changes the area.

206.comment: Realm of Farakhkert: Hills of Barsom
206.content: Hills just north of Asipattravana Swamp where the Barsom, a huge pine with pink foliage, grows, with its familiar the Pari Rashnu. The Order of Skeptics once held a musical ritual here to bond with Pari, a ritual Rashnu found too noisy.

207.content: A stretch of sandy beach and clear blue water on the far northwestern border of the Sumeru desert.

208.content:
Realm of Khab (also: Khab Realm, Barsam Flower's dream): The Realm of Khab is a quiet, damp, plant-grown place reached from Chatrakam Cave in the Lokapala Jungle of Sumeru's Dharma Forest. Aranara lore calls it the convergence of the memories of Nara Varuna and the Aranara, and the dream where the Barsam Flower sleeps. The Traveler visits it in the Risen Moon Chapter of the Agnihotra Sutra quests to fetch that flower.

It was once the home of "Nara" (the Aranara word for humans), who left stone houses and runes; after they fell asleep, plants grew from their dreams and took the place over. Fungi have since crept in and the Realm is weakened.

Its function in the story is protective: the Barsam Flower can sleep there, floating on water, safe from the Withering (called Marana by the Aranara).

The Realm is therefore less a settlement than a refuge and a memory: Aranara memories live in tubers, seeds and leaf veins, human memories in carved stone, and here the two flow together.

Geography: The route runs through Chatrakam Cave, a fungus-choked cave system that humans rarely enter, then out of the cave's far side, down a drop past vines that Aragaru persuades to part, into the Realm. Inside, the Barsam Flower grows beneath a seal of plant-eroded stones; water hangs overhead. The area is humid, silent and overgrown, and is guarded by Fungi and ruin machines.

Gameplay note: after both Starry Night Chapter and Risen Moon Chapter are done, lighting its Dendro monuments unlocks an unmarked waypoint.

Places: Chatrakam Cave, the approach, holds Aranara and Nara runes and a series of cracked, vine-bound stones that Aragaru breaks with Kusava. Inside the Realm are sealed side chambers reached by following three Seelie, and the chamber where the Barsam Flower grows.

Three runes in the cave tell a story in pictures: a river of light with star-blooming stems that sends brave Nara; the Grandmaster of Verdure lifting vines to let them pass to the Realm; and the Nara and Aranara driving off the dark Marana together with the Barsam Flower.

History: According to Aragaru, the Nara left the stones, but not their memories. Nara Varuna came and wept for them, and the place where the tears fell became the forest. The memories of Nara Varuna and the Aranara flowed into it and became the Realm of Khab.

Aragaru says the three Aranara used to come to the cave whenever the moon was high, to recall old stories as the Nara did. None of this is dated, and canon does not say who the Nara of the stone homes were.

Quests: Risen Moon Chapter (Agnihotra Sutra, 3.0). Aragaru needs the Barsam Flower for Arahaoma, the potion that lets the Aranara reach Mawtiyima and fight Marana. He and the Traveler break seals with Kusava, defeat Fungi and Winged Dendroshrooms, and reach the flower. When it is woken the dream disperses in a flood of water that sweeps them away. Aragaru then leaves for Mawtiyima Forest to prepare the ritual.

The quest can be taken before or after Starry Night Chapter; Aragaru's closing dialogue changes depending on whether the Zohrah Mushroom has been found. The chain ends with The Final Chapter.

Dangers: Fungi infest the cave and the Realm; Aragaru fears they will multiply and compete for nutrients. Ruin machines guard the sealed chambers. The Realm is weak, and once the flower is woken its stored "dream" collapses into a sudden flood.

Atmosphere: A hushed, humid, slightly uncanny place: quiet enough to give Paimon goosebumps, heavy with overhead water, soft with plants and old carved stone. The Aranara treat it with tenderness, as a sleeping place not to be disturbed lightly.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is only known to have appeared in the Risen Moon Chapter. The flower was taken and the dream dispersed; the Realm can still be revisited in game. Nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content mentions it.

209.content: A plant spirit's flower used as an ingredient of the Arahaoma elixir. Aragaru calls it a good friend of the Aranara who sleeps in the Realm of Khab. When woken it was angry but agreed to join the Aranara for Mawtiyima's revival. Its item text says "Barsam" is said to be a sacred tree long vanished from history.

210.content:
Red Desert Threshold (also: Edge of the End): The Red Desert Threshold is a one-time domain in Abdju Pit, in the Land of Lower Setekh of Sumeru's Great Red Sand. It is a corner of the ancient city of Gurabad where the wise once debated, later turned into a secret prison. Today monsters nest there and relics of the past remain. It opens only after starting the Golden Slumber quest.

The in-game text says legend holds that a prince exiled by his father was held in this jail, and that the "bronze revelation" first emerged in this lonely place where there is neither day nor night. This is a legend, not a confirmed account.

Geography: An underground holding complex reached through Abdju Pit, which is described as the desert's edge, with a palace buried under the sand and King Deshret's realm beyond. Abdju Pit did not exist before the quest Lost in the Sands; the area was previously called Abdju Road. The domain has one level, Edge of the End. Dendro is recommended.

The domain's special rule rewards triggering Dendro-related reactions (Burning, Quicken, Aggravate, Spread, Bloom, Hyperbloom, Burgeon) with a shockwave of True damage, at most once every three seconds. This is a gameplay mechanic.

History: In its first age the place belonged to Gurabad. The domain description says scholars once debated wisdom here and outlined the dream of the desert king (King Deshret). After that dream's bubble burst, it became a secret holding cell. The legend of an exiled prince (compare Shiruyeh, whom Parvezravan banished) attaches to the cells.

Gurabad itself fell in a plague, sinking into the earth in the story of Shiruyeh and Parvezravan; the domain text does not say whether this occurred here.

Shiruyeh's supporters, according to the Gurabad accounts, were commoners and former slaves displaced by Jinn-powered machines, and they portrayed him as the emissary of Nabu Malikata. Whether the cells below Abdju Pit held anyone from that movement is not stated.

Dangers: Mitachurls of several kinds (Blazing Axe, Wooden Shieldwall), Geovishaps, and Lawachurls (Thunderhelm, Stonehide).

Quests: Unlocked through Golden Slumber, a Sumeru world quest series that starts with Bonifaz in Aaru Village. In that series the Traveler helps a Mondstadt merchant's missing archaeology team, meets the Eremite mercenaries Jebrael and Jeht, and follows King Deshret's trail to Khaj-Nisut.

Atmosphere: Closed stone cells, no sun and no night, and the sense of a forgotten place under the sand where the old city's secrets were kept.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the domain is unchanged and accessible. No later content has altered it.

211.content:
Restricted Repository: The Restricted Repository is the Akademiya's vault of forbidden documents, accessible only to the Mahamatra and their trusted associates. When the matra stop a dangerous project, most of its files are destroyed, but some are kept here as a warning to later researchers. In the game it is entered only during the quest All Returns to Silence.

It is a small room of bookshelves behind a secret door, run by a keeper named Utayba.

Geography: The entrance is hidden in a wall, near the entrance of the House of Daena. Behind it is a small room full of bookshelves holding research archives of former students and researchers who studied banned subjects.

The bookshelves carry alarms, and a device operated by the keeper opens the hidden door. The wiki notes a similar room appears in Ilyas's thoughts in the quest Pride and Prejudice.

Places: Three files are readable in the Traveler's visit: a manual on interpreting secret texts, recording a Haravatat researcher sentenced to prison for deciphering forbidden documents; research data on mechanical life forms, recording a Spantamad researcher expelled from the Akademiya; and the sealed materials on the Court of Desolation.

The Court of Desolation file describes three stages of research: Discovery, Investigation and Fanaticism. Early work hinted that treasures bearing on life and death might lie in the Court and spawned a rumour of bringing the dead back to life. The Court itself was never found. Surviving stone tablets read that entering it costs one's life, and the view that the price makes the Court appear overtook the view that it is the key to entry. Researchers then attempted to sacrifice themselves, and the research was banned.

The file says Akademiya scholars kept researching in secret despite the ban, until seven scholars, including Murtada Radkani, were arrested; research then stagnated again.

People: Utayba is the administrator. Very few are allowed in even among the matra, and entry is granted only by him; he guides and supervises visitors. Nabil, a matra who does not normally have authorisation, brings the Traveler in using a letter from Cyno.

Utayba trusts Cyno, who has left the Akademiya, enough to open the room to Cyno's friends, and says very few people can be trusted with a real secret. He advises visitors to read only the Court of Desolation files, because sometimes the less one knows, the better, and warns them not to bump the alarm behind the bookshelf.

From Utayba's account in the quest: Murtada Radkani was the only son of Taj Radkani, Cyno's former partner and a long-serving, respected matra. Murtada was arrested in secret over the Court of Desolation research, so it was never public, and he took his own life not long after being jailed. Nabil wonders whether this is why Taj moved from active duty to an administrative post; the scene does not say.

Governance: The matra decide when research is too dangerous and must be halted. The Repository belongs to that system of control and secrecy: kept for warning, protected by a hidden door and alarms, and open to very few.

Culture: The Repository reflects the Akademiya's two faces. Nabil notes the Akademiya supports research and encourages all kinds of study, but when work proves dangerous the matra step in and suppress it, and the knowledge goes behind locked doors.

Atmosphere: Quiet, cramped and watchful: shelves of files, a keeper who urges haste, and the sense that every record is a warning.

Dangers: The alarms behind the shelves. Reading the wrong material is itself treated as a hazard, and the Court of Desolation file records researchers who tried to sacrifice themselves and others who were imprisoned.

Travel: Inside the Akademiya, hidden in a wall near the House of Daena. Nobody can enter without the keeper's consent. In the game the interior cannot be re-entered after the quest.

Quests: All Returns to Silence, the third part of Sands of Solitude in the Lupus Aureus Chapter, Act I. Cyno sends the Traveler with a letter to Nabil to look up information in the repository, in the Canned Knowledge smuggling case that leads to the Court of Desolation. The wiki records the quest as released in 3.1.

Status as of 7.1: Still the Akademiya's secret archive in the story as of 7.1, as far as the sources show.

212.content: Utayba is the Restricted Repository Administrator, an Akademiya-affiliated quest NPC. He lets the Traveler and Nabil view the Court of Desolation files because Cyno vouches for them. He is cautious and brisk with visitors and speaks well of Cyno.

213.comment: Restricted Repository: Court of Desolation research file
213.content: A sealed file in the Repository summarising how scholarly interest in the Court of Desolation became fanatical and was banned. See the places section for the three stages.

214.content: Murtada was Taj Radkani's only son and a researcher at the Akademiya. He was one of seven scholars arrested over Court of Desolation research and, as Utayba tells it, took his own life soon after being jailed. The arrest was kept quiet.

215.content:
Ruins of Dahri (also: Dahri ruins): The Ruins of Dahri are Khaenri'ahn ruins in the Ashavan Realm of Sumeru's Dharma Forest. In Sumeru Dahri is an archaic name for the lost underground kingdom of Khaenri'ah, and the ruin is full of Ruin Guards, which the Aranara call Big Iron Chunks. In the quest Irate Iron Chunk the Traveler follows the Aranara Arabalika underground to reach a root of the Varuna Contraption.

It is a separate place from the Valley of Dahri in the desert. Its enemies include Ruin Hunters and Ruin Cruisers.

Geography: A subarea of the Ashavan Realm, with a Caravan Ribat waypoint; the Traveler first meets Arabalika east of it. Below the surface is a cavern reached by draining water and following Arabalika's burrow.

A hole opens at the bottom of the drained area into a deep cavern full of inactive Ruin Guards around a stone 'branch'. The Grove of Dreams, another underground cavern holding one of the Varuna Contraption's energy sources, connects to the Ruins of Dahri to the west.

People: Arabalika, an Aranara with powerful Ararakalari, is exploring alone. He speaks bluntly and without the metaphors other Aranara use, and says he thinks little and only knows how to protect. He is dissatisfied with Paimon and tests the Traveler's strength before trusting them.

History: Dahri is the archaic term in Vahumana scholarship for Khaenri'ah, a word meaning roughly one who denies a creator, as the wiki's etymology note puts it. The ruins are among the remnants of Khaenri'ah that the wiki says share a grand scale, together with giant Ruin Golems and the Azosite factory under Gavireh Lajavard.

An Akademiya report at Devantaka Mountain mentions a legend of the Ruins of Dahri that may confirm the Schwanenritter existed. In Irate Iron Chunk Arabalika says the stone and iron here do not belong to Aranara, and he smells iron and calls it a bad smell. The seemingly broken Ruin Guards around the stone branch are quiet until the 'leaves' are turned, after which a huge Ruin Grader starts to move.

Atmosphere: Water and fungi on the surface and a deep cavern below that smells of iron to Arabalika. He says the stone and iron chunks here do not belong to the Aranara.

Dangers: Ruin Guards, Ruin Hunters and Ruin Cruisers; Floating Dendro Fungus and Winged Dendroshroom. Arabalika can defeat a Ruin Guard alone, and in the quest he deals Dendro damage at intervals while fighting alongside the Traveler.

Quests: Irate Iron Chunk is a quest in the Varuna Gatha series, begun after Varuna Gatha, with Arapandu asking the Traveler to help heal the Varuna Contraption. The party defeats Ruin Guards, activates a mechanism to drain the water, descends, turns three 'leaves' toward the branch, defeats a Ruin Grader and talks to Arabalika again.

The Varuna Contraption draws its power from a root system spread throughout Vana. Arabalika tells how Arapandu once protected Vana with Nara Varuna, drove away the black mud and healed the Contraption, and that the story of Nara Varuna is remembered even though Arabalika never met them. Slumbering Roots, a concurrent quest, covers other roots.

Arapandu hopes to heal the Contraption again for Festival Utsava, and in the Slumbering Roots quest he is not worried that Arabalika is in the Ruins of Dahri. The wiki ties the Contraption to Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, who created it to call timely rains over a section of the desert.

Status as of 7.1: Cleared of the main threat. Nothing found up to Version 7.1 changes the ruin.

216.content: Dahri is an archaic Sumeru term for Khaenri'ah, used especially in Vahumana scholarship. The Persian-Arabic word dahri refers to an atheist or one who denies a creator god, and the game uses it for Khaenri'ah. The Ruins of Dahri and the Valley of Dahri carry the name, and the wiki notes the term refers to Khaenri'ah in the game.

key: The Palace Abandoned by the Gods
217.content:
Safhe Shatranj (also: The Temples Forsaken, The Palace Abandoned by the Gods, The Great Rift, Chessboard of Safhe Shatranj): The Archive describes the plaza as an abandoned, ruined square that researchers believe was once a training field for ancient war machines. Rune mechanisms, sand piles and a huge central device seal the main temple; Primal Constructs still guard it and Eremites roam the canyon. After the Traveler wakes the central device the sand retreats and a plaza with sides of seemingly equal length appears, which is what the desert tribes call Safhe Shatranj.

It matters to the wider story because it is where Liloupar, the Mother of the Jinn, is found and bound to the Traveler, and later where chess pieces on the plaza let the Traveler travel to Gurabad itself and to other ruins.

Geography: Safhe Shatranj sits in the Desert of Hadramaveth, part of the Great Red Sand, in a canyon the Tanit call the Great Rift. Gurabad proper is said to lie hidden in the canyon cliffs, so Jeht and the wiki treat these ruins as its outlying temples and fortresses. The temple on the outskirts is the one the Traveler enters first; its halls loop back to one central chamber with a large device. Beyond it lie a river valley and the Pairidaeza Canyon. Azariq guesses that a spring deep in the canyon is all that remains of an old river valley.

Thick roots break through the stonework in several rooms; Azariq reads this as a sign that the place was far more humid and fertile when it was abandoned. Sealed doors send visitors round to the main hall by alternative routes. The wiki lists a Cascade Pool, Four-Leaf Sigil, Loose Sand Piles, Primal Obelisk and Weathered Obelisk among its exploration features. One of the Towers of Betrayal stands northwest of it.

Places: - The outlying temple of Gurabad: the main ruin, with a Teleport Waypoint, sealed gates and a great central device.
- The central plaza: revealed when the sand retreats, square with seemingly equal sides and a new door in the opposite cliff. This is Safhe Shatranj in the narrower sense.
- Liloupar's Cell: a prison turned oasis with a large tree and a bottle; its appearance changes once it is discovered.
- The chess pieces on the plaza and their activation devices in other desert ruins (Border Fort near Aaru Village, Deshret's Glass Goblet, Khaj-Nisut, King Deshret's Pillar near Opet Hall, the Soulferry, the Temple of Gurabad, and the Mausoleum of King Deshret).

Several mechanisms blow sand away in one direction once struck so that flowing runes form, which is how piles of sand barring the gates are cleared. The tribespeople avoid touching them out of taboo.

People: No one lives in the ruins. The quest The Temple Where Sand Flows Like Tears brings in Jeht, her Tanit senior Azariq, who sees the Traveler through the first gates and then turns back, and Matriarch Babel, who sent them. Liloupar is found deeper in the temple. Eremites are met in the Pairidaeza Canyon beyond it.

Azariq will not go deeper because the ruins are cursed and taboo for the Tanit. Jeht, who counts as half an outsider, is not bound by the same taboo, and the tribe was willing to send her on that basis.

History: Tanit tradition, relayed by Azariq, says the temple was first built by a vassal king named Ormazd in remembrance of the god-king Al-Ahmar. A tribal legend adds that in the days of Queen Nabu Malikata the Great Rift was green and ruled by giants, who grew vines to hear news of the heavens and were swallowed by the earth. Jeht's books say Gurabad fell to fire and the anger of the Jinn, while Azariq thinks the damage looks like the work of a mob, soldiers or tribespeople.

Liloupar's own account is that Ormazd was once her lover and that she brought ruin on his line across three generations. In the vision at Gurabad's gate the city is drowned by a red tide of pomegranate juice and the Jinn pour out of machine husks. These memories are shown through her eyes and reflect her point of view. See location.gurabad and npc.liloupar for the fuller account.

Atmosphere: Dry canyon heat and silence, sand pouring down from cracks when something deep in the ruins shakes, giant roots through rock, and an ancient mechanical hum that wakes when the great device starts. The tribespeople call the place bad luck, so entering it feels like trespassing on something the desert has chosen to forget.

At the cell the plants wither as the bottle is disturbed.

Dangers: Primal Constructs (including a Repulsor-type elite and a forgotten guardian called Anoushbord), Eremite Ravenbeak Halberdiers, Linebreakers, Crossbows and Sword-Dancers, plus Stretchy Geo Fungi and Grounded Geoshrooms. Sand piles block the way until the devices are used, and tremors suggest instability.

Travel: The temple lies on the outskirts of Gurabad and is reached from the Tanit camp by way of the canyon. Once activated, the chess pieces act as teleporters, and the Hidden Exploration Objective needs the Traveler to bring each activation device to its piece.

Quests: - The Temple Where Sand Flows Like Tears (World Quest, the Dirge of Bilqis, part 2): Jeht and Azariq lead the Traveler into the ruins to find the fragment of the Mother of the Jinn, whose aid is needed to enter the Eternal Oasis and restore the tribe's land. The Traveler activates four seal-breaking machines and the central device, reveals the plaza, defeats a guardian, finds Liloupar in her bottle and accepts her true name. Jeht is upset by that choice and is then called back by Babel's messenger.
- Memories of Gurabad (World Quest, Apocalypse Lost): after the Traveler has finished The Fallen Falcon and placed five chess pieces on the board, Liloupar asks to be connected with a piece, shows a vision of Gurabad, and brings the Traveler to Gurabad's gate. By the end she leaves her bottle to rejoin her children in Gurabad, though her gadget keeps working.
- Chessboard of Safhe Shatranj (Hidden Exploration Objective, unofficial name): bring seven activation devices to the seven chess pieces.

Gameplay note: completing the Hidden Exploration Objective awards seven Remarkable Chests and an achievement. Finishing Memories of Gurabad makes the Safhe Shatranj viewpoint accessible and makes the stone tablets of the desert readable.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the ruin stands open and cleared of sand, with Liloupar having left her bottle for Gurabad. The Tanit still regard it as accursed. No later canon changes it.

218.content:
Liloupar's Cell is a point of interest inside Safhe Shatranj. The Archive names it Liloupar's Gaol and asks what dire criminal the prison, now an oasis, once held. When the Traveler takes the bottle, the tree and other plants wither and Liloupar speaks, calling herself a Jinni and a former mother. Its look changes after discovery during The Temple Where Sand Flows Like Tears. Jeht notes that Jinn make contracts by giving a human their true name.

Liloupar later leaves the bottle to go to Gurabad (Memories of Gurabad), but her Jinni in the Magic Bottle gadget continues to work.

219.content: The Temples Forsaken is the earlier name of the subarea. Its Archive entry, The Palace Abandoned by the Gods, tells a desert song of long-lived giants thrown into a rift in one night. Part-way through The Temple Where Sand Flows Like Tears the name changes to Safhe Shatranj and the sand is cleared. The Tanit call the canyon the Great Rift, which Jeht explains as the maw of the earth.

220.comment: Safhe Shatranj: Chess pieces and activation devices
220.content: Seven chess pieces stand on the plaza. Each is paired with an activation device found in a different desert ruin; once the device is placed, the piece becomes a teleport point to where the device stopped. Liloupar connects to a piece during Memories of Gurabad and the Traveler is taken to Gurabad's gate. The pieces' original purpose is not stated in canon.

221.content:
Samudra Coast: Samudra Coast is the far northwest edge of Sumeru's desert, a shore of sandy beaches and clear blue water in the Realm of Farakhkert. Under it lies Madinat al-Nuhas, an old underground weapons testing site of the fallen kingdom of Khaenri'ah.

It was added with the Girdle of the Sands in version 3.6, and is where the wandering Fontaine artist Julien camps in the world quest "An Artist Adrift".

Geography: A beach and bay at the northwest limit of the desert, close to Asipattravana Swamp and the Hills of Barsom. The wiki's etymology note says samudra is the Sanskrit word for a large body of water.

A cave by the water lies between the coast and the swamp. Madinat al-Nuhas can be entered from the west end of Asipattravana Swamp and extends out beneath the coast.

Places: Madinat al-Nuhas ("City of Brass", a title borrowed from the Thousand and One Nights) was an underground Khaenri'ahn facility for testing weapons, particularly Ruin Machines. It still holds an incomplete prototype Ruin Golem and is powered by Azosite, like Hangeh Afrasiyab.

The facility was apparently adapted into a fortification from which Abyss monsters could be attacked, but it saw little use for that purpose. It is unlocked during "As the Khvarena's Light Shows: Nirodha".

People: Julien, who calls himself a renowned artist from Fontaine (the Traveler and Paimon doubt the title), is camped nearby. He came to Sumeru to gather inspiration, found the desert far drier than he is used to, and was planning to go home by water when his raft was washed away. He cannot swim.

After the Traveler feeds him a fried egg, Julien invites them to tea at his camp. A dog named Pepper is on the beach. The quest has the party find his luggage in the water and on the beach, check on the dog and investigate a sand pile, and defeat a Blazing Axe Mitachurl and hilichurls.

Julien says he passed through Chenyu Vale, where the air was still fairly humid, before the dry sandstorms of Sumeru hit him, and that he had meant to leave by water. He also regrets not buying a "mysterious egg" from a stranger that was said to turn aside a day's misfortune; Paimon suspects a scam. He suits wetter climates and was already planning to return to Fontaine with the inspiration he had gathered.

Quests: "An Artist Adrift" (3.6) becomes available after "The Splendorous Sky That Day" and runs in several parts. Madinat al-Nuhas appears in "As the Khvarena's Light Shows: Nirodha".

Atmosphere: Clear blue water and sand at the edge of a harsh desert, with an abandoned weapons facility underfoot.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 nothing is recorded as changing here.

222.content: An underground Khaenri'ahn weapons testing facility under the Samudra Coast, mainly for Ruin Machines, with an unfinished prototype Ruin Golem. Powered by Azosite. Later converted for defence against Abyss monsters. Entered from the west end of Asipattravana Swamp.

223.content:
Sanctuary of Surasthana (also: Surasthana): The Sanctuary of Surasthana is the palace at the very top of Sumeru City, above the Akademiya, in the crown of the Divine Tree. It is the residence of the Dendro Archon, Lesser Lord Kusanali (Nahida). For centuries no one outside the Akademiya's sages had seen the god living there, and the sages used the place as her prison. In the Chapter III Archon Quest she was freed and the Traveler met her face to face for the first time.

The name is Sanskrit-derived and means roughly "abode of a god". Under the sages' rule the Sanctuary was off limits even to ordinary Akademiya staff; since Nahida's rescue the Traveler and Paimon can visit, and she receives them there.

Geography: Sumeru City is built on the Divine Tree. The Grand Bazaar and ordinary buildings sit at the bottom, the Akademiya in the middle, and the Sanctuary at the very top. The official map text calls it a palace at the highest point of the city. Reaching it means going up through the Akademiya.

The map description before the rescue says the Dendro Archon is believed to dwell here and that no one apart from the sages has seen her for the last few hundred years. After Chapter III Act V the text changes to say that the light of wisdom has shone out from here over all of Sumeru under the sages' guidance. The interior opens only after the quest Jnagarbha Day; before that the Traveler sees only the outside, where the guard Ashk stands.

Branches are seen growing from the top of the Sanctuary in the closing scenes of Chapter III Act V, and a seed-like object with branches is glimpsed inside afterwards. The wiki records these as images only; canon gives no explanation, so treat them as atmosphere rather than a plot point.

Atmosphere: Quiet, enclosed and still. Nahida jokes in a voice-over that the wind never blows in the Sanctuary. A scene here feels like a high, sealed room above a busy city, with the noise of Sumeru City far below.

After the rescue the mood is lighter. Nahida talks with visitors here and, after the Archon Quest victory, answers the Traveler's questions in the Sanctuary. In a voice-over about Dori she recalls that Dori's first words on seeing the palace were "Nice palace. How much?" and that she has been unable to work out how much Mora it would be worth.

History: After Greater Lord Rukkhadevata died in the cataclysm five hundred years ago, the sages of the Akademiya found her successor, Lesser Lord Kusanali, and brought her to Sumeru City. Disappointed that the child god showed neither great wisdom nor great power, they shut her in the Sanctuary and turned the people's devotion to Rukkhadevata's memory. A device there, made by Rukkhadevata so she could meditate in peace, was altered by the Grand Sage of the day so that it could no longer be controlled from the inside; Alhaitham describes it as one god trapped by the power of another.

Under the Akademiya's rule the people of Sumeru almost never saw their Archon and most knew little about her. In Chapter III the sages' collaboration with the Fatui Harbinger Dottore aimed to replace her with a made god and to trap her consciousness in the Akasha. In Dreams, Emptiness, Deception the Traveler briefly trades places with Nahida's puppet-self and sees, from inside her real body in the Sanctuary, Scaramouche becoming a god. In Jnagarbha Day the Traveler, jailed on purpose in the confinement room near the Sanctuary, wakes her sealed consciousness. Alhaitham's plan then fills the Akasha with a forged order saying she has escaped the Sanctuary, drawing the guards away.

Grand Sage Azar went to the Sanctuary alone to check the order; because the Akasha had made him expect her absence, he at first failed to perceive her. Cyno met him there and demanded he plead guilty before the archon herself. Dehya frees the Traveler, who then meets Nahida in the Sanctuary. She reverts the Akasha to her own use, revokes the sages' access and prepares to stop the false god, giving the Traveler an upgraded Akasha Terminal. Later Act V quests start from the Sanctuary, including the preparation for the fight in the Joururi Workshop and the conversation after the victory.

People: Nahida lives here, and the guard Ashk stands outside. Before Chapter III only the sages were allowed in; after the rescue Viraf, stationed at the Akademiya, remarks to the Traveler that entering the Sanctuary is normally forbidden.

Cyno, then still General Mahamatra, says at the confrontation with Azar that under the Akademiya's own regulations even its staff were forbidden to come here. Visitors since the rescue include the Traveler and Paimon.

Governance: The Sanctuary has no government of its own. In practice the sages held it as a restricted site, and Nahida had little power over the nation while confined. After the rescue she can overrule the sages; four of the six sages were removed from their posts and sent to retrain in the Avidya Forest.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Sanctuary of Surasthana is the Dendro Archon's palace at the top of Sumeru City, no longer a prison. Nahida is free and the false-god scheme is over. Whether she still lives there permanently is not stated in the sources read.

224.comment: Sanctuary of Surasthana: Rukkhadevata's meditation device
224.content:
Inside the Sanctuary is a device made by Greater Lord Rukkhadevata so she could isolate herself and meditate undisturbed. According to Alhaitham in Jnagarbha Day, the Grand Sage of five hundred years ago modified it so that it can no longer be operated from the inside. The Traveler reaches Nahida's sealed consciousness not through the device but through a modified Akasha Terminal used from the confinement room.

A barrier surrounds Nahida in the Sanctuary until Cyno forces Azar to release her; the barrier then disappears when the Traveler enters. The wiki adds that, because the device was made by divine power, Nahida could not escape it on her own.

225.comment: Sanctuary of Surasthana: The rescue of Nahida (Jnagarbha Day)
225.content:
On Jnagarbha Day, when the Akademiya enters new information into the Akasha, Alhaitham's plan has the Traveler jailed on purpose in the confinement room, where a modified Akasha Terminal wakes Nahida's consciousness. Nilou dances outside the Akademiya while the guards, thanks to Alhaitham's forged order, run into the city to hunt for the supposedly escaped Archon; Dehya and the Eremites deal with them in the Bazaar. Cyno confronts Azar at the Sanctuary, after which Dehya frees the Traveler and the Traveler meets Nahida in person.

The forged order spreads through the Akasha, so guards receive it as if it came from the sages. Azar checks the Akasha himself, discovers an order he did not issue and goes to the Sanctuary to verify it. Nahida wakes only after working through her own self-doubt about being a worthy archon.

226.content:
Azar's justification in Jnagarbha Day is that it is better to keep her isolated in the Sanctuary so the Akademiya does not become embroiled in turmoil; Paimon calls this a pathetic excuse. Nahida was nevertheless able to learn through the Akasha and to act in a limited way in the outside world, for example through the bionic puppet Katheryne and through the mad scholars exiled to Aaru Village, without leaving the Sanctuary.

The original text of her "Toy Box" character story says the Akademiya researchers never supported her novel ideas and would not satisfy her wish for more toys, so she asked for only wood and some tools and made chessboards, cards and puzzles herself, following the instructions offered by the Akasha. After Where the Boat of Consciousness Lies the story is altered and that line about the researchers no longer appears.

227.content:
Sand-Embraced Home: The Sand-Embraced Home is a point of interest in Old Vanarana, in the Lost Nursery of Sumeru. It is unlocked during the Aranyaka world quest For the Children of the Past.

It can be reached by going down from the northern teleport waypoint in Old Vanarana. A mural there can be revisited after the Aranyaka is complete.

Revisiting the mural after completing the Aranyaka grants the achievement Though to the Earth I May Return...

Geography: Located in Old Vanarana, below the northern waypoint. Old Vanarana is part of the Lost Nursery and is affected by the Withering in the quest.

People: Arama accompanies the Traveler through Old Vanarana in this quest and speaks of the Aranara who were lost. The quest includes a step leaving Aramuhukunda's home, but whether it is this place is not stated.

History: The quest has the Traveler gather three Inscriptions of Remembrance, face a seal at the Tumor of the Withering, and uncover a way down.

Unlike most Withering-affected areas, Decay here builds up on its own over time during the quest, while Arama's aura reduces it.

Quests: For the Children of the Past, the second part of Nursery of Lost Dreams, leads into For All Children Who Long for Life.

Atmosphere: A quiet place below ground in Old Vanarana, linked to remembrance of the lost Aranara.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 no change was found.

No 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content was found that mentions it; the Aranyaka itself is the only canon reference.

228.content:
Sekhem Hall: Sekhem Hall is a hall in the eastern section of the Mausoleum of King Deshret in Sumeru's Hypostyle Desert, filled with Primal Constructs that do not attack. The Place of Breath branches off it.

The name comes from the sekhem, a ritual scepter of ancient Egypt. The Scarlet Sand Slate says Al-Ahmar had no enemies, because all who gave him no homage were destroyed by servants that issue from this place and reduced to a handful of sand.

Geography: A map level labelled for the eastern section of the Mausoleum. It has a waypoint, and a hallway off its right side leads, past a primal sconce, to the Place of Breath.

The hall holds many Primal Constructs identical to the boss met at the end of Dual Evidence, but they remain still.

History: It is not the subject of a quest of its own. Players pass through it on the way to the Place of Breath during Dual Evidence. Its role in King Deshret's time is known only from the slate's line about servants that enforced homage.

The line that enemies were reduced to a handful of sand is a grim picture of the king's protection. Whether this was literal or boasting is unresolved.

Atmosphere: A silent hall of motionless guardians: threatening by implication, harmless in practice. A scene here can use the contrast between the slate's boast and the dust-covered stillness.

Dangers: The constructs are inert and do not attack the player.

Status as of 7.1: Open to explore as of Version 7.1.

No source up to Version 7.1 that I checked changes it.

Coverage is thin: the sources give only the slate's line, an etymology and the access route, so the entry is deliberately short.

229.content:
Shamshir's Smithy (also: Shamshir Blacksmith): Shamshir's Smithy is Sumeru City's blacksmith, on Treasures Street. Its seasoned owner Ahangar has been critically acclaimed among Eremite mercenaries. He forges and sells weapons and enhancement materials. The map describes it as proof that even forging can be learned by study in Sumeru, though long experience still counts for a craftsman.

Mansur, an Akademiya researcher from the Amurta school who came to study air pollution at the smithy, has become Ahangar's apprentice.

People: Ahangar says he is a blacksmith who crafts weapons for the Eremites, plus tools, accessories and furniture for others. He can also make wooden weapons, but most of his orders are pattern-welded steel weapons for mercenaries, since many Sumeru researchers are not in the habit of arming themselves and find metal weapons off-putting. He is brief and practical, advises regular maintenance of one's weapons, and has adopted several children (Iradj and Dwarkanath are named); his thoughts turn to hoping the children are well. Mansur is an Amurta researcher who arrived to study air pollution for his thesis, became Ahangar's apprentice by accident and now finds ironworking much more fun than writing papers.

Mansur says the children Ahangar adopted all became researchers or joined the Eremites, so Mansur may end up the sole heir to the craft. He has kept the smithy's serious air-pollution problem from the Akademiya so that it is not shut down, which would leave him nothing to write about; he refuses to discuss the thesis.
