Ahangar is glad to finally have an apprentice. Ahangar will also mark ore deposits on the Traveler's map and challenges visitors to the card game, Genius Invokation TCG.

Customs: The shop's notices record Akademiya rules: large orders of pattern-welded steel weapons must first be reported to the Citadel of Regzar and approved; private orders outside the Teyvat Catalogue of Common Weapons, especially for automatic devices, are suspended; special requests need supporting documents from the relevant school. This shows how closely the Akademiya watches weapons in Sumeru City.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the smithy is open and unchanged.

Nothing in canon through 7.1 changes Ahangar, Mansur or the notices.

230.content:
Shapur Hotel (also: Shapur Inn): Shapur Hotel is the inn of Port Ormos, opened by Shapur and now managed by his daughter Sareh. A lift in front of the building saves guests the long climb up the incline, and it is free for anyone to use. Guests are asked to register their name, party size, reason for the stay and length of stay, though they may decline. Many guests play Genius Invokation TCG.

The hotel's interior can only be entered during Emilie's Story Quest. A cat called Sisi belongs to Shapur and often wanders off.

People: Shapur, the owner, is an older man who is constantly calling for his cat Sisi and, asked who he is, simply says he owns the inn. Sareh, the hostess, is polite and organised and is worried about Amandeep, a messy-looking researcher who lived there for a long time, mentoring young researchers on their papers, and who vanished on the day sea monsters were about without paying his bill. She has asked all of Port Ormos to help look. Also listed around the hotel: Alexandra and Przheva (merchants), Ruying (night merchant), Arayesh (hairdresser), Farahnaz (researcher) and the cats Nargis, Lale and Rozan.

During the Sabzeruz Festival event Chromatic Ode of Candies and Roses (5.1, limited), Shapur calls after Sisi for interfering with the Parade, then insists he saw a Flower Carriage and a cat even when told there is none. Separately, Sareh's idle thought is that, with no news lately, she will not contact the Akademiya for a while.

Quests: Floral Debt, Blood Due is Act I of Emilie's Story Quest, the Pomum de Ambra Chapter. Emilie, a Fontaine perfumer, arrives in Port Ormos for a flower exhibition in the hope of tracing a rumour that the extinct flower Auguste has reappeared. Tighnari helps with the exhibition. Emilie and the Traveler go to the hotel to meet her old teacher Edgar, who is in charge of the exhibition, and the stay at the hotel turns into a murder mystery.

Per the wiki summary, guests die in their rooms over the following days. Emilie and the Traveler work out that a sample of Auguste was hidden in a Glaze Lily with Slime Condensate so that its scent would release only at night, that the whole hotel was a trap set by a culprit called Kirya, and that Kirya had been disguised as Edgar. The chase ends in a domain in the final part, Base Note: Auguste. Motive and aftermath are left to Emilie's own entry.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the hotel is open for ordinary lodging and is unchanged in the overworld.

No later content alters the hotel. Sareh's worry about Amandeep remains open in the hotel's own dialogue.

231.content:
Silver Bottle Courtyard: The Silver Bottle Courtyard is the main town of the Veluriyam Mirage, the bottle-domain from the limited-time Version 3.8 event Secret Summer Paradise. The Traveler's group arrives here after entering the bottle, meets the caretaker Idyia here, and returns to it between stages of the repair. Its resident replicas run game stalls and a lakeside restaurant. It was event-only.

It is unlocked by the first event quest, A Mysterious Missive on Paper Wings, in which Klee, Kaeya, the Traveler and Paimon follow a Magic Invite sent by Klee's mother, Alice, on behalf of a friend in Sumeru. The great wheel at the heart of the town is the Mirage's central hub and the object the whole event is about repairing.

Geography: A town with a west and east side, an entrance facing west, a lakeside restaurant, and the main wheel. It contains a Waverider Waypoint, a Hydro Elemental Monument, Four-Leaf Sigils, Dendrogranum and Rocklifting Branches, and Nilotpala Lotus as its local specialty.

The Spino Blaster station stands in the town but was unusable before the quest Fairground Gathering, Summer Lights Illuminated. The central wheel, ridden by Choo-Choo Cart, has a top platform where Idyia goes to be alone each time a visitor leaves. In canon terms, everything in the Mirage begins as a Preprint, a flat blueprint turned solid by light from the core Streaming Projector.

People: Idyia, the caretaker, is an Oceanid in human form; she is the only resident who is not a Hydro Eidolon replica. Resident replicas here include Chatillon (who runs Spino Blaster), Madiha (Barking Fox tests), Gretchen (restaurant manager), Mandora (a former adventurer) and others, each modelled on a real visitor. Sangonomiya Kokomi came to the Mirage seeking a lost relic from Watatsumi Island.

Idyia's account, per the event: the waters of Fontaine turned painful for Oceanids, she fled and was lost in the desert, and Alice granted her wish to be away from everyone by giving her the Mirage. Visitors left gifts, which she uses to power the domain, and some asked for a Hydro Eidolon copy of themselves to carry on their dreams. Chatillon, per his wiki profile, was a real engineer who has since died. Idyia says Kaveh redesigned many of the Mirage's buildings.

History: The Mirage began when Idyia, hiding in the desert after fleeing Fontaine, received the domain from Alice. Over time, travellers who found the bottle had their wishes granted inside it, and left behind gifts that powered the domain. Not all were pleased to learn they could not take their creations out; some destroyed them. In the event, a Lawrence cousin of Eula's, Lessig, touched the domain's core, a water orb, and the Mirage went into disarray.

Quests: The Traveler, Paimon, Klee and Kaeya enter the bottle in A Mysterious Missive on Paper Wings; Glaze Domain, Multum in Parvo takes them to the courtyard, where they meet Idyia and Kokomi and set out to recover missing components of the central hub. In Back to Normal: The Story Hidden in the Bottle, Idyia places the recovered components in the core. When it still will not turn, Kokomi lends the Shinrou Casket; Idyia wishes that everyone who came to the Mirage will achieve what they truly wish for in reality, and the wheel begins to turn.

Returning Curios, a later quest, has Idyia ask the Traveler to find hidden treasures and bury them at a chosen spot. The Traveler and Klee also ride to the top of the wheel with Idyia.

Details of the residents: Mandora tells visitors she stopped adventuring in the stead of the real Mandora, who left to continue adventuring; Gretchen runs her lakeside restaurant with an unusual dining etiquette in which guests first fetch ingredients; Madiha speaks in test-engineer jargon. Idyia notes that residents' copies cannot hold their originals' memories, so she teaches them using her own memories of those visitors. The name of the Mirage is likely derived from a Pali word for lapis lazuli, per the wiki.

Atmosphere: A pleasant, quiet resort town in a glass bottle, with the odd sense that everyone was modelled on someone who left.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 canon, the Silver Bottle Courtyard is part of a time-limited area from Version 3.8; no later story returns to it.

At the end of the event the wheel was turning again and the Mirage was running normally, with Idyia welcoming visitors.

232.comment: Silver Bottle Courtyard: Idyia, Caretaker of the Mirage
232.content: Idyia is an Oceanid in human shape who keeps the Mirage. She is gentle and wants guests to relax in a quiet place. She is a friend of Alice, Klee's mother. Klee calls her "Aunty Desert" and Paimon "Mud Fairy". She cannot explain Preprints fully, comparing them to the blueprint a seed or egg carries.

233.content:
Sobek Oasis: Sobek Oasis is an oasis in the Hypostyle Desert, part of Sumeru's Great Red Sand. Adventurers crossing the red desert have been known to rest here. A stone tablet nearby promises that a golden sandstorm and burning sun will exorcise the darkness for those who perished here and return their spirits to the Orchard of Pairidaeza.

It was added in version 3.1 with the Hypostyle Desert and is named, in the wiki's account, after Sobek, the Crocodile King.

Geography: A watered spot in the Hypostyle Desert, the deep desert of the Great Red Sand. A teleport waypoint marks the oasis, and the stone tablet stands on the plateau north-east of it.

The Dune of Carouses and its Tomb of Carouses lie in the same desert area; other points in the area include the Garden of Endless Pillars, once part of the sapphire city of Tulaytullah.

History: The stone tablet's blessing speaks of the Orchard of Pairidaeza, the Eternal Oasis, as the destination for souls: "the golden sandstorm and burning sun will exorcise the darkness on your behalf, guiding you who perished here". It is a funerary hope written for those who died in the desert.

Sobek was one of the gods that King Deshret defeated and brought into his service. He became one of the Seven Pillars, the Crocodile King and Captain of Captains, a hot-tempered general who nevertheless blesses the land with abundance; his statues are commonly found in oases and water temples, and some mercenaries secretly worship him. These are the statements the wiki draws from the Guiding Notes and from the NPC Asenath.

Dangers: The general hazards of the Great Red Sand: heat, sandstorms and scarce water. No enemy list is recorded for the oasis itself.

Quests: No quest start at the oasis was found in the pages read.

Atmosphere: A resting place in the deep desert, with a funerary promise on a stone tablet nearby.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 nothing is recorded as changing at the oasis.

234.comment: Sobek Oasis: Sobek, the Crocodile King
234.content:
One of King Deshret's Seven Pillars, defeated in the Archon War and brought into his service. Hot-tempered, straightforward and warlike, yet a giver of abundance; his statues stand in oases and water temples. He appears as a muscular figure with a crocodile's head, half of it blue, and a miniature statue on his head. He is the namesake of this oasis in the wiki's account.

He was later said to be a prisoner in Aaru together with Heryshaf and Thoth, passing the time with tabletop games such as chess, and grew easygoing. Thoth, who calls him "Croco", and the other two were said to have pushed Deshret to defy the Heavenly Principles and use forbidden knowledge, after twice being rebuffed; they were banished to Aaru for what they themselves call their wickedness.

235.content:
Sumeru (also: Nation of Wisdom): Sumeru is the nation of wisdom in west-central Teyvat, ruled by the Dendro Archon Lesser Lord Kusanali, known personally as Nahida and by her divine name Buer. The Sumeru Akademiya, the most prestigious seat of learning in Teyvat, also governs the country from its campus in Sumeru City, which is built into a giant tree. The north is a dense rainforest of scholars, rangers and forest spirits. The south and west are the Great Red Sand, the desert of the long-dead King Deshret and home of the Eremite mercenary clans.

Visitors find a scholarly, exam-obsessed and practical society. For centuries it lived under sages who confined their own god, scorned the arts, discouraged dreaming and fed the people's minds into the Akasha network. Nahida was freed in Chapter III. She shut the Akasha down and has been reforming the Akademiya since, while the old suspicion between forest folk and desert folk slowly eases.

Geography: Sumeru borders Liyue to the east (the Dharma Forest is reached directly from The Chasm), Natlan lies beyond the western edge of its desert, and the far desert lies on the road toward Fontaine. The ruins of Khaenri'ah lie directly beneath it. It has three subregions: the Dharma Forest, the rainforest of the north and east where Sumeru City stands; the Great Red Sand (also called the Deshret Desert), King Deshret's old realm; and the remote Girdle of the Sands beyond it.

The Wall of Samiel stands where forest meets sand, raised to keep the rainforest from turning into desert; the Akademiya maintains it and forbids damaging it. The rainforest grew from desert that the Dendro Archon terraformed with the Varuna Contraption. The Great Red Sand itself is said to have formed about 6,000 years ago, when the first Celestial Nail buried an older forest and destroyed the ancient city of Ys. Ruin devices, sandstorms, oases and colossal pyramids fill the desert. The Girdle of the Sands is a cataclysm-era battlefield whose great rift, Tunigi Hollow, leads down to Khaenri'ahn ruins.

Government: The Dendro Archon is head of state, but the Sumeru Akademiya runs daily affairs. It has six Darshans (schools), each led by a Sage; one of them is also Grand Sage. The current Grand Sage is Naphis (Amurta), Tighnari's old teacher, who is famous for his temper and integrity. The other sages are Baladhuri (Vahumana), Alkindi (Spantamad), Firnas (Kshahrewar), Shakir (Rtawahist) and Rushd (Haravatat). The Matra, led by General Mahamatra Cyno, punish academic crimes.

Most of the civil service comes from the Akademiya; Alhaitham is its Scribe. Mahamata are alumni sent around the country to oversee information, decrees, trade and healthcare. The Navbed handles trade and taxes, with port masters at Port Ormos and Bayda Harbor, and the Vizier administers the Grand Bazaar and Treasures Street. The Forest Rangers protect the rainforest. The Corps of Thirty, an Eremite brigade on permanent contract, keeps the peace in Sumeru City. Under Grand Sage Azar the old sages became authoritarian: they controlled information, banned unlicensed books and finally all public performances, and conspired with the Fatui. After Chapter III, Azar and his three collaborating sages were removed and exiled. Alhaitham turned down the Grand Sage's seat and only briefly served as Acting Grand Sage. Four new sages were later chosen under Nahida's oversight, and Naphis became Grand Sage.

The Akademiya's rules rest on three virtues (Admonition, Ingenuity, Praxis) and six forbidden "sins": interfering with human evolution, tampering with life and death, delving beyond the universe, investigating the origin of words, revering gods without acts of devotion, and attempting the forbidden without fear. Breaking them can mean expulsion or prison. The sages took credit for these rules, but the Temple of Silence originally proposed them. Research on mechanical lifeforms is banned after cruel experiments in Spantamad.

Religion: Sumeru reveres the Dendro Archon as the God of Wisdom. Under the old sages she was a distant, little-respected figure locked away in the Sanctuary of Surasthana; only a few devotees such as Dunyarzad and Nilou honoured her. Many desert people instead revered the ancient King Deshret, sometimes called Al-Ahmar, and some Eremite groups still await his return. Since Chapter III the Akademiya and the people openly honour Nahida, and the Sabzeruz Festival marks her birthday.

Her Statue of the Seven shows a childlike figure seated on a huge leaf. Since Chapter III, the world has forgotten that Sumeru once had an earlier Dendro Archon. The Traveler alone remembers Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, and everyone else believes Nahida has always been the Dendro Archon and simply lost her memories in the cataclysm. Desert faith runs deep. The Temple of Silence keeps the knowledge and memory of Hermanubis, Deshret's jackal-headed minister. Desert folk who settled Aaru Village long ago did so to await Al-Ahmar's return. Before Chapter III some Eremites, misled by an Akademiya disinformation campaign, believed he would soon be revived.

History: Sumeru was shaped by three god-kings, the Dendro Archon of the forest, King Deshret of the desert and Nabu Malikata, the Goddess of Flowers. After Nabu Malikata died, Deshret turned to forbidden knowledge and brought madness, scales and the Withering onto his land. He died ending the catastrophe, and his civilisation broke apart into rival city-states. In the cataclysm 500 years ago, forbidden knowledge contaminated Irminsul, and Lesser Lord Kusanali was born as the new Dendro Archon. The sages confined her for five centuries. In Chapter III they also tried to build an artificial god with the Fatui Harbinger Dottore, but the Traveler and Nahida's allies defeated the plot.

Earlier still, before humans, the Dendro dragon Apep ruled this land, and Irminsul first grew in her court until the Heavenly Principles took both her authority and the tree. In 6.6, Irminsul seized up and Nahida collapsed, and Sumeru had to evacuate the whole rainforest. A Dottore working from inside Irminsul was behind it, and Pantalone backed him. Nahida had the Traveler bring her Mavuika's Pyro Gnosis and burned Irminsul down, and Dottore died with it. The reprogrammed Aaru now holds the world's records in Irminsul's place.

Customs: Learning shapes daily life: seniority depends on academic progress rather than age, and thesis defences are notoriously gruelling. Before Chapter III, Sumeru adults famously did not dream, which the sages praised as rational, and art was seen as useless. People dream again now and the arts are recovering, though talking about art still kills a conversation. The great festivals are the Sabzeruz Festival and the Akademiya Extravaganza.

The Sabzeruz Festival began as a birthday banquet for the old Dendro Archon, at which the Goddess of Flowers danced and purple Padisarah flowers bloomed under her feet. Today it celebrates Kusanali's birthday. Its customs are the Haft-Mewa table of seven foods, an actor playing Farris the Knight of Flowers for the children, and the Dance of Sabzeruz, which Nilou performs at the Grand Bazaar. The old sages starved the festival of funds; Nahida's restoration brought back official celebrations. The Akademiya Extravaganza combines a yearly Wisdom Gala, where the Darshans compete for students, with an Interdarshan Championship held every four years. Before the Akasha shut down, users woke their terminals with the words "May the Mighty God bless us with their voice of wisdom."

Each year the Akademiya gives the Pir Kavikavus Prize to a groundbreaking scholar under forty. The Grand Bazaar's Zubayr Theater is home to Nilou's troupe. Eremite sword-dances and music preserve their ancestors' worship rituals and fighting styles. Sumeru's local wine is frigid snake wine. Desert lore was written in a script credited to Thoth.

Economy: Sumeru's main trade runs through Port Ormos, its largest port. Port Ormos is cheaper and looser than the capital, and smuggling is more common there. Bayda Harbor in Lokapala Jungle is another entry point with its own port master, and Caravan Ribat is the trade post at the forest-desert border. Knowledge itself is a commodity. The Akasha used to give out information by clearance level, and illegal Canned Knowledge capsules were sold on a black market. Eremites hire out as guards and soldiers all over Teyvat and have an open partnership with the Adventurers' Guild. The Bimarstan gives free Akademiya medical care, and Pardis Dhyai supplies the Forest Rangers with seeds and research. Merchants like Dori sell almost anything to anyone.

Sumeru has many state-backed public services but also scams: training centres have sprung up for people who cannot get into the Akademiya, and some of them are frauds. A route from Mondstadt's Dornman Port to Port Ormos has opened. In 6.6 the evacuation and the Fatui's fake "merchant caravans" entering through Bayda Harbor disrupted trade. The Fatui later sent relief supplies from Snezhnaya.

Military: Sumeru has no national army. The Corps of Thirty is the oldest Eremite brigade, founded by thirty mercenaries the sages hired, and it guards Sumeru City from the Citadel of Regzar under its commander, the Parchamdar Rukh Shah. Other Eremite bands guard posts like Caravan Ribat. The Matra investigate and arrest offenders, and the Forest Rangers police the rainforest. In crises Sumeru depends on Vision-bearers and allies. In 6.6 Cyno, Dehya, Candace, Jeht and Eremite fighters stormed Sumeru City while others infiltrated Irminsul.

Foreign relations: Snezhnaya: the old sages worked with the Fatui. Dottore, once the Akademiya student Zandik, used Sumeru for experiments and walked away with both the Electro and Dendro Gnoses. In 6.6 Pantalone financed and covered the attack on Irminsul. Afterwards Pulcinella sent a carefully worded apology and relief aid, and Nahida and Naphis agreed to keep watch on Snezhnaya. Natlan: Mavuika handed over the Pyro Gnosis to resolve the Irminsul crisis and accepted its loss calmly when Nahida came to tell her. Inazuma: the Electro Gnosis and the puppet Scaramouche (now the Wanderer, who serves Nahida) came from Ei's realm. Mondstadt: Lisa and Signora (Rosalyne) studied at the Akademiya, and Collei once lived in Mondstadt. Nod-Krai: Nefer comes from Sumeru, and the angel Nicole came from Nod-Krai with her to help in 6.6. Liyue: The Chasm links the two.

The Akademiya admits foreign students and sends Driyosh across Teyvat, so Sumeru scholars turn up in every nation. Kaeya once stowed away to Sumeru as a boy, hoping to learn about Khaenri'ah beneath it. In 7.1 the Tsaritsa questioned the Traveler about the vanished Pyro Gnosis. The Traveler also told Pierro that the forbidden knowledge had been purged from Irminsul in Sumeru.

Dangers: Withering Zones, whose Decay can kill people who lack a Vision. Fungi, Rishboland Tigers and Ruin Machines in the forest. Sandstorms, quicksand, heat and Primal Constructs in the desert, along with the remains of forbidden knowledge. Hostile Eremite bands and kidnappers. Abyss forces around Tunigi Hollow. Divine Knowledge Capsules and attempts to touch Irminsul's knowledge have driven scholars mad.

Atmosphere: In the forest: humid green shade, giant mushrooms and glowing plants, rain on broad leaves, scholars arguing over theses in taverns and the bazaar's spices and music. In the desert: red dunes, colossal ruins half-buried in sand, oasis camps and wary mercenaries. Sumeru City rises in tiers up the Divine Tree from the docks to the Akademiya, with the Sanctuary of Surasthana at the top.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, Sumeru is at peace and rebuilding after the Irminsul crisis of 6.6. Nahida has recovered and governs openly with Grand Sage Naphis and the Akademiya. Irminsul has been burned away, and Aaru now stores the world's records in its place. The Archon Quest has moved on to Snezhnaya (Chapter VII). At the end of 7.1 Sumeru's Celestial Nail began, like every other Nail, to cast a strange light into the sky.

Dottore is dead. The Fatui still hold the Electro and Dendro Gnoses. The Pyro Gnosis disappeared in the fire. Thoth and Heryshaf of the Seven Pillars are staying at the Temple of Silence. Collei is now a full Forest Ranger and has been freed of her god remains. Alhaitham and Kaveh have repaired their damaged home. After the Nails began to glow in 7.1, Candace, Dehya and Dehya's mercenaries camped near Mt. Damavand in the Desert of Hadramaveth to keep watch.

The Akasha remains out of daily use. Nicole has moved her dependence from Irminsul to Aaru. Before collapsing, Nahida gave the Traveler a flower-shaped key whose secret about an "inverted statue" is still unexplained.

236.comment: Sumeru: Sumeru City and the Divine Tree
236.content:
Sumeru City, the "City of Wisdom", is built up the trunk and branches of the Divine Tree in Avidya Forest. The docks are at the bottom. The lower and middle tiers hold the Grand Bazaar with the Zubayr Theater, Treasures Street, Lambad's Tavern and the Bimarstan. Higher up is the Akademiya campus with its library, the House of Daena. The Sanctuary of Surasthana, Nahida's treetop palace, sits at the very top. The Corps of Thirty is based at the Citadel of Regzar.

The Grand Sage's office is above the House of Daena, which fell out of use while the Akasha was running. In 6.6 the city was evacuated, the Fatui occupied it and Dottore's Irminsul tree burst up nearby. It has since been rebuilt.

237.comment: Sumeru: The Rainforest and the Aranara
237.content:
The Dharma Forest is a damp, layered rainforest of giant trees, mushrooms and rivers. Its areas are Avidya Forest (Sumeru City, Gandharva Ville), Lokapala Jungle (Bayda Harbor, Mawtiyima Forest, Chatrakam Cave), Ardravi Valley (Port Ormos, Vimara Village, Devantaka Mountain), Ashavan Realm (Caravan Ribat, Pardis Dhyai, Apam Woods), Vissudha Field, Vanarana and the Lost Nursery. The Forest Rangers (Vanara) work out of Gandharva Ville, where Tighnari is Forest Watcher. Pardis Dhyai is Amurta's botanical research station. The Aranara are shy, plantlike forest spirits who love memories and songs and can shape dreams. They live in hidden Vanarana and are usually seen only by children. They feared adult humans ("Nara") after the cataclysm took away people's dreams.

The forest's ancient king, the tiger Viaghara, died defending it in the cataclysm; Rishboland Tigers are his successors. In 6.6 Nahida asked the Aranara to show themselves openly to humans, and the Pari Sorush flew a group of them to the desert.

238.comment: Sumeru: The Desert and King Deshret
238.content:
The Great Red Sand was King Deshret's realm. Its areas are the Hypostyle Desert, the Lands of Upper and Lower Setekh (Valley of Dahri, Aaru Village, Khaj-Nisut) and the Desert of Hadramaveth. His giant pyramid, the Mausoleum of King Deshret, rises over the Hypostyle Desert, and the ruins of Khaj-Nisut lie in the Land of Lower Setekh. He ruled through his Seven Pillars and the Jinn, defeated many gods, and with Nabu Malikata's illicit celestial help began building Aaru, an artificial afterlife. After her death he succumbed to forbidden knowledge. The Dendro Archon helped contain the disaster and was shrunk to a child's size by the effort, and Deshret gave his life to end it. Ay-Khanoum, the City of Amphitheaters the three god-kings built together, lies in ruins, and later ruined cities like Gurabad and Tulaytullah record centuries of vassal kings, betrayals and wars.

Aaru Village, guarded by Candace, began as the last bastion of Deshret's people. Desert dwellers long resented the rainforest and the Akademiya. Some believed the Dendro Archon had betrayed Deshret, until in Chapter III a transcript by Deshret's last priest Kasala, which Alhaitham deciphered, showed her as the desert's saviour. Gurabad fell after the Jinni Liloupar, wife of its founder Ormazd, spent three generations orchestrating its destruction in revenge for his tyranny.

239.comment: Sumeru: The Sumeru Akademiya and the Six Darshans
239.content:
The Akademiya is thousands of years old and takes students from all over Teyvat. Its Six Darshans each have a specialty and a uniform colour: Amurta studies biology (green), Rtawahist illuminationism (blue), Spantamad elementalism (red), Haravatat semiotics (black), Vahumana aetiology (yellow) and Kshahrewar technology (white). Their Sages form the governing council, and one of them serves as Grand Sage. Former members include Lisa, Signora and Dottore. Students rise from Driyosh (travelling scholars) to Dastur (two accepted theses) and Herbad, and graduating after thirty is common.

The Six Darshans began as the Six Great Schools, founded together with the Akademiya. Other Darshans came and went over the centuries. One, the Nagarjunites, broke away and survives in the Girdle of the Sands as the Order of Skeptics. The old Grand Sage Azar's console linked the Akademiya's knowledge capsules to the Akasha on Jnagarbha Days.

240.content:
The Akasha was a mind-linking network, worn as a leaf-shaped Akasha Terminal over the left ear, that gave users knowledge according to their clearance. It ran on the Dendro Gnosis and was secretly powered by its users' harvested dreams. The sages used it to monitor people, predict their movements and spread propaganda. Nahida, the "First Akasha Terminal", shut it down after Chapter III and gave her Dendro Gnosis to Dottore.

In 6.6 the scholars searched the Temple of Silence's records for a substitute for the Dendro Gnosis, built an energy amplifier and restarted the Akasha. Every connected mind together then overloaded the corrupted Irminsul. It is not part of daily life today. Long use of the Akasha dulled independent thinking.

241.comment: Sumeru: The Sages' Conspiracy and the Sabzeruz Samsara
241.content:
In Chapter III, Grand Sage Azar and three other sages, disappointed in their "childish" god, joined Dottore to make a new God of Wisdom from the puppet Scaramouche, using the Electro Gnosis. They imprisoned the sages Naphis and Baladhuri, who objected. They also trapped Sumeru in a repeating dream of the Sabzeruz Festival to harvest people's minds through the Akasha, and gathered "divine knowledge" from maddened scholars. The Traveler, Nahida, Nilou, Dehya, Alhaitham, Cyno, Tighnari and the desert fighters of Rahman and Candace's village broke the loop and freed Nahida on Jnagarbha Day. Then Nahida and the Traveler defeated Scaramouche's mech, Shouki no Kami.

Nahida then traded the Electro Gnosis to Dottore on condition that he destroy his other segments, and traded her Dendro Gnosis for his knowledge about Teyvat's false sky. Scaramouche's memories were later reset, and he went on to become the Wanderer. During the crisis Nahida named the Traveler her "First Sage".

242.content:
In the cataclysm the first Dendro Archon, Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, stayed behind to guard Irminsul and was contaminated with it by forbidden knowledge. Because she could not erase herself, she made Lesser Lord Kusanali from the purest branch of Irminsul to be her reincarnation. In Chapter III Act V her lingering consciousness asked to be removed, and Nahida purged her from Irminsul. The contamination cleared, the people of Sumeru could dream again and Eleazar vanished, but every memory of Rukkhadevata disappeared. The Traveler, who is not recorded in Irminsul, is the only one who remembers her.

After the erasure, history quietly rearranged itself around the gap. Her deeds remain, such as the rainforest and the Aranara, who once called her Queen Aranyani, but they are now credited to Nahida or explained in other ways. Nahida still feels a lingering "warmth" she cannot place. The Traveler keeps the secret, as Rukkhadevata wished.

243.comment: Sumeru: The Temple of Silence and Hermanubis
243.content: The Temple of Silence keeps the desert knowledge of King Deshret's era. Hermanubis founded it at Tulaytullah. When a king of Gurabad besieged it, Hermanubis broke himself into Ba Fragments so his followers could fight back. The Temple later went to the rainforest, but about 400 years ago it left the corrupt sages and settled near Thamud Oasis, while the Akademiya kept a hollow office of the same name as a cover. Its leader Bamoun put the last two fragments into two children, his grandson Sethos and Cyno, before Cyrus took Cyno away. After the quest Oathkeeper, Cyno held both fragments. He made Sethos the Temple's leader, and the Temple has been working with the Akademiya again.

244.content:
"Eremites" is a blanket name for the desert's many clans and mercenary bands, which are proud, quarrelsome and often hired out across Teyvat. They are Sumeru's only authorised mercenaries. Some draw elemental power from ancient desert spirits bound in their weapons. The Corps of Thirty, with green scarves instead of the usual red, polices Sumeru City. Other bands range from Dehya's Blazing Beasts to Deshret zealots such as Ayn Al-Ahmar.

Desert people were long treated by the old sages as tools and kept from the Akasha's wisdom. Since Chapter III, Nahida has sent supplies to the desert, and Rahman's band works with Setaria to bring education to desert communities. In 6.6 a Corps of Thirty member, Qanafiya, spied for the Fatui until Nefer and Cyno caught him.

245.comment: Sumeru: The Seven Pillars and Aaru
245.content: King Deshret's Seven Pillars were Heryshaf (his deputy), Sobek, Thoth, Hermanubis, the constructs Bennu (guardian of Aaru's gates) and Shesepankh (overseer of the Jinn), and Apep, who never accepted the title. Deshret sealed Thoth, Sobek and Heryshaf in Aaru, his unfinished afterlife, until someone answered three questions of Nabu Malikata's. In 6.6 Nefer gave the intended answer, "time", which freed them, and the Pillars agreed to open Aaru. Alhaitham and Kaveh, with Thoth's help, reprogrammed it to take over Irminsul's role. Notes attributed to the Belyi Tsar suggest this was Nabu Malikata's purpose for Aaru all along: a system independent of the ley lines and of fate.

246.content:
After the Nod-Krai crisis, Collei dreamt that everyone's identities in Sumeru City had been scrambled, and Nicole's voice told her it was a premonition. Irminsul had stopped processing information, Nahida took the load on herself and collapsed, and the rainforest was evacuated to Caravan Ribat and later Aaru Village. A ley-line barrier sealed Sumeru off from the world. Apep sheltered Nahida, while Jinn sandstorms and Fatui troops harried the desert until Liloupar calmed the Jinn. The attacker turned out to be Dottore, who had entered Irminsul "through death" and, with Pantalone's backing, grew a monstrous Irminsul tree near the city. Sumeru's allies overloaded Irminsul through the Akasha. The Traveler carried Mavuika's Pyro Gnosis across the barrier, and the Traveler and the Wanderer went inside Irminsul while information was redirected to Aaru. With the permission of the Shades Ronova, Istaroth and Naberius, Nahida set the Gnosis alight, and Irminsul burned for seven days and nights. Dottore's own segments dragged him into the flames.

Afterwards Collei was promoted, and in Mondstadt Liloupar absorbed Collei's god remains, which were Nabu Malikata's, before fading peacefully. Nahida agreed to attend the sages' feasts as long as no tomatoes were served.

247.content:
The Withering is a blight born of forbidden knowledge that drains land and life and turns forest into desert. The Aranara call it Marana. Its human form, Eleazar, slowly covers victims in dark scales and was once incurable. When Rukkhadevata was purged from Irminsul, the Withering stopped spreading and Eleazar was cured, but existing Withering Zones remain dangerous and the Forest Rangers still clear them.

Homecoming (3.6) revealed that Tumors of the Withering are the "deaths" of elemental lifeforms that escaped Apep's body when forbidden knowledge corrupted it.

248.comment: Sumeru: Girdle of the Sands and the Pari
248.content: In the cataclysm, the Hydro Archon Egeria fell at Tunigi Hollow. Her body became the Amrita of the Vourukasha Oasis, and the Dendro Archon grew the tree Harvisptokhm from it to anchor Egeria's remaining consciousness. The tree later sealed the rift. To save the tainted Amrita, the divine bird Simurgh flew into it and shattered into Khvarena, whose motes became the Pari, spirits who cleanse defilement and form Laupa bonds with humans. A breakaway Darshan, the Order of Skeptics, guards the seal. In Khvarena of Good and Evil, the ex-Skeptic Klingsor, now serving the Abyss, tried to break it, and the Traveler and the Pari Sorush stopped him.

249.content: Apep, the Dendro Dragon Sovereign, ruled this land before the gods. She consumed Deshret's body by prior agreement and was corrupted by its forbidden knowledge. After Nahida and the Traveler restored her Heart of Oasis with a Fire Seed, she repaid them in 6.6 by sheltering the comatose Nahida. She also warned that she would hold Nahida accountable if the ley lines suffered.

250.content:
Sumeru City (also: City of Wisdom, Sumeru Akademiya city): Sumeru City is the capital of Sumeru and is known across Teyvat as the "City of Wisdom". It is built on the Divine Tree, a colossal tree in Avidya Forest, and falls under the Sumeru Akademiya, the nation's great school and government. Ordinary life, markets and taverns sit near the foot of the tree, the Akademiya occupies its middle, and at the very top rests the Sanctuary of Surasthana, the palace of the Dendro Archon Lesser Lord Kusanali (Nahida).

Height in the city doubles as social rank: the lower levels are for the common folk, and promotion or higher study is spoken of as "moving up". It is where the central events of Sumeru's Archon Quests unfolded: the Akademiya's god-making plot and, much later, the Irminsul crisis.

Geography: The city is built on the Divine Tree, which carries the Akademiya and everything below it. The Grand Bazaar and everyday buildings stand at the base, the Akademiya in the middle, the Sanctuary of Surasthana at the top. The city lies in Avidya Forest, within Dharma Forest, and a river runs from it to Port Ormos.

Saying "down below" in the city is understood to mean the bottom of the tree. Besides the tree itself, the city has outlying districts: southern outskirts with farms and a docks area, and a northern area with farmland and the Bimarstan (the city's medical institution). The Grand Bazaar has three entrances. Students of the Amurta Darshan such as Yasmin monitor and record the condition of the Divine Tree's roots as a precaution.

Places: Grand Bazaar: a lively, artistic market, home to the Zubayr Theater (Nilou's troupe). Treasures Street: the liveliest street, with the Puspa Cafe, the Adventurers' Guild branch and the Citadel of Regzar of the Corps of Thirty. The Akademiya: the main building of the Sumeru Akademiya, with the House of Daena library at its heart. Sanctuary of Surasthana: the palace at the top. Lambad's Tavern: Sumeru's main restaurant, run by Lambad. Bimarstan: the city's medical institution.

Lambad claims to be a legendary sailor; the Adventurers' Guild branch is run by Kamal with Katheryne at reception. The Akademiya's doors open automatically on approach, and it also holds the Razan Garden. In the story the Sanctuary's interior only opens up after the quest Jnagarbha Day. Kaveh redesigned the booth seating on the second floor of Lambad's Tavern. Notices are carried on public boards such as the Akademiya public message board, the Diwan, Kalimi Exchange and Mahamata boards, the Puspa Cafe board and the Zubayr Theater billboard.

People: Residents include Akademiya students and researchers, the Matra under General Mahamatra Cyno, Corps of Thirty mercenaries, merchants, farmers, dockworkers and performers. Nahida lives at the Sanctuary, and Naphis leads the Akademiya as Grand Sage as of 7.1. Kaveh (an architect), Alhaitham (a scribe) and Nilou (a dancer at the Zubayr Theater) live and work in the city; the Forest Rangers Tighnari and Collei visit often.

The Grand Bazaar's inhabitants are described as mostly ordinary people seeking a steady life. Local mercenary groups include the Corps of Thirty (whose Parchamdar, Rukh Shah, is stationed at the Citadel of Regzar) and Eremite mercenaries who take jobs in the city.

Governance: The Akademiya runs the city and nation day to day. Six Darshans (schools: Haravatat, Vahumana, Kshahrewar, Amurta, Rtawahist and Spantamad) are each led by a sage, and the Grand Sage leads them all. The Matra enforce order. Its rules rest on three virtues (Admonition, Ingenuity, Praxis) and six banned fields of research; breaking them can bring expulsion or imprisonment.

The Akasha System, a knowledge network used through terminals, ran through the city, though it is not part of daily life now. The old sages, led by the Grand Sage Azar, scorned the arts as useless, restricted public performance and kept Nahida confined in the Sanctuary for five hundred years. After the Archon Quest's third chapter, Azar and the other sages who sided with the plot were removed and Naphis and Baladhuri were released from imprisonment; Alhaitham served briefly as Acting Grand Sage. As of 7.1 the sages are Naphis (Amurta, Grand Sage), Baladhuri (Vahumana), Alkindi (Spantamad), Firnas (Kshahrewar), Shakir (Rtawahist) and Rushd (Haravatat). Naphis and Nahida work together.

Culture: Learning is the city's pride and its pressure: a degree is notoriously long and stressful to earn, and theses are the hardest hurdle. Under the old sages the arts were marginalised; once Nahida took her place, performance, books and music returned.

Stressed students often escape to Port Ormos. The Sabzeruz Festival honours the Dendro Archon, with the Zubayr Theater as a stage, though talking about art can still be a conversation-killer. Padisarah flowers are a local specialty of Sumeru City. The tree's physical hierarchy is mirrored in a social one: the lower levels belong to the common folk, and advancement means climbing.

History: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata's rainforest civilisation built the city on the Divine Tree. Five hundred years ago forbidden knowledge corrupted Irminsul and Rukkhadevata, and Lesser Lord Kusanali, her successor, was kept by the sages in the Sanctuary. In Chapter III the sages and the Fatui Harbinger Dottore built an artificial god; Nahida was freed and Rukkhadevata was erased from Irminsul at her own request.

By the wiki's reading, Rukkhadevata made the rainforest after parting from King Deshret, her followers (who would found the Amurta Darshan) helped, and the sages assisted her in running the nation. The sages' plot also trapped the people in a dream loop. Recent history (6.6): after the Nod-Krai crisis, Collei dreamed, through Nicole, that the identities of everyone in Sumeru City had been switched. Nahida and the new sages evacuated the whole rainforest's population to Caravan Ribat. Civilians who tried to return were afflicted by an anomaly near the Yasna Monument, and some killed one another. A surviving Dottore, backed by Pantalone, attacked Irminsul from inside, and a massive Irminsul tree emerged in Sumeru City. The Traveler, the Wanderer, Paimon and Tighnari climbed the Divine Tree towards the Sanctuary while Cyno, Dehya, Candace and others fought into the city as a distraction. The allies overloaded Irminsul with the Akasha, and Nahida then burned it with the Pyro Gnosis over seven days and nights.

The wiki's Sumeru history adds other threads touching the Akademiya: Zandik (later the Fatui Harbinger Il Dottore) studied there more than 400 years ago before Pierro recruited him; Lisa, counted its best student in 200 years, graduated in two years and returned to Mondstadt; the Temple of Silence left the rainforest more than 400 years ago, after which the Akademiya created a front organisation to handle information unfit for public release.

Atmosphere: A city of terraces and walkways climbing a great tree: dappled green light, spiced air from Treasures Street, hawkers and students arguing over theses, and the quiet gravity of the Akademiya above. Down below, the Grand Bazaar is warm and noisy; in the Akademiya's halls people speak softly about citations and funding; at the very top the Sanctuary stands in near-silence. After the Irminsul crisis there is a sense of recovery and relief.

Dangers: Inside the city proper, danger is mostly social and institutional: academic misconduct, banned fields of research, and the Akademiya's old habit of imprisoning dissenters. The Matra and the Corps of Thirty watch for crime. In the story the Fatui have operated in the city, through the Akademiya's conspiracy and again during the Irminsul crisis. Outside, the rainforest has the Withering and wild fungi.

Travel: A river runs from the city to Port Ormos, the nation's largest port and a trade and travel hub. Gandharva Ville, the Forest Rangers' base, lies in Avidya Forest. During the Irminsul crisis the population was evacuated to Caravan Ribat.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Sumeru City is inhabited again after the evacuation of the Irminsul crisis (6.6). Nahida lives in the Sanctuary of Surasthana, free; Naphis leads the Akademiya as Grand Sage.

Irminsul no longer exists in its old form: it was burned and its storage function was taken over by the reconfigured Aaru, with no lasting damage reported. Dottore died in the burning. The Pyro Gnosis that Nahida used then disappeared without trace. A letter from Pulcinella of the Fatui apologised for the trouble Dottore caused and said relief supplies had been sent; Nahida and Naphis agreed to keep watch on what Snezhnaya does. No later crisis in the city is shown through 7.1.

251.content: The Divine Tree is the tree on which Sumeru City is built; it holds up the Akademiya. A student named Yasmin jokes that its years exceed all the rice grains in all the pilaf of Port Ormos. Amurta students record the condition of its roots as a preventative measure. The bottom is the common area with the Grand Bazaar, the middle the Akademiya, and the top the Sanctuary of Surasthana.

252.content:
The treetop palace above the Akademiya is the home of the Dendro Archon, Lesser Lord Kusanali. For about five hundred years it was also her prison, as the sages kept her confined within; no one but the sages saw her for centuries. A map description updated after the Archon Quest says that for centuries the light of wisdom shone out from here to illuminate Sumeru. Surasthana is Sanskrit-derived and can mean a temple or residence of a god.

During the Irminsul crisis Nahida invited the Traveler to visit her in the Sanctuary, where a guard, Mu'tasim, was high-strung because of her very vulnerable state. In the final infiltration the Traveler's party climbed the Divine Tree's branches up to it. After the crisis the Traveler met Nahida and the Wanderer there to talk it over.

253.comment: Sumeru City: The Akademiya and House of Daena
253.content: The Akademiya is the main building of the Sumeru Akademiya, built into the Divine Tree; its library, the House of Daena, lies at its heart, and the Grand Sage's office is above it. Students and researchers of every Darshan study here, and the Matra keep order.

254.comment: Sumeru City: Grand Bazaar and Zubayr Theater
254.content: The Grand Bazaar is the lively, artistic heart of everyday Sumeru City, with three entrances and many stalls of handmade goods. The Zubayr Theater, within it, is managed by Sheikh Zubayr and associated with Nilou's troupe.

255.comment: Sumeru City: Treasures Street and Puspa Cafe
255.content: Treasures Street is the liveliest street in Sumeru City. It holds the Puspa Cafe, shops, the local Adventurers' Guild branch (Branch Master Kamal, receptionist Katheryne) and the Citadel of Regzar, where the Corps of Thirty are based under their Parchamdar, Rukh Shah. Padisarah can be gathered there.

256.content: Sumeru's main restaurant, near Treasures Street. Its owner, Lambad, claims to be a legendary sailor who sailed far and wide; it is hard to tell how much he exaggerates, but the food at least supports the claim to know many cuisines. Kaveh redesigned the booth seating on the second floor as thanks to Lambad, who gave him a seat and free drinks when he was nearly penniless; he spent over a fortnight drinking there. The Traveler and Paimon ate there after the Irminsul crisis.

257.comment: Sumeru City: The Irminsul Crisis in Sumeru City
257.content: In Song of the Welkin Moon Acts IX and X the city was evacuated, Dottore's Irminsul tree emerged there, and Pantalone, the Ninth Harbinger, operated from the city with his own agents while a Corps of Thirty spy at Caravan Ribat was exposed. The Traveler fetched Mavuika's Pyro Gnosis through the Natlan border, and the allies overloaded Irminsul with the Akasha. Inside it Nahida got the three Shades' permission and burned it; Dottore was dragged into the flames by his own other segments. Afterwards, Pantalone watched the burning and Dottore bade him farewell using his real name, Feofan.

258.comment: Sumeru City: Chapter III in Sumeru City
258.content: The Akademiya's old sages colluded with Dottore and the Fatui to create an artificial God of Wisdom, crowning Scaramouche as Shouki no Kami with the Electro Gnosis and feeding him the dreams of the populace through the Akasha. The Sabzeruz Festival's dream loop trapped the people of the city. The Traveler, Alhaitham, Cyno, Nilou, Dehya and others freed Nahida, defeated the false god, and Nahida took the Electro Gnosis. She then asked the Traveler to help purge forbidden knowledge by removing Rukkhadevata from Irminsul, after which everyone except the Traveler forgot her and history recorded Nahida as the only Dendro Archon.

259.content: The Akademiya Extravaganza is a festival run by the Akademiya in Sumeru City, made up of the annual Wisdom Gala (Darshan booths across the city) and the Interdarshan Championship, held every four years. It is shown during the limited-time 3.6 event A Parade of Providence, in which Kaveh won the championship and the right to wear the Diadem of Knowledge, then destroyed the diadem after placing it on its stand.

260.content:
Tanit Camps (also: Tanit Camp, Tanit Encampment, Tanit Tribe camp): The Tanit Camps are the tent settlement of the Tanit, an old Eremite tribe, on the southern border of the Desert of Hadramaveth in Sumeru. They were the home of Matriarch Babel and, for a time, of Jeht, the Traveler's friend. After the events of the world quest series Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters..., the camps are empty: the tribe is gone and the Vahumana Dastur Tanjiyy is the only person living there.

The camps are the Tanit's most recent settlement. The tribe prized words and learning but refused to trust the Akasha, so its tents hold many books that were smuggled out of the Akademiya's library. Visitors who arrive after the tribe's fall find ash, abandoned tents and supplies still in place.

Geography: The camps lie in the Great Red Sand, on the southern border of the Desert of Hadramaveth. They are a cluster of tents around the Matriarch's tent, with water on the western side and a bridge leading to further tents to the north. Wadi Al-Majuj, where the final quest of the Her Foes series begins, is nearby.

The camp's layout, as shown by the objects left in it: Babel's tent holds the Akademiya-marked contract and, after the Akasha crisis ends, a merchant's letter; Jeht's tent stands apart and keeps its own note and a list of names; Aderfi's and Masseira's tents hold books; a tent north across the bridge holds a scholarly archaeology anthology.

Places: Matriarch Babel's tent is the centre of the camp. Jeht's tent and the tents of Aderfi, Masseira and others surround it. A water source lies on the west side, where a book of lunar philosophy was left. Aderfi's tent is where the Tanit read their smuggled books; Masseira's is where a joke book was found with a sour note on it. Outside Babel's tent lie the signed contract with the Akademiya and, later, the merchant's letter. Jeht's tent door carries a short cheerful note saying she is out on business, with a stick-figure drawing of herself grinning. After her story ends, the namelist in her tent changes place.

People: While the tribe lived here, the NPCs at the camp were the Matriarch Babel, Jeht (with her companion Benben), the mercenary guards Mendas and Hugeweh, the farmer Yuften, the tent-holders Aderfi and Masseira, and the Falcon Tadhla. After Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters... only Tanjiyy, a Vahumana Dastur from the Akademiya, remains. He came to give educational assistance to the Tanit under a deal that Setaria had made and found the camp deserted.

Tanjiyy treats the mystery as history: he sees the Tanit's tragedy as part of the same record as the legend of the God King, and he has sent his findings to the Akademiya and applied for a new project to study them. He says the General Mahamatra, Cyno, has promised supplies and protection for researchers sent to the camp. He found a few card decks in the tents and is willing to play the Traveler.

Tanjiyy also notes that he found a large number of books smuggled out of the Akademiya, and that any remaining belief in the Goddess of Flowers among the Tanit has probably vanished for good. His idle line, wondering what really happened to the Tanit, is the camp's last echo of the tribe.

Governance: The Tanit had no written law; they followed what was passed down in their blood and habits. A Matriarch led the tribe together with nine Elders, and the enemies they hated most were not outsiders but traitors within the tribe. Babel held the title until her death and, by the time of the Traveler's visit, had removed the other Elders.

Babel's authority rested on the idea that the tribe is a family, so anyone she judged a traitor had betrayed that family. Jeht, a "half-outsider", was used to deal with such traitors. Babel signed contracts on the tribe's behalf, such as the agreement hiring Tanit warriors to escort an Akademiya researcher across the desert.

Culture: The Tanit are matrilineal and revere the Goddess of Flowers. They value words and knowledge but distrust the Akasha, so they educate themselves on long walks across the desert and with books smuggled out of the Akademiya. They trade crocodile products, spices and essential oils to Sumeru's markets and hunt Wenut for spices.

The tribe also raised "Falcons", children lost in the desert and trained as devoted hunters, a custom wiki sources trace to a perversion of the old priests' archery ceremonies. Only a few Falcons are favoured by the Elders. Books at the camp are worn from use: even a volume of Fontainian film reviews has been handled until its pages discoloured. A tribe merchant's letter shows the Tanit's worry that Akademiya researchers who show interest in Gurabad or the Eternal Oasis would bring harm.

History: The Tanit are said to be the oldest tribe of the Desert of Hadramaveth, with many branches, and the camps are their latest settlement. The camps entered the story in Version 3.4 with The Dirge of Bilqis, in which Jeht brought the Traveler and Paimon to meet Babel. Babel secretly meant to seize the Eternal Oasis and its Jinni, Liloupar, and, after the Traveler and Jeht discovered the Orchard of Pairidaeza, ordered the Traveler killed. When the Traveler worked out the truth and told Jeht, Jeht turned on the tribe; the confrontation at the camp left Babel dead and the tribe destroyed.

Babel had removed rival Elders with the help of Snezhnayan supplies and technology offered by the Fatui, then turned on the Fatui. She told Jeht the Traveler had joined the Fatui, and told the Traveler the same of Jeht, to separate them. At the camp's entrance, Babel said she wanted the Oasis for the tribe so it could topple Sumeru, and wanted Jeht as her successor. Jeht answered that her true mother was Ufairah, and refused to kill her best friend. The wiki's tribe page says the survivors were only those Babel had sent to warn the other tribes and exiles who had not been silenced.

Afterwards Jeht, with Benben following, left, free to belong where she chose. The camp stayed untouched, with ash and signs Tanjiyy found disturbing. He reported it to the Akademiya, and the General Mahamatra has promised protection for the researchers. Before that, in the Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises quest, a letter in Babel's tent shows the tribe hearing rumours that the Grand Sage Azar had been deposed and that book restrictions were being lifted.

Atmosphere: An abandoned desert camp: dry heat, tents with their belongings still in them, ash and stains, quiet where a tribe's noise once was. Books, cards and keepsakes make the place feel lived in. Tanjiyy's cheerful chatter is the only warm note.

Dangers: While the tribe lived, the camp was guarded by Eremite warriors and Falcons, and its Matriarch was hostile to anyone she thought a threat. After the tribe's fall, the camp itself is not a stated threat; the surrounding Desert of Hadramaveth keeps its sandstorms, Eremites and ruins, and the Fatui hid camps in the area during the Jeht quests.

Travel: The camps sit at the southern border of the Desert of Hadramaveth. Outsiders were admitted by the Matriarch's permission, which Jeht obtained for the Traveler and Paimon before The Dirge of Bilqis.

Quests: The Dirge of Bilqis brings the Traveler to the camps. Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters... (three parts: Behold, the Sign Comes Like A Thief...; Make Bright the Arrows, Gather the Shields...; For Her Judgment Reaches to the Skies...) ends with Babel's death at the camp's entrance. It is gated behind the series Apocalypse Lost and Rejoice With Me, for What Was Lost Is Now Found.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the camp is abandoned. Babel is dead and the Tanit are gone; only the Vahumana Dastur Tanjiyy stays, studying what happened.

Jeht left with Benben and no longer belongs to the tribe. No later story, including Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya, returns to the camps.

261.comment: Tanit Camps: The Fall of the Tanit
261.content: Babel's betrayal is the tribe's last chapter: she tried to turn the Traveler's friendship with Jeht into a weapon, then ordered the Traveler's death to control the Jinni Liloupar. Jeht refused, killed Babel, and the tribe fell. Babel had already sent members to warn the other tribes of Jeht's supposed treachery.

262.comment: Tanit Camps: Tanjiyy at the Camps
262.content: Tanjiyy, a Vahumana Dastur, came to the camps for educational assistance and found them deserted. He is friendly, treats the Tanit's fate as history worth reconstructing, and offers the Traveler a card game with decks he found in the tents. He does not know the real cause of the tribe's fall.

263.comment: Tanit Camps: Smuggled Books of the Tanit
263.content: Many books at the camp carry the Akademiya Library emblem and were smuggled out. Titles include On Language and Rhetoric (IV), Pursina's Essays: 26, 101 Painful Jokes, Lunar Philosophy, Anthology on Desert-Based Archaeology (III) and a Fontainian film volume that failed Akademiya review. Heavy wear shows the tribe read them often. The tribe merchant's later letter says restrictions on many books are being lifted.

264.content:
Temir Mountains: The Temir Mountains are a range in Gavireh Lajavard, in Sumeru's Girdle of the Sands. They are the main passage between the Desert of Hadramaveth and the rest of the Girdle. Legend says the range was formed from molten metal, and the desert folk treat it as the border of the red desert.

The wiki lists the mountains as the base of the Order of Skeptics, the scholars who split from the Akademiya and made friends with the Pari. They were added in version 3.6.

"Temir" means iron in several Turkic languages. Two minerals are gathered here: Mourning Flower, a crimson flower said to be watered by the blood of martyrs of the cataclysm, and Trishiraite, a stone formed from congealed elemental energy.

Geography: A mountain belt that serves as the primary passage between the Desert of Hadramaveth and the rest of the Girdle of the Sands.

The western range holds Fravashi Trees that can be restored by waking the Pari spirits sleeping in them. A Skeptic outpost stands behind a Statue of the Seven in Gavireh Lajavard, where a note insists on strict control over entry and exit of all mountain passes so that a ceremony and plan can be completed.

History: Trishiraite's description recalls the old Sumeru legend of Dahri, an underground kingdom said to have fallen to the dark disaster of the cataclysm after straying from the true path. Mourning Flowers are said to bloom on ancient battlefields, watered by the blood of heroes who died in that war.

In "Monumental Study" (3.6) the Traveler and Sorush meet Sosi in the mountains and restore a Khvarena Monument by finding four inscription fragments, after fighting Fatui led by Markozov, the "Leader of Those Pursuing Knowledge". Once complete, the inscription records that Amrita and Khvarena extinguished the phantoms mirroring the bedevilled sky, gives praise to the spirits of light and the protection of Dahri, warns that the Khvarena has no beginning or end and the Amrita must be kept pure by ritual prayer, and urges later visitors to be diligent rather than neglectful.

Trishiraite is described as the deep-red ore left after the flames of the sun-swallowing battles died; hardest stones were set alight then, and listeners are told they may still hear echoes of the fighting. The tribes of the plains add a second tradition about Mourning Flowers: the innocents stained by the war's filth are barred from eternal samsara and can only weep among the flowers. Trishiraite was first introduced in 3.6 and its name echoes Trishira, a three-headed rakshasa of the Ramayana (out-of-universe note).

Dangers: Fatui camps, marked by Sosi in Monumental Study, and the wider hazards of Gavireh Lajavard, whose boss is the Iniquitous Baptist.

Quests: "Monumental Study" (3.6) starts here once the first step of "As the Khvarena's Light Shows" is done, and Fravashi Tree quests in the western mountains let the Traveler wake residual Pari. Both belong to the Girdle of the Sands and Khvarena of Good and Evil content.

Atmosphere: A border range at the edge of the red desert, known in legend as molten metal turned to stone.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 nothing is recorded as changing here beyond the events of the 3.6 quests.

265.comment: Temir Mountains: Temir Mountains in Desert Lore
265.content: Loading screens call it a legendary mountain range said to be formed from molten metal, which desert folk regard as the border of the red desert. A Skeptic note on controlling mountain passes shows how important the road is.

266.content:
Temple of Silence (also: Temple of Silence base): The Temple of Silence is the underground base of the organisation of the same name, in the Land of Lower Setekh near Thamud Oasis. Its map description says it keeps silent vigil over all that is ancient. It guards knowledge that survives from the age of King Deshret, and it is now led by Sethos, with Cyno as its de jure leader.

Players unlock it in Cyno's story quest Oathkeeper, in the part "Footprints Sunken Beneath the Sands", after which its entrance reveals itself when approached. It has a square and an inner temple; the Akademiya's office of the same name is only a front.

Places: An entrance leads into a square and then, through an inner door, the temple itself. Inside are a great hall, a ceremonial hall, an east hall, the room of its former head Bamoun, a statue of Hermanubis and a mural of the Bennu.

People: Members shown here include Asenath, Betresa, Charmian, Djer, Intef and Khensa. Sethos leads it; Bamoun, its former head, has died.

Duaenre also appears among its members in the quest "Sage of Sages". Cyrus, a former member, defected from it.

Governance: Tradition says the Temple follows the person who holds the most Ba Fragments (pieces of Hermanubis' spirit). After the duel in Oathkeeper Cyno held both, so he is formally leader, but as General Mahamatra he handed the running of the Temple to Sethos, who pledged to open its knowledge to those he and Lesser Lord Kusanali judge worthy.

History: Hermanubis and his followers founded the Temple after King Deshret's death and settled in Tulaytullah as keepers of Deshret's surviving knowledge. When the king of Gurabad besieged the city and Tulaytullah's rulers betrayed the Temple, Hermanubis shattered his spirit into Ba Fragments and gave them to his followers, who drove the army off but were then shunned. They left for the rainforest, and about 400 years ago they raised a large underground temple near Thamud Oasis.

Distrust of the Akademiya's sages led the Temple back to the desert, and the Akademiya hid the break by founding an empty office with the same name. As faith faded without Hermanubis, Bamoun tried to restore the Temple by implanting Ba Fragments in children: his adoptive grandson Sethos and Cyno. In Oathkeeper Bamoun used Cyrus as a bargaining chip; Cyno beat Sethos in a duel, took both fragments, and Bamoun then let himself pass away.

Atmosphere: Silent, ancient and solemn, a hushed underground sanctuary of statues, murals and guarded halls.

Dangers: The Temple's trials are fought against guardians (Grounded Geoshrooms and Hydroshrooms, and Primal Construct Reshapers) during the duel with Sethos.

Quests: Oathkeeper (Lupus Aureus Chapter Act II): The Mysterious Letter, After Repose, Footprints Sunken Beneath the Sands, Sage of Sages, The Dead Past is the Living Present. These are a major spoiler for Cyno and Sethos.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Temple is active under Sethos and is rebuilding ties with the Akademiya.

Further details: The wiki notes that a Temple of Silence member once commented on Alhaitham's default outfit, but that member likely belonged to the Akademiya's front office. In the book A Thousand Nights, envoys of the Temple of Silence tell a Vahumana Dastur of his mentor's death, and a rumour about Faruzan's disappearance claims she was held within the Temple. A report in the Valley of Dahri also cites an order from the Temple that Khaenri'ah machines be sealed.

267.comment: Temple of Silence: The Temple of Silence organisation
267.content: The organisation proper is covered by its own faction notes. Key points: it is led by Sethos with Cyno as de jure leader; it was founded by Hermanubis; the Akademiya's office of the same name is a hollow front; and the Akademiya's six cardinal sins were originally proposed by the Temple, though the sages took credit for them.

268.content:
Thamud Oasis: Thamud Oasis is an oasis in the Land of Lower Setekh in Sumeru's Great Red Sand. It is where Saleh, the Electrum City of Warriors, once stood. Its Viewpoint text calls oases like it gems adorning the sea of sand.

Saleh was home to the golden-eyed Thamudians and was known for seven walls. The kingdom was short-lived, was drawn into the wars between desert kingdoms and was destroyed; today there is little sign of it. The oasis still gives caravans and wanderers springs and plants.

Geography: A green oasis of springs and plants amid the sand of Lower Setekh. Exploration objects here include Dendroculi, Dendrogranum puzzles and a Four-Leaf Sigil.

History: Saleh existed from the time of King Deshret's civilisation and became known as one of the Cities of the Seven Towers. By Parvezravan's reign inscriptions record it paying annual tribute to Gurabad as King Deshret's primary vassal kingdom.

After King Deshret's death Saleh was one of the many desert kingdoms in the era of warring city-states. Inscriptions name a Khagan, Turan, as its first named leader; he became regent for the young Artaxir and was later ousted and executed as a traitor with his three sons. King Humayun of Tulaytullah, who claimed Shah Ramshahr's throne by marriage, was beheaded at Saleh during an event called the Jinn Uprising. Later the tyrant Badanah ruled it before being assassinated by Faramarz and Makhaira, and after Faramarz's third ascension the people rebelled again, only to be pacified by Makhaira as queen regent of Tulaytullah.

The wiki records that some Eremite tribes descend from the Thamudians, among them the Iab and the Unut, who destroyed each other in a plot arranged by Nefer in revenge for the massacre of the Shimti tribe (Dance of Death: Serpent and Scorpion). These details come from inscriptions and quests, not from the oasis page.

Dangers: Hilichurls of several kinds, a Wooden Shieldwall Mitachurl, fungi and Winged Dendroshrooms, and desert wildlife such as Desert Sumpter Beasts, Red Vultures and Spinocrocodiles.

Atmosphere: A calm green refuge in red sand that carries a vanished city's memory without any visible walls.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is a quiet oasis with no city; Saleh survives only in texts and inscriptions.

269.comment: Thamud Oasis: Saleh, the Electrum City of Warriors
269.content:
Saleh was an ancient city-state around Thamud Oasis, home to the golden-eyed Thamudians, with seven walls. It paid tribute to Gurabad under Parvezravan and later fell amid the wars of the desert kingdoms.

Its rulers named in inscriptions include Turan the Khagan, Humayun of Tulaytullah and Badanah; see the Thamud Oasis history for the order of events.

270.content:
The Akademiya (also: Akademiya building, Akademiya headquarters): The Akademiya is the main building of the Sumeru Akademiya, the prestigious institute of learning and governing body of Sumeru. It is built into the middle of the Divine Tree that carries Sumeru City, above the Grand Bazaar and below the Sanctuary of Surasthana, and holds the House of Daena library at its heart. Scholars, students and officials of the Six Darshans work here. For centuries it was ruled by six sages whose control of knowledge, through the Akasha System, went far beyond teaching.

Under the sages the Akademiya regulated information and secretly collaborated with the Fatui to create a false god. After the plan was stopped in Chapter III Act V (3.2), four of the six sages were removed.

Geography: The Akademiya sits in the middle of the Divine Tree, between the Grand Bazaar and ordinary buildings at the bottom and the Sanctuary of Surasthana at the very top. Its doors open on their own as visitors approach. Inside, paths lead up the tree through places such as Razan Garden, and the House of Daena stands at the centre.

The Grand Sage's office is above the House of Daena, reached by a lift on a raised platform in the library; after the quest Jnagarbha Day the lift is shown going up to the office or down to the confinement room. The confinement room is a completely enclosed space inside the Akademiya, close to the Sanctuary. The Divine Tree is old enough that, in an NPC's joke, it has seen more years than there are rice grains in all the pilaf in Port Ormos, and Amurta students record the state of its roots.

Height in Sumeru City is also a social ladder: the bottom is for common folk and moving up means promotion or higher education. A speaker who says "down below" means the foot of the tree. Many areas have their own message boards, including the Akademiya Public Message Board in Razan Garden.

Places: House of Daena: the largest library in Teyvat, described on the map as once the bank of all the world's knowledge, now overshadowed by the Akasha System but still a symbol of Sumeru. Razan Garden: a serene garden up the tree with gazebos and Padisarah, entered from the Akademiya's doors; its name is Persian for "vines" and the Chinese name means a quiet garden.

Beyond the building: the Bimarstan, a free public hospital staffed by Amurta; Pardis Dhyai, Amurta's botany research centre; the Grand Bazaar and Treasures Street; and the Corps of Thirty, an Eremite mercenary brigade under permanent contract with the sages to keep the peace in Sumeru City. In the House of Daena, borrowing rules say only students and teachers may take books, and some volumes are restricted to higher-level researchers.

Books in the library include the Scroll of Streaming Song, The Folio of Foliage and The Tale of Shiruyeh and Shirin; quest-item books kept there include An Ode to Khvarena, The Lay of Al-Ahmar and The Shepherd and the Magic Bottle. A researcher's note found in one chest jokes about donating 5,000 Mora each time a thesis is put off.

People: The Six Great Sages head the Akademiya, one for each Darshan, and one of them is the Grand Sage. The Mahamata are civil administrators and the Matra enforce discipline.

Researchers hold the ranks of Driyosh (travelling scholars), Dastur (those who passed two theses) and Herbad (prestigious senior researchers). Seen near the entrance and inside: the mercenary Hana of the Corps of Thirty, researchers and students such as Khaldun, Sitt, Yasmin, Yavanani, Ziryab, Hawa, Iris, Shatir and Zinat, and in the House of Daena the librarian Katayoun and the international student Gregor. Panah the Mahamata appears in the library after Chapter III Act V.

Notable alumni and associates include Tighnari (a graduate of Amurta, student of Naphis), Alhaitham (enrolled at seven, now Scribe), Kaveh, Cyno (the General Mahamatra, of Spantamad), Lisa (who graduated in two years and was called their best student in two hundred years, then left for Mondstadt), and the expelled scholar Il Dottore, who as a Harbinger returned and offered the sages a new god. Tsuyuko, Henry Morton and Signora are mentioned as having studied there.

Governance: Sumeru's day-to-day affairs are run from the Akademiya. It is divided into six Darshans, each led by a sage, and the Grand Sage is the central leader among them. Its rules rest on three virtues and six sins.

The Darshans, each with a specialty and uniform colour, are Amurta (biology, green), Rtawahist (illuminationism, blue), Spantamad (elementalism, red), Haravatat (semiotics, black), Vahumana (aetiology, yellow) and Kshahrewar (technology, white). The three virtues, from Sumeru's talent books, are Admonition, Ingenuity and Praxis, likened to branches, leaf-veins and roots of the nation of wisdom. The six sins, banned to protect scholars from careless pursuit of knowledge, are interfering with human evolution, tampering with life and death, delving beyond the universe, investigating the origin of words, revering gods without acts of devotion, and attempting the forbidden and fearing none. Breaking these invites expulsion or imprisonment.

Other offices: the Mahamata (Akademiya alumni sent across Sumeru to oversee information, decrees, trade and healthcare; the Scribe belongs here), the Matra (disciplinary officials, including inspection for illegal Canned Knowledge), the Navbed (port and tax affairs), the Vizier (administration in the Grand Bazaar and Treasures Street) and the Temple of Silence, which the wiki says was a front, the true order having left for the desert four hundred years ago (revealed in the quest Oathkeeper). Mechanical-life research is banned after past cruelty in animal vivisection.

Culture: The Akademiya admits students who pass its entrance exams, children included at schooling age. Degrees are famously long and stressful, with the thesis defence the hardest hurdle.

Students call each other seniors and juniors by academic progress rather than age, and those who cannot enrol rely on the Akasha, independent study or training centres. The Akademiya's views shaped Sumeru: it disparaged art as impractical, which spread to the public, marginalising performers, dancers and designers; even after Chapter III, talk of the arts is called a quick way to kill a conversation. Each year the Pir Kavikavus Prize goes to a promising scholar under forty.

Students may take elective courses outside their own Darshan, and there is a swimming elective. The habitual liar Kasim claims some sages are officially affiliated with the Fatui, and the Amurta sage Siman Farrokhzad has ties to an Eremite tribe that once worked for the Fatui; the wiki cautions that little evidence supports a wider link.

History: The Akademiya was founded by Greater Lord Rukkhadevata with its first Darshans, and was already prestigious by the cataclysm five hundred years ago. After her death, the sages, disappointed with the new god Kusanali's lack of obvious wisdom, locked her in the Sanctuary of Surasthana, took control of the Akasha System, and ran the nation themselves.

In Chapter III, Il Dottore returned and offered to make a new god. Azar and three other sages accepted; Naphis of Amurta and Baladhuri of Vahumana refused and were imprisoned. The plan involved harvesting divine knowledge from crazed scholars, a dream samsara run through the Akasha, and misinformation about King Deshret's revival, with Scaramouche modified as the vessel. The sages banned unapproved information, then public performances, which led to the Sabzeruz Festival crisis. In Dreams, Emptiness, Deception, Dottore also used the Akasha to stage a mob scene at the Akademiya's entrance and had the sage's secretary Setaria imprisoned.

Jnagarbha Day, when new information is entered into the Akasha, was chosen for the rescue. Alhaitham led the Traveler in through the front door and into the House of Daena, where Azar caught them, exiled Alhaitham to Aaru Village and jailed the Traveler in the confinement room; this was a staged ploy. Nilou's dance outside drew attention, the forged order drew away the guards, and Cyno forced Azar to answer to Nahida. Afterwards the four sages involved were removed and exiled to the Avidya Forest to cultivate their wisdom, Naphis and Baladhuri were freed, and Nahida personally oversaw the choice of new sages. Nahida then halted the Akasha System.

Atmosphere: A scholarly place where wisdom is also pressure: students in the colours of different Darshans pass by, researchers worry about theses, and mercenaries of the Corps of Thirty keep order. Under the sages it was watchful and controlling over information; after Chapter III it is a looser, less certain institution.

The House of Daena at the centre is vast and, per the wiki, used less than before because people relied on the Akasha. Razan Garden is serene, with gazebos and the public message board.

Dangers: The risks are social and informational: the Matra punish forbidden research and Canned Knowledge, the Akasha once shaped what people were allowed to know, and entry to certain places, such as the Sanctuary, was restricted.

Travel: The Akademiya is reached by climbing the Divine Tree from the Grand Bazaar. Doors lead up to Razan Garden and on to the Sanctuary of Surasthana.

Quests: Chapter III of the Archon Quests: Dreams, Emptiness, Deception (3.1) and Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises (3.2), especially Jnagarbha Day.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Akademiya continues as Sumeru's centre of learning and administration under reformed leadership. The sages who planned the false god were removed after 3.2; Naphis is Grand Sage, with Baladhuri, Alkindi, Firnas, Shakir and Rushd as the other sages (as shown in 6.6). Nahida halted the Akasha after Chapter III; during the 6.6 Irminsul crisis it was briefly restarted so the allies could overload Irminsul, and it is not shown back in everyday use. The sages' history of controlling information still shapes habits.

The old assumption that knowledge could be obtained from the Akasha has been replaced by the slower route of study; training centres and the Mahamata remain.

271.content:
The largest library in Teyvat, at the heart of the Akademiya. Run by a Grand Conservator who procures and maintains the collection; the previous holder retired, and Rifaet and Vikram were the candidates. Shatir calls Lisa "Mondstadt's Grand Conservator" and says she would have been his first choice had she stayed. Daena is a Zoroastrian term for insight and revelation.

Only students and teachers may borrow books. A lift on the central platform goes to the Grand Sage's office and the confinement room after Jnagarbha Day. In Chapter III the Traveler and Alhaitham go into the library to lie low before Azar finds them.

272.content: A calm garden on the path up the Divine Tree, reached by the Akademiya's left or right doors, with gazebos and Padisarah. Researchers and students such as Darya, Farghani, Homayun, Makhfi, Muganna, Qushji, Arina and Armin are found here. The Akademiya Public Message Board stands in the garden.

273.comment: The Akademiya: Grand Sage's office and the confinement room
273.content:
Above the House of Daena sits the Grand Sage's office, with the Grand Sage's console, through which restricted commands are executed; on Jnagarbha Day the sages load research and decrees into Knowledge Capsules for entry into the Akasha.
