The perils near Vanarana are Vanagni (the Aranara name for Whopperflowers, which Arama says answer only with rage and flames) and, in the past, the Withering of Marana, which still marks Old Vanarana until Aranyaka Part III. Fire and salt are feared by the Aranara.

Marana is, in Araja's telling, the name of death: it urges everything toward death and chooses "avatars", tall dark warped beings. Araja says these are stories and not his own memories.

Travel: Humans cannot normally find the way. In the world's story, a visitor plays the five-note Rhythm of the Great Dream on a lyre in front of the strange arch to enter, and again at the Silapna to move between real and dream Vanarana. The Traveler borrowed a Mondstadt-style lyre from Amadhiah in Vimara Village.

Only children, and a few adults whom the Aranara trust (such as Rana and, in the wiki's note, Yoimiya), can see the Aranara.

Quests: The key quest is Aranyaka (World Quest series, 3.0), especially Part II "Dream Nursery" (The World of Aranara, Children of the Forest, Encounter in the Woods, An Unwavering Culinary Dream, Varuna Gatha, For a Better Reunion, Festival Utsava). Parts III and IV concern Old Vanarana and Rana's awakening. Smaller quests include Trees and Dreams (unlocks the Tree of Dreams) and The Viparyas of Vanarana.

No Archon Quest is required for Aranyaka. In gameplay, offering Dendro Sigils to the Tree of Dreams increases Vanarana's Favor and unlocks rewards.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Vanarana is at peace, with the Aranara safe in the dream village and the threat from Marana's Avatar ended.

Old Vanarana began to recover after Marana's Avatar was destroyed; Arama is now an Ashvattha Tree. Arana and Rana have set off on a journey together.

No later events (6.x, 7.0-7.1) were found that change Vanarana.

325.comment: Vanarana: Tree of Dreams and Araja
325.content:
The Tree of Dreams grows in a cave at the heart of Vanarana and seems sentient. Per the wiki, Araja turned his original body into the tree after the Cataclysm so he could sustain a dream large enough for the other Aranara. His body cannot move, but his mind can manifest a body inside the dream. At Festival Utsava he reveals that he cannot leave the dream because he is the Tree of Dreams. Over about 500 years he has lost many memories.

Araja's friends in the past were Araji, Arapacati and Aramuhukunda, and he took part in the last Festival Utsava before the dream. In play, the tree is where Dendro Sigils are offered (Vanarana's Favor, gameplay). Arama also mentions "the very first Ashvattha's Tree of Dreams" rooted in Sarva; whether it is the same tree is unclear.

326.content: The Aranara's festival, held in the dream Vanarana during Aranyaka. The Traveler and Paimon collect a flower from each Aranara as a token of friendship, everyone plays the Rhythm of the Great Dream on the stage, and Arama weaves the flowers into a garland for the Traveler. It is a permanent quest and not a limited-time event.

327.comment: Vanarana: Old Vanarana and Marana's Avatar
327.content: Old Vanarana was the Aranara's home for hundreds of years before the Cataclysm. Afterwards they sealed Marana's Avatar deep inside with four layers of seals, including three Inscriptions of Remembrance by Aramaha, Arayama and Araji, who became Vasara Trees. Corruption still leaked, until the Traveler and Arama broke the seals, entered the Land of Grounded Dreams and destroyed the Avatar in Aranyaka Part III. Old Vanarana then began to heal.

328.content: A small garden in a cave at the west end, tended by Aranakula and Arakara, who grow "happy Viparyas". The name is unofficial wiki usage. After the quest The Viparyas of Vanarana the 13 Viparyas can be harvested; in the real clearing the plants are Sweet Flowers instead.

329.content:
Vanarana Nursery: Vanarana Nursery is an unofficial name for a small garden in a cave at the west end of Vanarana in Sumeru. The Aranara Arakara and Aranakula tend it, working hard to grow happy Viparyas.

Arakara is always there; Aranakula returns after the Traveler helps restore the Varuna Contraption in A Prayer for Rain on the Fecund Land (this timing is flagged as unverified). In the real Vanarana, Varsha can be found at the nursery after Giving Flowers.

After the quest The Viparyas of Vanarana, all 13 Viparyas can be harvested and respawn every three days. In the real Vanarana they are replaced by Sweet Flowers; harvesting one kind does not remove the other.

Geography: A cave garden on the western edge of Vanarana. It looks different in the dream version, with blooming Viparyas, and the real version, with Sweet Flowers.

People: Arakara and Aranakula, Aranara gardeners. Varsha visits the nursery in the real Vanarana after Giving Flowers.

Quests: The Viparyas of Vanarana and Giving Flowers, both world quests.

Atmosphere: Small, gentle and tended, a patient corner of a village of dreams.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 no change was found.

The wiki flags this page as a stub, so details here may change when a fuller source is found.

330.content:
Veluriyam Mirage (also: Bottleland): The Veluriyam Mirage, nicknamed Bottleland, is a pocket world inside a wondrous glass bottle, said to lie hidden in Sumeru's desert. It appears only in the limited-time 3.8 event Secret Summer Paradise. Its caretaker is Idyia, an Oceanid who fled Fontaine, and the place is built to grant visitors a quiet respite and their heart's desires.

The invitation came through Klee's mother Alice, who sent Klee a letter and a "Magic Invite". Klee, Kaeya, the Traveler and Paimon arrive, meet Collei, Eula and Sangonomiya Kokomi already inside, and find the Mirage's central hub broken. The party gathers three missing parts to start it again; the deeper reveal is that the town's residents are Hydro Eidolon copies of earlier guests.

The place runs on "Preprints," two-dimensional blueprint spaces entered through Streaming Projectors, with light reflected through the bottle turning them into the world. Idyia states that this kind of magic works only inside the bottle.

Geography: Inside the bottle is a humid, green and watery pocket world, a striking contrast with the desert outside. The official loading text calls it a beautiful, quiet domain where special Hydro life-forms live. Game-wise it is a limited-time area rather than an actual Domain, although the story calls it one. The main hub is the Silver Bottle Courtyard, with a giant wheel, the Central Hub, above it; the Overgrown Valley holds a cavern with a painter's hidden mural.

Travel is helped by the Choo-Choo Cart, a cart ride in the area run by three caretakers (Ferdinand, Jeroney, Haddo). Exploration features include Hydro Eidolons, Streaming Projectors, Gleaming Lamps, Four-Leaf Sigils, Valaya (the Sumeru ring puzzle) and Bloatty Floatty, plus Nilotpala Lotus and Kalpalata Lotus as local specialties.

Places: Key places: the Silver Bottle Courtyard (arrival point); the fairground and its big tent run by Maymunah, a Spantamad scholar; Zosimos's treehouse theatre; the cart area; the Overgrown Valley; and the Central Hub with the Ferris-wheel ride that works again at the end.

The fairground tent is itself a domain-like challenge area. The blueprint core of the Mirage is a spindle, set in a Preprint, where the three repaired components are fitted together.

People: Idyia is the Oceanid caretaker, called "Aunty Desert" by Klee and "Mud Fairy" by Paimon, a wish-granting fairy of local legend. Maymunah runs the fairground; Zosimos is a stage director; Lessig, a visitor from the Lawrence Clan, came to the Mirage to try to restore his family's honour and caused the breakdown by accident. Eula came after hearing a Lawrence Clan cousin had gone to Sumeru, Collei helped guide the group, and Kokomi came looking for the lost Shinrou Casket.

The three caretakers of the cart area were rescued by Idyia from a sandstorm after an adventure. A painter's diary found around the Overgrown Valley describes someone who asked Idyia to improve his skill and was declined, since she does not force changes on others and thinks shortcuts are not good.

History: Idyia fled Fontaine after the old waters grew full of pain and hatred (she speaks of Oceanids fleeing, and mentions Rhodeia, who has since settled in Qingce Village in Liyue), and collapsed in the desert. According to the wiki's profile, Alice met her and granted her wish for a place away from everyone by giving her this bottle. Over time travelers found it, their wishes were granted, and they left gifts that powered the Mirage and were copied by Hydro Eidolons.

Preprints, Idyia says, are like the blueprints seeds and eggs carry, and light through the bottle turns them into the Mirage; the diary fragments say a painter visited for months, and treasure ciphers called Returning Curios (an event quest) were left by guests who hid mementos and stories. Idyia explains that some guests became upset when they could not bring creations outside; others asked for Hydro Eidolon copies of themselves to carry on their dreams.

According to the wiki, many buildings were redesigned by Kaveh (Idyia says so in a quest). The finale of Act III has Kokomi explain that every resident has an elemental signature despite lacking a Vision, so Hydro Eidolons can take any form including human. Idyia reveals herself as an Oceanid; the components are the gifts guests left her; and Kokomi borrows the Shinrou Casket, a relic that gathers shinki from the prayers made to it, from the core and gives Idyia the wish: that everyone who came to the Mirage achieve what they truly wish in reality. The Central Hub starts again.

Atmosphere: A fairground summer: warm lamplight, water droplets that guide visitors, painted flats, a Ferris wheel and little trains, and a hush beneath. Visitors feel like guests of a mild, slightly shy host who regrets her first greeting going wrong. Cheerful nostalgia and loneliness sit side by side, since Idyia says she often rides the wheel alone after someone leaves.

Dangers: Minor: the Silver Bottle Courtyard has slimes, Cryoshrooms and mitachurls as ordinary exploration enemies. The real trouble is the broken core, which stalled the central hub and trapped Hydro Eidolons in the fairground tent.

Travel: Entry is by an invitation. In the story the party uses Klee's Magic Invite to teleport to the desert and Klee calls for help; a bottle appears and they enter it. Items cannot be carried out, Idyia says.

Quests: Secret Summer Paradise (3.8): Act I "An Invitation From Afar!" (A Mysterious Missive on Paper Wings; Glaze Domain, Multum in Parvo; Zip Along), Act II "Mirage Paradise in Crisis!" (Fairground Gathering, Summer Lights Illuminated), Act III "Dreams and First Encounters!" (Treehouse Theater: Candlelit Shadows Dancing; Back to Normal: The Story Hidden in the Bottle), plus the event quests Capturing Light and Shadow and Returning Curios. The event also gave the playable Layla as a reward for collecting Fascinating Phenocrysts and Kaeya's outfit Sailwind Shadow for Joyeux Vouchers.

Status as of 7.1: The Mirage was available only during Version 3.8's event and is not a permanent part of the map. No later events or quests revisit it that were found as of 7.1.

331.content: Idyia is an Oceanid and the caretaker of the Veluriyam Mirage. She fled Fontaine when the waters changed and, per the wiki's profile, is a friend of Alice. She hopes visitors will find some respite from their journeys and looks after the wishes guests have left in her care. In the finale she reveals her true form as an Oceanid and wishes on the Shinrou Casket.

332.comment: Veluriyam Mirage: Hydro Eidolons and Preprints
332.content: Hydro Eidolons are the water-made residents of the Mirage and can take any form, including copies of earlier guests. Preprints are two-dimensional spaces on murals reached through Streaming Projectors, which turn the exploration into a platformer; the official description says they are accessible 2D spaces akin to murals.

333.content: A relic lost from Watatsumi Island that listens to the wishes of those who pray to it, building up shinki, the source of its power. Kokomi came to the Mirage because all clues pointed here. During the finale she asks Idyia to use it to make a wish that restores the Central Hub.

334.content:
Village Chief's House (also: Aaru Village chief's house, Uncle Anpu's house): The Village Chief's House is the home of Uncle Anpu, the Aaru Village chief, in the Great Red Sand. He has led Aaru Village for a long time and offers travellers food and lodging to the best of his ability. At night the village guard Belkacem is also found here.

Anpu warns desert travellers that loose sand or unusually strong wind is a sign to shelter in the village at once, although it does not guarantee a sandstorm.

People: Uncle Anpu is kind, a little long-winded and proud of looking after his village; he says he has seen many reckless people get into trouble in the desert and urges the Traveler to respect danger. After the Traveler completes King Deshret and the Three Magi, he mentions that the village boy Isak wants to thank the Traveler and says he is a good example to children. His idle thoughts wonder whether he is fulfilling his duties as village chief; at night he is surprised by some events he heard of. Belkacem is a guard on duty by night.

In Dreams, Emptiness, Deception (Chapter III Act III) the Traveler and Dehya are staying in the village when Anpu arrives and explains that the Village Keepers have gone missing without a trace. Cyno tells the Traveler that the Keepers are exiled Akademiya scholars whose ramblings the Akademiya wanted away from other people, and explains how the village first shunned them.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Anpu is still village chief.

No quest through 7.1 changes the house. The Village Keepers' fate is told in Archon Quest content rather than here.

335.content:
Vimara Village (also: Vimara): Vimara Village is a small, tranquil fishing village on the river between Sumeru City and Port Ormos, in Ardravi Valley. Many caravans pass through it travelling between the two, though few merchants stay. Its viewpoint text says there is nothing to the village apart from a tranquil life and invites exhausted travelers to rest a while. It is also where the Aranyaka quest series, about the shy plantlike Aranara and the village's missing children, takes place.

The village chief is the elderly Amadhiah. Forest Rangers (called Forest Watchers in the quests), such as Rana, patrol the surrounding woods, which contain Withering zones.

Geography: Vimara Village stands beside the great river Ardravi, in Ardravi Valley within the Dharma Forest region. Ardravi Valley's own description calls the river Sumeru's great waterborne mercantile route, kept pure by the Forest Watchers. The river path leads one way to Sumeru City and the other to Port Ormos.

Nearby are Gandharva Ville (the Forest Rangers' base), Devantaka Mountain and, further into the forest, Vanarana, the Aranara's dream-nursery. The valley's local specialties are Nilotpala Lotus and Rukkhashava Mushrooms. In the open world the village has a fishing spot, a Waverider waypoint and a Four-Leaf Sigil, plants used for quick travel.

People: Vimara has a small cast of villagers: the chief Amadhiah, the merchants Bahram and Yuewen, the hunter Aurelius, a researcher named Nabati, and several children. Bahram says business just covers his costs, but fewer merchants means less competition and it is peaceful there.

Amadhiah's family includes Iosaphat, his child, and the grandchildren Kavus and Sudabeh. Iotham is another of the village children. Alphonso, a young man who says he is an apprentice from Fontaine, has lived in the village for years and is close to Rana and the children. Other villagers listed in the area include Arezo, Banka, Granny Jehiet (who comes from the desert), Kumar, Kurash and Zadith (a student). Rana, a Forest Watcher, grew up in the village and still keeps a house there, though her patrols bring her home less often.

Culture: Village life is slow and modest, with fishing, herb gathering (Sudabeh went out for herbs for Amadhiah) and passing trade. Amadhiah keeps a Vintage Lyre that he received from a bard who once came from Mondstadt, and lends it to the Traveler. Iotham calls the desert "Valuka" and says Granny Jehiet comes from there; he claims he has heard of the Aranara only through her stories. Amadhiah worries over the children and says Rana pushes herself too hard, hoping she finds something worthwhile on her journey.

History: Nothing in the sources read gives a founding date or older history for Vimara Village. It was introduced in version 3.0 with Sumeru, and the village's story in canon is that of the Aranyaka series. Its name's etymology is a variant of Sanskrit vimala, meaning "purity".

Quests: The Aranyaka world quests begin around the village. In Woodland Encounter, the Traveler and Paimon meet Rana, who guides them here. The village's children have gone missing in turn and come back days later with no memory of it. After the Traveler's party drives off Eremites chasing Iotham, defeats a Fatui ambush in a cave and frees him from a Withering zone, Rana falls ill and is taken by the Aranara Arana, who explains she needs a Bija to recover.

Amadhiah lends the Traveler a Vintage Lyre so they can play the Rhythm of the Great Dream and enter the dream version of Vanarana. In the later parts the Aranara host the Festival Utsava, the corrupted Marana is fought, and Arana gives up her memories to make the Bija. Back in Vimara Village, the Bija wakes Rana, who receives a Dendro Vision and leaves with Arana to make new memories.

Arana confessed that she had put the missing children to sleep and removed part of their memories before returning them, which is why they remembered nothing; she says that children forget the Aranara when they grow up. Sudabeh was the first to go missing, while gathering herbs for Amadhiah, and Kavus followed. In the hidden exploration objective The Bad Guy in Vimara Village, the Traveler can unmask Alphonso as Trofin Snezhevich, a Fatui agent raised by the House of the Hearth and sent to capture an Aranara: he had tricked the children into going into the forest alone so the Fatui could seize them, and the Aranara rescued them and wiped those memories. Confronted, he either leaves for good or dies fighting; Amadhiah, unaware of the truth, later wonders why he left without a word.

Atmosphere: Quiet water, fishing lines, boats passing and caravans stopping to rest. Under the trees there are patches of Withering, and Forest Watchers walk the paths. The air is warm and slow, and the villagers expect little excitement.

Travel: Caravans and boats pass along the river between Sumeru City and Port Ormos. A Waverider waypoint helps river travel. Few merchants stay overnight because most go on to Port Ormos.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Vimara Village is a quiet riverside stop. Rana left on a journey with Arana at the end of the Aranyaka quests, and Amadhiah hopes she finds something worthwhile.

No story event specific to the village is recorded after the Aranyaka quests. The rainforest was evacuated in the 6.6 Irminsul crisis; the sources do not say anything about the village in particular.

336.content: The elderly chief of Vimara Village, with weak eyesight he apologises for. He lends the Traveler a Vintage Lyre that he received from a Mondstadt bard. He is a grandfather to Kavus and Sudabeh, and fond of Rana. He vaguely remembers the Aranara as plantlike fairies and knows only stories.

337.comment: Vimara Village: Children of Vimara and the Aranara
337.content: Several children of Vimara Village vanished into the woods and came back days later with no memory, because the Aranara Arana had put them to sleep and wiped part of their memories after befriending them. The adults could not find them and the Traveler's early attempts to coax the truth out of the children by telling stories failed. Iotham was later rescued from a Withering zone in a cave.

338.content: A Forest Watcher who grew up in Vimara Village and guides the Traveler there. Despite lacking a Vision, she charges into a Withering zone to save Iotham and falls sick, then recovers when the Bija is brought. At the end she receives a Dendro Vision and leaves the village with Arana, after telling Tighnari of her plans.

339.comment: Vimara Village: Port Ormos and the River Route
339.content: Port Ormos is Sumeru's largest port, a trading hub beneath two giant trees where smuggling is more common than in Sumeru City and prices are lower. A river runs from Sumeru City to the port, and Vimara Village sits on it, so caravans between the two often pass through.

340.content:
Vissudha Field (also: Vissudha): Vissudha Field is a green, open area of Sumeru's Dharma Forest, just outside Sumeru City. Its notable feature is the Fane of Ashvattha, which holds the Ashvattha Tree, the oldest Vasara Tree and the progenitor of the Aranara, and which seals the entrance to the Aranara's old home, Old Vanarana. Mushrooms grow here, a Jadeplume Terrorshroom lurks in it, and the Aranara tie it to the Aranyaka quests.

It was released in Version 3.0 and extended west in 3.4 so that it joins the Desert of Hadramaveth. Its name draws on Vissudha, the fifth chakra in Hindu tantra, a symbol of purity.

Geography: The field lies in the Dharma Forest subregion of Sumeru, and Travelers' Tales anecdotes place it outside Sumeru City. It holds a Statue of The Seven, a fishing point, and one subarea, the Fane of Ashvattha. The wiki lists Rukkhashava Mushrooms and Nilotpala Lotus as local specialties.

In Version 3.4 the area was expanded west to connect with the Desert of Hadramaveth, so it serves as a green threshold between the rainforest and the desert. The Fane's name is not shown on the map until the quest For Fruits, Seeds, and Trees has been completed.

Places: The Fane of Ashvattha: a sacred hollow containing the Ashvattha Tree, the first Vasara Tree and progenitor of the Aranara. It also seals the way into Old Vanarana, the Aranara's former home.

Old Vanarana is a separate subarea within the Lost Nursery area, reached from the Fane through the Door of Vana, the first of four seals the Aranara laid after the Cataclysm to imprison Marana's Avatar. The wiki's page for this field also records a notice in front of the Steeple of Ignorance warning visitors about large Rishboland Tigers; that domain itself is listed near Chatrakam Cave in the Lokapala Jungle.

People: Aranara, the small forest spirits who regard the Ashvattha Tree as their origin, are tied to the place, though most adults cannot see them. Eremites and treasure hoarders also appear in the area, and the Aranara cook Arachatora features in a quest here.

Cyno and Tighnari appear in a Travelers' Tales anecdote set here: Tighnari is shopping for mushroom soup ingredients for Collei while Cyno ponders a mushroom-related question, and in a follow-up Cyno is collecting bark and soil samples.

History: Arama tells that Queen Aranyani sang here long ago, when the land still had sand, and the Ashvattha Tree responded, sprouting from Sarva. It produced a pomegranate whose first seed to sprout was Aramuhukunda, the first Aranara, and the others followed. This is the Aranara's own account.

In the quest For Fruits, Seeds, and Trees (Aranyaka Part III, 3.0) the Traveler and Arama bring three Vasoma Fruits to the Ashvattha Tree, find its dream corroded by the Withering (Marana), and cleanse it. The tree cannot bear a Bija, so Arama prepares to grow a new Ashvattha Tree and leads the Traveler into Old Vanarana in For the Children of the Past. Arama did become the new Ashvattha Tree inside Old Vanarana, after which Old Vanarana began to recover.

According to the Laurel Coronet text, Viaghara, ruler of the jungle, blessed the Aranara under the first Vasara Tree, and his pact with the divine kept birds and beasts from harming them. After the Cataclysm the Aranara sealed Marana's Avatar in Old Vanarana with four layers: the Door of Vana from the Fane, three Inscriptions of Remembrance made by Aramaha, Arayama and Araji (who later became Vasara Trees in Ashvattha's Concourses), the Ararakalari seals of many Aranara, and a final seal at the Sand-Embraced Home guarded by Aramuhukunda. Despite this, Marana's corrosion slowly leaked out.

Dangers: The Jadeplume Terrorshroom, a Dendro fungus, is the field's normal boss. Eremites, treasure hoarders and Withering Zones can be met, and the wiki mentions a notice about large Rishboland Tigers active at night.

Withering Zones appear in quests near the Fane. In the hidden exploration Even Beasts Get Homesick, a Sumpter Beast is followed to its destination in the Ashavan Realm, where its owner, an Eremite Crossbow, must be defeated.

Quests: Aranyaka Part III (Nursery of Lost Dreams): For Fruits, Seeds, and Trees and For the Children of the Past start or pass through here. The world quest Cooking, the Flavor of Nature (An Unwavering Culinary Dream) begins here. Anecdotes: Cyno: Myco-management and Cyno: Food. Hidden exploration: Even Beasts Get Homesick.

Search Chronicle: For Childhood Dreams! is also in the wiki category for the field, but only its title was reviewed.

Atmosphere: A mild, green, mushroom-scented rural field close to the capital, with a quiet sacred place at its centre where an ancient tree holds the dreams and memories of the forest's small spirits.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the field is open to explore; nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 changes it.

The Ashvattha Tree in the Fane is withered, and a new Ashvattha Tree grows in Old Vanarana from Arama.

341.content: The Fane of Ashvattha holds the Ashvattha Tree, the first and oldest Vasara Tree and the origin of the Aranara. Arama says it sprouted from Sarva when Queen Aranyani sang, and its fruit produced Aramuhukunda, the first Aranara. It also seals the entrance to Old Vanarana. By Aranyaka Part III the tree is corroded by Marana and cannot bear a Bija, so Arama becomes the new Ashvattha Tree inside Old Vanarana.

342.content: Vasara Trees are usually created by Aranara and hold dreams and memories. An Aranara can choose to become one and remains partly conscious. Aranara are sometimes described as seeds that may one day grow into Vasara Trees. Each tree bears a Vasoma Fruit once cleansed.

343.content:
Vourukasha Oasis (also: Vourukasha): Vourukasha Oasis is the birthplace and homeland of the Pari, avian flower-like beings who guard it. It holds a sea of pure dew called Amrita, formed from the remains of the original Hydro Archon, Egeria, and at its centre grows the Harvisptokhm, a giant tree that keeps what is left of her consciousness. After an Abyss attack the Pari elder Zurvan sealed the Oasis with the Great Songs of Khvarena, admitting only heroes who have bonded with Pari and pilgrims who come to worship Egeria.

The Oasis lies in the Girdle of the Sands within the Realm of Farakhkert and is the setting of the Khvarena of Good and Evil quest series (3.6). Its name echoes the Vourukasha, the cosmic sea of Zoroastrian belief, with the Harvisptokhm as its tree of all seeds.

Geography: A sacred oasis built around the central Harvisptokhm. The Amrita Pool holds the primordial Amrita; the tree's interior, with the great lotus Gaokerena inside, is entered through a hollow at Tunigi Hollow or over the stump's top. A thorn-filled canyon holds Asipattravana Swamp just to the north.

Before the Traveler cleanses it, the Harvisptokhm looks like a withered stump under the Sign of Apaosha, a defiled mark that hangs in the sky. Afterwards it sprouts a glowing blue canopy, and after The Hymn of Tir Yazad (Part 2) a tower of pure Amrita grows on top.

People: The Pari live here: Zurvan, the First Pari and elder; Mihir, a familiar of thorns; Rashnu; and Sorush, a young Pari who joins the Traveler. The wiki also lists Sefana and Fedhri among the Oasis's NPCs. Visitors are rare. Zurvan limits entry to heroes who have bonded with Pari and to pilgrims who come to worship Egeria.

Pari are the sentient form of Khvarena. Each has a fated responsibility they must carry out alone. At the end of their life they turn into Plumes of Purifying Light that return to the Amrita Pool; a Pari tainted by Abyssal corruption is rejected by the Oasis and becomes a Fravashi Tree, and their bonded human, called Yasnapati, brings lost Pari home.

Culture: Pari consider Egeria their god. They exist to avert catastrophe and cleanse defilement, and the Great Songs of Khvarena are their ritual power.

History: In the cataclysm 500 years ago Egeria, the previous Hydro Archon, was slain; Greater Lord Rukkhadevata grew the Harvisptokhm from the Amrita, her remains, anchoring Egeria's consciousness in the mortal world. The tree absorbs the defilement leaking from the Abyssal rift at Tunigi Hollow and keeps it sealed. The divine bird Simurgh sacrificed herself into thousands of Khvarena, drank the Amrita and mixed her Khvarena with it, creating the Pari. The first Pari, Zurvan, woke during the cataclysm, fought Abyssal creatures, and found Dainsleif shortly after Khaenri'ah's fall.

Zurvan, Dainsleif and the one-armed sage Nagarjuna found the Harvisptokhm with the help of Khaenri'ahn ruin constructs and held the first Rite of Ab-Zohr, which cleansed sky and earth and created the other Pari, who bonded with the Skeptics. Sometime later, after an Abyss attack, Zurvan sealed the Oasis with the Great Songs of Khvarena. The Oceanids, created by Egeria, came to Tunigi Hollow looking for their old master after rejecting the new Hydro Archon Focalors, saw the tree was not what they hoped, and scattered; later people followed their pilgrimage trail.

In the quest series the Traveler and Sorush answer a growing build-up of defilement, shown as the Sign of Apaosha. Zurvan tells the Traveler that if the filth overwhelms the tree, the rift at Tunigi Hollow could reopen. The events of The Hymn of Tir Yazad (Part 2) extinguish the Sign; Zurvan says the power of defilement can never be fully removed, only delayed, and that the Pari will rest and recover.

Dangers: Abyssal defilement, which can twist Pari and cloud areas like Asipattravana Swamp with purple mist; Abyss monsters tied to the Tunigi Hollow rift; and any visitor the Pari judge unworthy. Zurvan opens her sealed home only to bonded heroes and pilgrims.

Atmosphere: A sacred, ancient and guarded place. The wiki's intro speaks of a sea of pure dew with a tree at its heart, and the Pari talk of duty and of a cycle that returns them to the water. Zurvan greets trespassers sternly, while Sorush's talk is bluntly tough.

Quests: Khvarena of Good and Evil (3.6): The Splendorous Sky That Day, Asipattravana Itihasa, The Hymn of Tir Yazad, Pale Fire and related quests. The Traveler gains Sorush, helps the Pari awaken Khvarena, cleanses the Harvisptokhm and extinguishes the Sign of Apaosha.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Oasis is calm: the Sign of Apaosha is gone and the Pari rest.

Zurvan keeps the seal in place and the Harvisptokhm is whole, crowned with Amrita. Nothing from 6.x or 7.0-7.1 has changed this.

344.content:
The Pari are avian, flower-like beings descended from the divine bird Simurgh who live in the Vourukasha Oasis. They are the only sentient form of Khvarena. Zurvan is the first; Mihir is a familiar of thorns; Sorush, young and untested, stays with the Traveler. Their Plumes of Purifying Light return to the Amrita Pool.

Zurvan says they exist to avert catastrophe and cleanse defilement. Sorush was born after the previous catastrophe and has not seen the old war, and Zurvan calls her tough talk a cover for a good heart.

345.content:
The giant tree at the Oasis's centre. Greater Lord Rukkhadevata grew it from the Amrita, the remains of Egeria. It binds Egeria's remaining consciousness to the mortal world, seals the Abyssal rift at Tunigi Hollow and absorbs its defilement. Inside is the giant lotus Gaokerena where the god of the Pari slumbers.

Its Zoroastrian namesake is the tree of all seeds in the cosmic sea Vourukasha, within which grows the Gaokerena and on which the Simurgh perches.

346.content:
Wadi Al-Majuj: Wadi Al-Majuj is a canyon region south of Mt. Damavand in Sumeru's Desert of Hadramaveth. In its dark rift lie the ruins of ancient Gurabad's great gate, and a canyon, the Pairidaeza Canyon, cuts through it with Eremite camps beside it.

It was added in version 3.4. Its name combines the Arabic wadi (river valley) with 'Majuj', the desert folk's word for hilichurls.

Geography: South of Mt. Damavand, with a large canyon running through it. Parts of the Pairidaeza Canyon are open to the sky and hold Eremite camps; other parts run underground over a basin of shallow water, and the canyon leads into Liloupar's Cell.

Features include a cascade pool, Four-Leaf Sigil, Primal Obelisk and Ruins Torch, and a Time Trial Challenge.

Places: The great gate of Gurabad, fallen into the dark valley rift, and the mansions and estates that now serve as bandit nests; the Pairidaeza Canyon; and Liloupar's Cell at the end of that canyon.

The Remnants of the Ancient Orchard viewpoint describes the gate as once a place where poetry and beauty gathered, where only the cream of the crop could stand and behold their noble mortal lord. The Gap of the Hidden Ruins viewpoint says mighty Gurabad's monuments could not escape the rift, and that their mansions and estates became nests for roving bandits, adding humiliation to destruction.

History: Gurabad was a city founded by Ormazd, King Deshret's favoured vassal; the wiki says it fell after Liloupar used Abyssal power in revenge, with much of the city swallowed by a chasm and a plague after. These are the ruins at the canyon's edge.

Akademiya logs from elsewhere in the desert say 'Majuj' is the desert folk's name for the creatures that Sumeru calls hilichurls, and the team came to think they were survivors of an ancient country, transformed.

People: Eremite camps lie in the canyon. At some earlier time an Eremite expedition including Jebrael, Samail and a man named Tarafa searched for Gurabad's hidden treasure.

Pathfinders' Logs, written by Tarafa, mourn the party's dead: Umur lost to a cyclone near Gurabad's ruins, Bahaddin blinded by a Red Vulture, Rabeed killed in his sleep by a scorpion, and Jebrael fallen from the ruins in the gorge. Tarafa found a keystone at a third place of worship and believed the treasure must lie behind Gurabad's gate.

A sixth log, available after the Dual Evidence quest, reverses this account (see the entry on the logs).

Dangers: Eremite camps, bandits among the ruins, hazards of the rift and cyclones.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the canyon is open, its Eremite camps in place and Gurabad's gate still lost in the rift.

No change to the area is recorded after version 3.4.

347.content: Six notes in the canyon tell of an Eremite expedition to Gurabad in which several members died. Tarafa wrote the first five, asking the reader to turn back from a cursed journey; Jebrael and Samail are named as the last survivors alongside him. Collecting all six grants the hidden achievement Genesis of the Rift.

348.content: The sixth log, written by a member who says he faked his own death, apparently Jebrael whose fall Tarafa recorded, accuses Tarafa of betraying the team and causing the deaths of Umur, Bahaddin and Rabeed, and of nearly attacking Samail. It also calls the stone slate Babel's ploy and fears Gurabad holds no treasure. It is available after the Dual Evidence quest.

349.content:
Wenut Tunnels (also: Tunnels of the Wenut): The Wenut Tunnels are the system of caverns below the Sands of Al-Azif in Sumeru's Desert of Hadramaveth. They are the dangerous home of the Wenut, huge eyeless sand-worms, and of the area boss Setekh Wenut.

The in-game viewpoint says the mortal palaces have long fallen and the Wenut now rule here, turning the place into a court and garden to their liking.

Geography: A network of underground caverns arranged on three map levels (upper, middle and lower), beneath the Sands of Al-Azif. The wiki lists the City of the Deceased domain with them as a point of interest.

The Sands of Al-Azif above are one of the flatter parts of the desert, with many Wenut roaming the surface; the tunnels below are the cavern system dangerous to enter that is their home.

People: No humans live here. The Wenut are eyeless predators that hunt by sound and vibration. The Setekh Wenut, titled The Last Prince of the Sands, is a boss of the Mystical Beasts type that strikes with physical and Anemo attacks.

Archive text says the creatures once thrived alongside their progenitors and offspring in a land of grass and huge trees, swimming through wet soil like fish; when the gifts of heaven turned that soil to sand, the line that survived adapted to earth-living and became the Wenut. Some desert folk wrongly believe sandworms are the last stage of the quicksand eel.

The Adventurer Handbook says Wenut sometimes take plant-like shapes, and some say this is because they were scions of the lord of plants, while others say it lures prey seeking shade or fruit. Loading screens add that some legends make them near kin and descendants of dragons.

History: Setekh Wenut's text says the desert was once a land of fragrant flowers, huge trees and countless beasts, and that the only ones who remember it are the blind predators called Wenut, spoken of with respect and fear.

Desert folk still hunt the Wenut for their valuable spices: fat from their bodies yields costly seasoning, and swindlers grind Sand Grease Pupae and sell them as Wenut spice.

Dangers: The Wenut themselves, and Setekh Wenut. In a fight it first digs and sweeps, and later floats with Windbite Bullets that can be shattered with non-Anemo elements to paralyse it (gameplay).

Eyewitnesses in the Fulminating Sandstorm event spoke of Wenut in the double digits at least.

Travel: The tunnels lie below the Sands of Al-Azif. How they are entered is not described in the sources read. Because Wenut hunt by sound and vibration, noisy movement is likely to draw them (an inference, not a stated rule).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tunnels are open and the Wenut still rule them.

No change to the area is recorded after version 3.4.

350.comment: Wenut Tunnels: The Last Prince of the Sands
350.content:
The boss of the Wenut Tunnels, an eyeless predator from deep in the Great Red Sand that finds prey by sound and vibration. Its attacks are physical and Anemo. It drops the Pseudo-Stamens. It also carries the title Lord of the Desert in its description.

In its floating phase, Windbite Bullets orbit it; hitting two in a row with Cryo, Electro, Hydro or Pyro attacks paralyses it for about ten seconds and lowers its resistance to those elements (gameplay detail, not lore).

351.comment: Wenut Tunnels: Fulminating Sandstorm and the Wenutslayer Cannon
351.content: Limited-time event (Fulminating Sandstorm). The Kshahrewar researchers Shriya and Vinayak, who bicker over funding and design, build a turret called the Wenutslayer Cannon against the Wenut's violent behaviour; Shriya studies why the Wenut and the environment are behaving abnormally. The event is set in the Desert of Hadramaveth, and Vinayak claims eyewitnesses saw Wenut numbering in the double digits.

352.content:
Wikala Funduq (also: Wikala Inn): Wikala Funduq lies on the southeastern side of Port Ormos. It is the port's trade hub and, according to the wiki's citation of an NPC, the centre of Sumeru's commerce. The Sumeru Akademiya controls it. Traders, supervisors and Eremite mercenaries pass through.

Trade supervisors Dilawar and Gauhar oversee transactions; merchants Afanasi and Tavernier and the Eremite mercenaries Desai and Vanita are also stationed here.

People: Dilawar, a trade supervisor, is cynical: he says traders must be ready to end up penniless, as total wealth is fixed and anyone who profits has tricks up their sleeve; he suggests a casual trader try the Kalimi Exchange. Gauhar, also a trade supervisor, is a stickler for rules: only transactions within regulations are allowed, with registration, inspection, approval, contracts and a second approval, and anyone skipping a step takes the consequences. Afanasi and Tavernier are merchants; Desai and Vanita are Eremite mercenaries.

Dilawar's idle thought is that simple-minded people should not do business; Gauhar wishes everyone followed the rules as he does.

Quests: In Ever So Close (Chapter III Act I), after dealing with Dori, the Traveler and Paimon go to Wikala Funduq to meet Alhaitham. Alhaitham says he chose it because the Akademiya controls the Wikala and has people working there, and he came to Port Ormos under the pretence of official business; he says no one here is interested in what they say and that the matra will not come. He tests the Traveler with Canned Knowledge in the wilds and returns here to wait for their answer about Dori's information.

Alhaitham's reasons for the choice are his own: the Akademiya presence gives him cover for official business in Port Ormos.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Wikala Funduq is unchanged.

No quest up to 7.1 changes the supervisors or the Akademiya's control.

key: Where a Titan's Shins Were Broken
353.content:
Wounded Shin Valley (also: Where a Titan's Shins Were Broken): Wounded Shin Valley is a subarea of the Desert of Hadramaveth in Sumeru's Great Red Sand. It bore this name long before the great Ruin Golem of the Hadramaveth sank into the sand here, where it now lies immobile.

The valley appears in the world quest series The Dirge of Bilqis, whose party drives the ancient war machine to this spot. The viewpoint, Where a Titan's Shins Were Broken, is unlocked after that quest series' Dune-Entombed Fecundity: Part III.

Geography: A valley in the open desert, the third and last place the Hadramaveth's Ruin Golem stands. The golem went from the Dunes of Steel, to a spot north of the Sands of Three Canals, to here.

After it sinks, the golem permanently loses its ability to move or punch, though its eye cannon can still be fired manually, like that of the golem in the Valley of Dahri.

Places: The Ruin Golem of the Hadramaveth, whose arm generator rooms, control cabin and plates are open to explore. The wiki counts it as one of three known Ruin Golems in Sumeru, with those of Devantaka Mountain and the Valley of Dahri, and it is in far better repair than the others.

Interactable papers inside tell of two ages. Modern ones: a contract in which the Tanit matriarch Babel assigns the warriors Azariq and others to escort the Kshahrewar researcher Jazira Yassar across the desert, and Azariq's copied blueprints of the machine's power system. Ancient ones: an unsigned dying letter by a Khaenri'ahn soldier who still believes his Marshal will save them and that glory will return, and the discarded research page of the scholar Zandik, who calls the machine the 'Gurabad Specimen' and notes how it tilts with its own motion and would sicken any pilot.

Zandik's note guesses that the machine's pilot may have had modified inner ears or wore special adhesive boots and gloves, because a trial of piloting it had to stop after half a minute.

History: Before the quests, the golem lay in the Dunes of Steel. It is a Khaenri'ahn machine of the same kind as the one on Devantaka Mountain.

The valley's name predates the golem's fall: the viewpoint says it has been called Wounded Shin Valley for a long time, and that the name now bears extra weight because an iron giant has lost its footing here.

Dangers: The Eremites (Azariq's subordinates) fought in the quest; the open desert's sandstorms.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the valley is open and the golem lies sunk and immobile.

No change to the area is recorded after version 3.4.

354.comment: Wounded Shin Valley: Ruin Golem of the Hadramaveth
354.content: A giant Khaenri'ahn war machine, said to have once been piloted by humans called the Schwanenritter, and the best preserved of the three known golems in Sumeru. During The Dirge of Bilqis the party moves it to cross quicksand; at Wounded Shin Valley it sinks and can no longer move.

355.comment: Wounded Shin Valley: The Golem's Last Journey
355.content:
In The Dirge of Bilqis, Jeht, Liloupar and the Traveler use the decommissioned Ruin Golem to cross the dunes toward the Eternal Oasis. At the end of Dune-Entombed Fecundity: Part III, Azariq (Babel's Left Hand in the Tanit tribe, who had learned of the technology from the Fatui) demands Liloupar to restore the desert's oases. Jeht challenges and kills him. Aderfi, outside the machine, reveals Azariq meant to replace Babel with Jeht and wed her; the party decides to tell Babel later and presses on to Deshret's Glass Goblet.

The golem sinks into the valley at the end of its journey. Babel suspected Fatui involvement in Aderfi's betrayal, but the Fatui's exact role is not detailed.

356.content:
Yasna Monument: Yasna Monument is a small subarea of the Ashavan Realm in the Dharma Forest of Sumeru. It is the site of the Memory of Stone, a memorial plaque the Aranara set up for Nara Varuna.

The Memory of Stone was made so that a visible memory would show that Vana and the Aranara never forget their adventures with the Aranara. The Traveler cleans it in the world quest Memory of Stone, which starts here.

The quest follows Varuna Gatha, the Aranara story of Nara Varuna, and involves the Aranara Aranakula, spore-covered stones and a hidden cave.

Geography: Located in the Dharma Forest within the Ashavan Realm, the hilly, wooded and wet southern region of Sumeru. Stones around the monument are covered with spores during the quest, and a cave "branch" lies under a Four-Leaf Sigil at the southwest of a hill.

The Ashavan Realm is described by the game as a materially rich land of hills, woods and wetland, with ramparts defending its western edge against sandstorms. The name Ashavan is Zoroastrian-derived.

The name Yasna is Avestan for a Zoroastrian ceremony and for the main body of Avestan liturgical texts, which suits a place devoted to ritual remembrance, though the game states no such link.

People: The Aranara Aranakula is the figure the Traveler meets for the Memory of Stone quest. Nara Varuna is the Golden Nara whom the memorial honours; Araja describes Varuna as kind, brave and honest.

In the quest the Traveler must move forward without being noticed by the Fungi nearby, and Aranakula runs off if they are spotted; defeating the Fungi is pointless because new ones spawn.

History: The monument stands for the Aranara's remembrance of a Nara who befriended them long ago. It belongs to the same story thread as the Aranyaka, the book of stories between Aranara and Nara.

Atmosphere: Quiet and tender: a mossy memorial in the forest, cared for by small creatures who fear forgetting.

Quests: Memory of Stone (part of the Varuna Gatha series) begins here and leads on to A Prayer for Rain on the Fecund Land.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the monument remains a quiet Aranara memorial site; nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content changes it.

357.content: The Memory of Stone is the plaque marking Aranara remembrance of Nara Varuna. Its cleaning is the objective of the Memory of Stone quest, in which the Traveler and Aranakula clear spores from the stones and find a "branch" in a cave, following a Seelie to the three "leaves".

358.content:
Yazadaha Pool: Yazadaha Pool is a subarea of Avidya Forest in Sumeru's Dharma Forest, added in Version 3.0. It is a water area where Eremites and hilichurls are found.

Exploration objects include a Ruins Torch, Tri-Yana Seeds and Valaya. The local wood is Adhigama Wood.

Geography: A pool within the dense rainforest of Avidya Forest. The Chinese name is Tianbi Pool.

Dangers: Eremite Axe Vanguards, Daythunders, Linebreakers and Sword-Dancers, plus hilichurls, Hydro Samachurls, Pyro Hilichurl Grenadiers and Stretchy Geo Fungi.

Atmosphere: A damp forest clearing around still water, with Eremite patrols and hilichurl camps nearby.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is an ordinary explorable subarea.

The pool belongs to the Dharma Forest subregion and was added in Version 3.0. The wiki records no quests, NPCs or description text for it.

359.comment: Yazadaha Pool: Valaya and Tri-Yana Seeds
359.content: Valaya are an exploration mechanic of Sumeru; Tri-Yana Seeds and a Ruins Torch can also be found at the pool.

360.content:
Zubayr Theater: The Zubayr Theater is a small theater troupe's home in the Grand Bazaar of Sumeru City, set in a tree hollow. Its manager, playwright and director is Sheikh Zubayr, and Nilou, the dancer styled the Star of Zubayr Theater, is associated with the troupe.

The troupe is small enough that nearly everyone except the actor Kourosh wears several hats; Zubayr himself also composes, choreographs and directs action. His name is a pun on Shakespeare, according to the wiki.

People: Sheikh Zubayr is exacting and dry, and says one must act with gumption. Kourosh is the juggler and aspiring actor, whom Zubayr describes as mediocre but persistent and still worth teaching. Najia is the props engineer, and Nilou is the troupe's gifted dancer.

After Nilou's story quest Zubayr says new members have joined, and that Nilou is teaching the young Inayah to dance and judges her diligent. He considers talent the deciding factor in the arts.

Quests: Nilou's Story Quest "To the Wise" (Lotos Somno Chapter Act I, 3.0) is built around the troupe's evening play and banquet. The Sumeru Archon Quest also involves Sheikh Zubayr among its cast.

Atmosphere: A cramped, busy backstage world of scripts, props and rehearsals in the middle of the market.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the troupe still performs; the pages consulted record no later change.

361.content: A playwright and manager who refuses interviews and asks that staff not be bothered over small matters. He tells the Traveler that Kourosh is the weakest performer yet worth teaching, and that he cannot expect everyone to be as gifted as Nilou. The name "Zubayr" is an Arabic masculine name meaning strong or brave.
